:::

::: context golden Answers written down once
A golden vector is an input with its exact expected output, worked out once by hand or with an independent tool, and kept in the test suite forever. For a packet format it catches the bugs that round-trip tests miss: if the encoder and decoder share the same mistake, such as a wrong bit position, a round trip still succeeds, while a comparison against the golden bytes fails at once. Standards documents often publish golden vectors for exactly this reason, as CRC variants publish check values.
:::

::: context single-source Say each fact once
If the payload length is stored in the struct and also given separately in the header, the two can disagree, and then some code will trust one and some the other. Deriving the data length from the payload at the moment of encoding means there is nothing to disagree with. Database designers call the same idea normalisation; programmers call it DRY, "don't repeat yourself". In flight software it also shrinks the list of inputs a reviewer has to check.
:::

::: context software-bus Publish and subscribe on board
In cFS, applications never call each other directly. Each one publishes messages, every one of them a CCSDS packet, onto a software bus, and any application can subscribe to message IDs it cares about. The bus copies or passes a pointer to each subscriber's pipe, a queue much like the ring buffers of milestone 1. New applications can be added without changing old ones, because nobody needs to know who is listening.
:::

--- task
The starter has the constants, `PacketType`, `PrimaryHeader` and `Packet`. Write:

1. `Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w)`: `BadArg` if `w` is null or a field does not fit its bits (version over 7, APID over 0x7FF, sequence flags over 3, sequence count over 0x3FFF), and then nothing is written. Otherwise write the three big-endian 16-bit words described in the lesson (the secondary header flag and `data_length` are written as given) and return the writer's status.
2. `Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h)`: `BadArg` for a null pointer. Read three 16-bit words and fill every field of `*h`. If the reader fails (fewer than 6 bytes), return its status and leave `*h` untouched. It does not check the values.
3. `Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written)`: write the whole packet: primary header, 4-byte time, payload, CRC-16 of all the bytes before it. It sets the secondary header flag to 1 and works out the data length itself (the total size minus 7), ignoring those two fields of `p.hdr`. Check in this order: `out` or `written` null → `BadArg`; version not 0 → `BadVersion`; a field too wide → `BadArg`; `payload_len` over `kMaxPayload` → `BadLength`; `cap` smaller than the packet → `NoSpace`. On success set `*written` to the size (12 + payload length); on failure do not touch it.
4. `class PacketEncoder`, with a private `StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32>` of next sequence counts:
   - `Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written)`: `BadArg` if `payload` is null with `len` over 0 or `apid` is over 0x7FF; `BadLength` if `len` is over `kMaxPayload`; `Full` if `apid` is new and the map already holds 32 APIDs. Otherwise encode a packet with version 0, sequence flags 3, the APID's next count and the given time and payload, and return what `encode_packet` returns. Only on success does the APID's next count go up by one (16383 wraps to 0) and the built count go up.
   - `std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const`: the count the next packet on `apid` will carry (0 for an APID never used).
   - `Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq)`: set it (`BadArg` if `apid` is over 0x7FF or `seq` over 0x3FFF).
   - `std::uint32_t packets_built() const`: how many packets were built successfully.
--- starter
// ============================================================================
// ORBIT flight software core
// Rules, as on a real spacecraft:
//   - no heap allocation after start-up: fixed-size pools and static arrays
//   - no exceptions, no recursion
//   - every function checks its inputs and returns a status code
// ============================================================================
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// ---- Status codes: the project's whole error vocabulary ---------------------
// The numbers go into acknowledgement packets, so never reorder them.
enum class Status : std::uint8_t {
    Ok = 0,
    NotImpl,      // a stub: not written yet
    BadArg,       // an input is null or out of range
    Full,         // a fixed-capacity container has no room
    Empty,        // nothing to take out
    NotFound,     // no such key, id or handle
    NoSpace,      // an output buffer is too small, or a pool is used up
    Duplicate,    // the same thing twice
    OutOfRange,   // a result does not fit its type
    NotReady,     // called before set-up finished
    TooShort,     // fewer bytes than the format needs
    BadVersion,   // a packet version we do not speak
    BadType,      // the wrong kind of packet
    BadLength,    // a length field that cannot be right
    BadCrc,       // the checksum does not match
    UnknownApid,  // a packet for an application we do not have
    BadOpcode,    // no such command
    BadArgs,      // a command's arguments are wrong
    Forbidden,    // not allowed in the current mode
    Overrun,      // a frame ran out of time
};

const char* status_name(Status s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Status::Ok: return "OK";
        case Status::NotImpl: return "NOT_IMPL";
        case Status::BadArg: return "BAD_ARG";
        case Status::Full: return "FULL";
        case Status::Empty: return "EMPTY";
        case Status::NotFound: return "NOT_FOUND";
        case Status::NoSpace: return "NO_SPACE";
        case Status::Duplicate: return "DUPLICATE";
        case Status::OutOfRange: return "OUT_OF_RANGE";
        case Status::NotReady: return "NOT_READY";
        case Status::TooShort: return "TOO_SHORT";
        case Status::BadVersion: return "BAD_VERSION";
        case Status::BadType: return "BAD_TYPE";
        case Status::BadLength: return "BAD_LENGTH";
        case Status::BadCrc: return "BAD_CRC";
        case Status::UnknownApid: return "UNKNOWN_APID";
        case Status::BadOpcode: return "BAD_OPCODE";
        case Status::BadArgs: return "BAD_ARGS";
        case Status::Forbidden: return "FORBIDDEN";
        case Status::Overrun: return "OVERRUN";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// ---- Heap watch: counts every operator new, so the checks can prove that ----
// ---- the flight code never touches the heap. Leave it as it is. -------------
static long long g_heap_allocs = 0;

void* operator new(std::size_t n) {
    ++g_heap_allocs;
    void* p = std::malloc(n == 0 ? 1 : n);
    if (p == nullptr) std::abort();
    return p;
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { std::free(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { std::free(p); }

long long heap_allocs() { return g_heap_allocs; }

// ---- RingBuffer: a first-in, first-out queue of fixed capacity --------------
// Invariant: 0 <= count_ <= N, and the items, oldest first, sit at
// (head_ + 0) % N, (head_ + 1) % N, ..., (head_ + count_ - 1) % N.
template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class RingBuffer {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a ring buffer needs room for at least one item");

public:
    // Adds v at the back. Full when there is no room: nothing changes.
    Status push(const T& v) {
        if (count_ == N) return Status::Full;
        items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Adds v at the back; when full, the oldest item is dropped to make room.
    // Returns true when an item was dropped.
    bool push_overwrite(const T& v) {
        if (count_ < N) {
            items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
            ++count_;
            return false;
        }
        items_[head_] = v;          // the oldest slot becomes the newest
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        ++dropped_;
        return true;
    }

    // Takes the oldest item out into *out. Empty when there is none.
    Status pop(T* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        --count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest item into *out without taking it out.
    Status peek(T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the i-th oldest item (0 is the oldest) into *out.
    Status at(std::size_t i, T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (i >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = items_[(head_ + i) % N];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    void clear() {
        head_ = 0;
        count_ = 0;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return count_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    bool empty() const { return count_ == 0; }
    bool full() const { return count_ == N; }
    std::uint32_t dropped() const { return dropped_; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::size_t head_ = 0;       // index of the oldest item
    std::size_t count_ = 0;      // how many items are held
    std::uint32_t dropped_ = 0;  // items lost to push_overwrite
};

// ---- Pool: N fixed blocks, handed out and taken back in O(1) ----------------
// A handle names a block by its index and the block's generation. Releasing a
// block bumps its generation, so an old handle to it stops working.
struct Handle {
    std::uint16_t index;
    std::uint16_t gen;   // 0 never names a live block
};

constexpr Handle kNoHandle = {0xFFFF, 0};

template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class Pool {
    static_assert(N > 0 && N < 0xFFFF, "a pool holds 1 to 65534 blocks");

public:
    Pool() { reset(); }

    // Every block free again; every old handle stops working.
    void reset() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            next_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(i + 1);   // N marks the end
            gen_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[i] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[i] + 1);
            used_[i] = false;
        }
        free_head_ = 0;
        in_use_ = 0;
    }

    // Takes a free block, clears it to T{} and writes its handle.
    // The most recently released block is handed out first.
    Status acquire(Handle* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (free_head_ == N) {
            ++failures_;
            return Status::NoSpace;
        }
        const std::uint16_t i = free_head_;
        free_head_ = next_[i];
        used_[i] = true;
        items_[i] = T{};
        ++in_use_;
        if (in_use_ > high_water_) high_water_ = in_use_;
        *out = {i, gen_[i]};
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Gives a block back. A stale, foreign or doubled handle is refused.
    Status release(Handle h) {
        if (!valid(h)) return Status::BadArg;
        used_[h.index] = false;
        gen_[h.index] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[h.index] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[h.index] + 1);
        next_[h.index] = free_head_;
        free_head_ = h.index;
        --in_use_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    bool valid(Handle h) const { return h.index < N && h.gen != 0 && used_[h.index] && gen_[h.index] == h.gen; }

    T* get(Handle h) { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }
    const T* get(Handle h) const { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }

    std::size_t in_use() const { return in_use_; }
    std::size_t available() const { return N - in_use_; }
    std::size_t high_water() const { return high_water_; }
    std::uint32_t failures() const { return failures_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t next_[N] = {};   // free list, threaded through the indexes
    std::uint16_t gen_[N] = {};
    bool used_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t free_head_ = 0;  // N when no block is free
    std::size_t in_use_ = 0;
    std::size_t high_water_ = 0;   // the most blocks ever in use at once
    std::uint32_t failures_ = 0;   // acquires refused because none was free
};

// ---- Packet buffers and queues that share one pool --------------------------
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacketBytes = 128;
constexpr std::size_t kBufferCount = 24;

struct PacketBuffer {
    std::uint8_t bytes[kMaxPacketBytes];
    std::uint16_t len;
};

using BufferPool = Pool<PacketBuffer, kBufferCount>;

// A FIFO of packets. The bytes live in blocks of a shared pool; the queue
// itself holds only handles, so moving a packet never copies 128 bytes twice.
template <std::size_t Depth>
class PacketQueue {
public:
    explicit PacketQueue(BufferPool* pool) : pool_(pool) {}

    // Copies a packet in. NoSpace when the pool is used up, Full when this
    // queue is at its depth; either way nothing is queued and no block leaks.
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || bytes == nullptr || len == 0 || len > kMaxPacketBytes) return Status::BadArg;
        if (fifo_.full()) return Status::Full;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = pool_->acquire(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        std::memcpy(b->bytes, bytes, len);
        b->len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        fifo_.push(h);   // cannot fail: checked for room above
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest packet out and frees its block. If it does not fit
    // in cap bytes it stays queued and the result is NoSpace.
    Status take(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || out == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;   // cannot happen while the invariant holds
        if (b->len > cap) return Status::NoSpace;
        std::memcpy(out, b->bytes, b->len);
        *len = b->len;
        fifo_.pop(&h);
        pool_->release(h);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The length of the oldest packet, without taking it.
    Status front_len(std::size_t* len) const {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;
        *len = b->len;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return fifo_.size(); }
    bool empty() const { return fifo_.empty(); }
    static constexpr std::size_t depth() { return Depth; }

private:
    BufferPool* pool_;
    RingBuffer<Handle, Depth> fifo_;
};

// ---- StaticMap: a hash map of fixed capacity, open addressing ---------------
// Keys are unsigned integers (APIDs, opcodes, parameter ids). A key's home
// slot is key % N; collisions probe forward one slot at a time, wrapping.
// Erased slots become tombstones, so a search never stops early at a gap
// that used to hold something. Every loop runs at most N times.
template <typename K, typename V, std::size_t N>
class StaticMap {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a map needs at least one slot");

public:
    StaticMap() { clear(); }

    void clear() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) state_[i] = Slot::Empty;
        size_ = 0;
        last_probes_ = 0;
    }

    // Inserts key, or overwrites its value if it is already there.
    // Full when the key is new and no empty slot or tombstone is left.
    Status put(K key, const V& value) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at != N) {
            values_[at] = value;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        // Not present: reuse the first tombstone on the key's path, or the
        // first empty slot. Both are on the path locate() just walked.
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        for (std::size_t probes = 0; probes < N; ++probes) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) {
                state_[i] = Slot::Used;
                keys_[i] = key;
                values_[i] = value;
                ++size_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        return Status::Full;
    }

    Status get(K key, V* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = values_[at];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    V* find(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }
    const V* find(K key) const {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }

    bool contains(K key) const { return locate(key) != N; }

    Status erase(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        state_[at] = Slot::Tomb;
        --size_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Writes up to max keys into out, smallest first; returns how many.
    // Insertion sort into the caller's array: no heap, no recursion.
    std::size_t sorted_keys(K* out, std::size_t max) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return 0;
        std::size_t n = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) continue;
            const K k = keys_[i];
            if (n < max) {
                std::size_t j = n++;
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            } else if (max > 0 && k < out[max - 1]) {
                std::size_t j = max - 1;   // k beats the largest kept key
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            }
        }
        return n;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    // Slots examined by the last put, get, find, contains or erase.
    std::size_t last_probes() const { return last_probes_; }

private:
    enum class Slot : std::uint8_t { Empty, Used, Tomb };

    static std::size_t home(K key) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(key % N); }

    // The slot holding key, or N. Stops at an empty slot or after N probes;
    // a tombstone does not stop it.
    std::size_t locate(K key) const {
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        std::size_t probes = 0;
        while (probes < N) {
            ++probes;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Empty) break;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Used && keys_[i] == key) {
                last_probes_ = probes;
                return i;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        last_probes_ = probes;
        return N;
    }

    K keys_[N] = {};
    V values_[N] = {};
    Slot state_[N] = {};
    std::size_t size_ = 0;
    mutable std::size_t last_probes_ = 0;
};

// ---- Big-endian byte writing and reading, with a sticky error ---------------
// Network byte order: the most significant byte goes first. After the first
// write or read that does not fit, the object stays failed: every later call
// returns the same error and changes nothing, so a caller can do a whole
// run of calls and check ok() once at the end.
class ByteWriter {
public:
    ByteWriter(std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t cap) : buf_(buf), cap_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : cap) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t v) { return put(&v, 1); }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[2] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 2);
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[4] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 24), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 16),
                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 4);
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t v) { return u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(v)); }
    Status bytes(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (src == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        return put(src, n);
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return len_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > cap_ - len_) return fail(Status::NoSpace);   // len_ <= cap_ always, so no wrap
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, src, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t cap_;
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

class ByteReader {
public:
    ByteReader(const std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t len) : buf_(buf), len_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : len) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[1];
        const Status s = take(b, 1, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = b[0];
        return s;
    }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[2];
        const Status s = take(b, 2, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b[0] << 8) | b[1]);
        return s;
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[4];
        const Status s = take(b, 4, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            *v = (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[0]) << 24) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[1]) << 16) |
                 (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[2]) << 8) | static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[3]);
        }
        return s;
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t* v) {
        std::uint32_t u = 0;
        const Status s = u32(v == nullptr ? nullptr : &u);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::int32_t>(u);   // two's complement, defined since C++20
        return s;
    }
    Status bytes(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (dst == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status skip(std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t pos() const { return pos_; }
    std::size_t remaining() const { return len_ - pos_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status take(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n, bool have_out) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (!have_out) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    const std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t len_;
    std::size_t pos_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

// ---- CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE -----------------------------------------------------
// Polynomial 0x1021 (x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1), start value 0xFFFF, bits taken
// most significant first, no final XOR. crc16("123456789") is 0x29B1.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcInit = 0xFFFF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcPoly = 0x1021;

// One bit at a time: 8 shift-and-maybe-XOR steps per byte. The reference.
std::uint16_t crc16_bitwise(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return kCrcInit;
    std::uint16_t crc = kCrcInit;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ (data[i] << 8));
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

// The 256 answers to "what do 8 steps do to this top byte", worked out by
// the compiler, so the table costs nothing at start-up and sits in ROM.
struct CrcTable {
    std::uint16_t entry[256];
};

constexpr CrcTable make_crc_table() {
    CrcTable t{};
    for (int b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
        std::uint16_t crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b << 8);
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
        t.entry[b] = crc;
    }
    return t;
}

constexpr CrcTable kCrcTable = make_crc_table();

// Continues a CRC over more bytes: crc16_update(crc16(a), b) == crc16(a then b).
std::uint16_t crc16_update(std::uint16_t crc, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return crc;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t top = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((crc >> 8) ^ data[i]);
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((crc << 8) ^ kCrcTable.entry[top]);
    }
    return crc;
}

// One table lookup per byte.
std::uint16_t crc16(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return crc16_update(kCrcInit, data, n); }

// ---- The packet format ------------------------------------------------------
//  bytes 0-5   primary header, CCSDS style, big-endian:
//              version:3 | type:1 | secondary header flag:1 | APID:11
//              sequence flags:2 | sequence count:14
//              data length: bytes after the primary header, minus 1
//  bytes 6-9   secondary header: time in milliseconds since boot
//  bytes 10-   payload, 0 to kMaxPayload bytes
//  last 2      CRC-16 of every byte before it
constexpr std::size_t kPrimaryHeaderBytes = 6;
constexpr std::size_t kSecondaryHeaderBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kCrcBytes = 2;
constexpr std::size_t kPacketOverhead = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + kSecondaryHeaderBytes + kCrcBytes;   // 12
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPayload = 96;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacket = kPacketOverhead + kMaxPayload;   // 108
constexpr std::uint16_t kMaxApid = 0x7FF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSeqMask = 0x3FFF;
constexpr std::uint8_t kSeqUnsegmented = 3;

enum class PacketType : std::uint8_t { Telemetry = 0, Command = 1 };

struct PrimaryHeader {
    std::uint8_t version;       // 3 bits; always 0
    PacketType type;            // 1 bit
    bool has_secondary;         // 1 bit
    std::uint16_t apid;         // 11 bits
    std::uint8_t seq_flags;     // 2 bits; 3 means "not split"
    std::uint16_t seq_count;    // 14 bits
    std::uint16_t data_length;  // 16 bits
};

struct Packet {
    PrimaryHeader hdr;
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t payload_len;
    std::uint8_t payload[kMaxPayload];
};

Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w) { return Status::NotImpl; }

Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h) { return Status::NotImpl; }

Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) { return Status::NotImpl; }

class PacketEncoder {
public:
    Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len,
                 std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
        return Status::NotImpl;
    }
    std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const { return 0xFFFF; }
    Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq) { return Status::NotImpl; }
    std::uint32_t packets_built() const { return 0xFFFFFFFFu; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> seq_;
};
--- solution
// ============================================================================
// ORBIT flight software core
// Rules, as on a real spacecraft:
//   - no heap allocation after start-up: fixed-size pools and static arrays
//   - no exceptions, no recursion
//   - every function checks its inputs and returns a status code
// ============================================================================
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// ---- Status codes: the project's whole error vocabulary ---------------------
// The numbers go into acknowledgement packets, so never reorder them.
enum class Status : std::uint8_t {
    Ok = 0,
    NotImpl,      // a stub: not written yet
    BadArg,       // an input is null or out of range
    Full,         // a fixed-capacity container has no room
    Empty,        // nothing to take out
    NotFound,     // no such key, id or handle
    NoSpace,      // an output buffer is too small, or a pool is used up
    Duplicate,    // the same thing twice
    OutOfRange,   // a result does not fit its type
    NotReady,     // called before set-up finished
    TooShort,     // fewer bytes than the format needs
    BadVersion,   // a packet version we do not speak
    BadType,      // the wrong kind of packet
    BadLength,    // a length field that cannot be right
    BadCrc,       // the checksum does not match
    UnknownApid,  // a packet for an application we do not have
    BadOpcode,    // no such command
    BadArgs,      // a command's arguments are wrong
    Forbidden,    // not allowed in the current mode
    Overrun,      // a frame ran out of time
};

const char* status_name(Status s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Status::Ok: return "OK";
        case Status::NotImpl: return "NOT_IMPL";
        case Status::BadArg: return "BAD_ARG";
        case Status::Full: return "FULL";
        case Status::Empty: return "EMPTY";
        case Status::NotFound: return "NOT_FOUND";
        case Status::NoSpace: return "NO_SPACE";
        case Status::Duplicate: return "DUPLICATE";
        case Status::OutOfRange: return "OUT_OF_RANGE";
        case Status::NotReady: return "NOT_READY";
        case Status::TooShort: return "TOO_SHORT";
        case Status::BadVersion: return "BAD_VERSION";
        case Status::BadType: return "BAD_TYPE";
        case Status::BadLength: return "BAD_LENGTH";
        case Status::BadCrc: return "BAD_CRC";
        case Status::UnknownApid: return "UNKNOWN_APID";
        case Status::BadOpcode: return "BAD_OPCODE";
        case Status::BadArgs: return "BAD_ARGS";
        case Status::Forbidden: return "FORBIDDEN";
        case Status::Overrun: return "OVERRUN";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// ---- Heap watch: counts every operator new, so the checks can prove that ----
// ---- the flight code never touches the heap. Leave it as it is. -------------
static long long g_heap_allocs = 0;

void* operator new(std::size_t n) {
    ++g_heap_allocs;
    void* p = std::malloc(n == 0 ? 1 : n);
    if (p == nullptr) std::abort();
    return p;
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { std::free(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { std::free(p); }

long long heap_allocs() { return g_heap_allocs; }

// ---- RingBuffer: a first-in, first-out queue of fixed capacity --------------
// Invariant: 0 <= count_ <= N, and the items, oldest first, sit at
// (head_ + 0) % N, (head_ + 1) % N, ..., (head_ + count_ - 1) % N.
template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class RingBuffer {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a ring buffer needs room for at least one item");

public:
    // Adds v at the back. Full when there is no room: nothing changes.
    Status push(const T& v) {
        if (count_ == N) return Status::Full;
        items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Adds v at the back; when full, the oldest item is dropped to make room.
    // Returns true when an item was dropped.
    bool push_overwrite(const T& v) {
        if (count_ < N) {
            items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
            ++count_;
            return false;
        }
        items_[head_] = v;          // the oldest slot becomes the newest
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        ++dropped_;
        return true;
    }

    // Takes the oldest item out into *out. Empty when there is none.
    Status pop(T* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        --count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest item into *out without taking it out.
    Status peek(T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the i-th oldest item (0 is the oldest) into *out.
    Status at(std::size_t i, T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (i >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = items_[(head_ + i) % N];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    void clear() {
        head_ = 0;
        count_ = 0;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return count_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    bool empty() const { return count_ == 0; }
    bool full() const { return count_ == N; }
    std::uint32_t dropped() const { return dropped_; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::size_t head_ = 0;       // index of the oldest item
    std::size_t count_ = 0;      // how many items are held
    std::uint32_t dropped_ = 0;  // items lost to push_overwrite
};

// ---- Pool: N fixed blocks, handed out and taken back in O(1) ----------------
// A handle names a block by its index and the block's generation. Releasing a
// block bumps its generation, so an old handle to it stops working.
struct Handle {
    std::uint16_t index;
    std::uint16_t gen;   // 0 never names a live block
};

constexpr Handle kNoHandle = {0xFFFF, 0};

template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class Pool {
    static_assert(N > 0 && N < 0xFFFF, "a pool holds 1 to 65534 blocks");

public:
    Pool() { reset(); }

    // Every block free again; every old handle stops working.
    void reset() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            next_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(i + 1);   // N marks the end
            gen_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[i] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[i] + 1);
            used_[i] = false;
        }
        free_head_ = 0;
        in_use_ = 0;
    }

    // Takes a free block, clears it to T{} and writes its handle.
    // The most recently released block is handed out first.
    Status acquire(Handle* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (free_head_ == N) {
            ++failures_;
            return Status::NoSpace;
        }
        const std::uint16_t i = free_head_;
        free_head_ = next_[i];
        used_[i] = true;
        items_[i] = T{};
        ++in_use_;
        if (in_use_ > high_water_) high_water_ = in_use_;
        *out = {i, gen_[i]};
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Gives a block back. A stale, foreign or doubled handle is refused.
    Status release(Handle h) {
        if (!valid(h)) return Status::BadArg;
        used_[h.index] = false;
        gen_[h.index] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[h.index] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[h.index] + 1);
        next_[h.index] = free_head_;
        free_head_ = h.index;
        --in_use_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    bool valid(Handle h) const { return h.index < N && h.gen != 0 && used_[h.index] && gen_[h.index] == h.gen; }

    T* get(Handle h) { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }
    const T* get(Handle h) const { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }

    std::size_t in_use() const { return in_use_; }
    std::size_t available() const { return N - in_use_; }
    std::size_t high_water() const { return high_water_; }
    std::uint32_t failures() const { return failures_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t next_[N] = {};   // free list, threaded through the indexes
    std::uint16_t gen_[N] = {};
    bool used_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t free_head_ = 0;  // N when no block is free
    std::size_t in_use_ = 0;
    std::size_t high_water_ = 0;   // the most blocks ever in use at once
    std::uint32_t failures_ = 0;   // acquires refused because none was free
};

// ---- Packet buffers and queues that share one pool --------------------------
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacketBytes = 128;
constexpr std::size_t kBufferCount = 24;

struct PacketBuffer {
    std::uint8_t bytes[kMaxPacketBytes];
    std::uint16_t len;
};

using BufferPool = Pool<PacketBuffer, kBufferCount>;

// A FIFO of packets. The bytes live in blocks of a shared pool; the queue
// itself holds only handles, so moving a packet never copies 128 bytes twice.
template <std::size_t Depth>
class PacketQueue {
public:
    explicit PacketQueue(BufferPool* pool) : pool_(pool) {}

    // Copies a packet in. NoSpace when the pool is used up, Full when this
    // queue is at its depth; either way nothing is queued and no block leaks.
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || bytes == nullptr || len == 0 || len > kMaxPacketBytes) return Status::BadArg;
        if (fifo_.full()) return Status::Full;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = pool_->acquire(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        std::memcpy(b->bytes, bytes, len);
        b->len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        fifo_.push(h);   // cannot fail: checked for room above
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest packet out and frees its block. If it does not fit
    // in cap bytes it stays queued and the result is NoSpace.
    Status take(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || out == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;   // cannot happen while the invariant holds
        if (b->len > cap) return Status::NoSpace;
        std::memcpy(out, b->bytes, b->len);
        *len = b->len;
        fifo_.pop(&h);
        pool_->release(h);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The length of the oldest packet, without taking it.
    Status front_len(std::size_t* len) const {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;
        *len = b->len;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return fifo_.size(); }
    bool empty() const { return fifo_.empty(); }
    static constexpr std::size_t depth() { return Depth; }

private:
    BufferPool* pool_;
    RingBuffer<Handle, Depth> fifo_;
};

// ---- StaticMap: a hash map of fixed capacity, open addressing ---------------
// Keys are unsigned integers (APIDs, opcodes, parameter ids). A key's home
// slot is key % N; collisions probe forward one slot at a time, wrapping.
// Erased slots become tombstones, so a search never stops early at a gap
// that used to hold something. Every loop runs at most N times.
template <typename K, typename V, std::size_t N>
class StaticMap {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a map needs at least one slot");

public:
    StaticMap() { clear(); }

    void clear() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) state_[i] = Slot::Empty;
        size_ = 0;
        last_probes_ = 0;
    }

    // Inserts key, or overwrites its value if it is already there.
    // Full when the key is new and no empty slot or tombstone is left.
    Status put(K key, const V& value) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at != N) {
            values_[at] = value;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        // Not present: reuse the first tombstone on the key's path, or the
        // first empty slot. Both are on the path locate() just walked.
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        for (std::size_t probes = 0; probes < N; ++probes) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) {
                state_[i] = Slot::Used;
                keys_[i] = key;
                values_[i] = value;
                ++size_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        return Status::Full;
    }

    Status get(K key, V* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = values_[at];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    V* find(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }
    const V* find(K key) const {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }

    bool contains(K key) const { return locate(key) != N; }

    Status erase(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        state_[at] = Slot::Tomb;
        --size_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Writes up to max keys into out, smallest first; returns how many.
    // Insertion sort into the caller's array: no heap, no recursion.
    std::size_t sorted_keys(K* out, std::size_t max) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return 0;
        std::size_t n = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) continue;
            const K k = keys_[i];
            if (n < max) {
                std::size_t j = n++;
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            } else if (max > 0 && k < out[max - 1]) {
                std::size_t j = max - 1;   // k beats the largest kept key
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            }
        }
        return n;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    // Slots examined by the last put, get, find, contains or erase.
    std::size_t last_probes() const { return last_probes_; }

private:
    enum class Slot : std::uint8_t { Empty, Used, Tomb };

    static std::size_t home(K key) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(key % N); }

    // The slot holding key, or N. Stops at an empty slot or after N probes;
    // a tombstone does not stop it.
    std::size_t locate(K key) const {
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        std::size_t probes = 0;
        while (probes < N) {
            ++probes;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Empty) break;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Used && keys_[i] == key) {
                last_probes_ = probes;
                return i;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        last_probes_ = probes;
        return N;
    }

    K keys_[N] = {};
    V values_[N] = {};
    Slot state_[N] = {};
    std::size_t size_ = 0;
    mutable std::size_t last_probes_ = 0;
};

// ---- Big-endian byte writing and reading, with a sticky error ---------------
// Network byte order: the most significant byte goes first. After the first
// write or read that does not fit, the object stays failed: every later call
// returns the same error and changes nothing, so a caller can do a whole
// run of calls and check ok() once at the end.
class ByteWriter {
public:
    ByteWriter(std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t cap) : buf_(buf), cap_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : cap) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t v) { return put(&v, 1); }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[2] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 2);
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[4] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 24), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 16),
                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 4);
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t v) { return u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(v)); }
    Status bytes(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (src == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        return put(src, n);
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return len_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > cap_ - len_) return fail(Status::NoSpace);   // len_ <= cap_ always, so no wrap
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, src, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t cap_;
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

class ByteReader {
public:
    ByteReader(const std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t len) : buf_(buf), len_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : len) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[1];
        const Status s = take(b, 1, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = b[0];
        return s;
    }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[2];
        const Status s = take(b, 2, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b[0] << 8) | b[1]);
        return s;
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[4];
        const Status s = take(b, 4, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            *v = (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[0]) << 24) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[1]) << 16) |
                 (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[2]) << 8) | static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[3]);
        }
        return s;
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t* v) {
        std::uint32_t u = 0;
        const Status s = u32(v == nullptr ? nullptr : &u);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::int32_t>(u);   // two's complement, defined since C++20
        return s;
    }
    Status bytes(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (dst == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status skip(std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t pos() const { return pos_; }
    std::size_t remaining() const { return len_ - pos_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status take(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n, bool have_out) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (!have_out) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    const std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t len_;
    std::size_t pos_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

// ---- CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE -----------------------------------------------------
// Polynomial 0x1021 (x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1), start value 0xFFFF, bits taken
// most significant first, no final XOR. crc16("123456789") is 0x29B1.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcInit = 0xFFFF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcPoly = 0x1021;

// One bit at a time: 8 shift-and-maybe-XOR steps per byte. The reference.
std::uint16_t crc16_bitwise(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return kCrcInit;
    std::uint16_t crc = kCrcInit;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ (data[i] << 8));
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

// The 256 answers to "what do 8 steps do to this top byte", worked out by
// the compiler, so the table costs nothing at start-up and sits in ROM.
struct CrcTable {
    std::uint16_t entry[256];
};

constexpr CrcTable make_crc_table() {
    CrcTable t{};
    for (int b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
        std::uint16_t crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b << 8);
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
        t.entry[b] = crc;
    }
    return t;
}

constexpr CrcTable kCrcTable = make_crc_table();

// Continues a CRC over more bytes: crc16_update(crc16(a), b) == crc16(a then b).
std::uint16_t crc16_update(std::uint16_t crc, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return crc;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t top = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((crc >> 8) ^ data[i]);
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((crc << 8) ^ kCrcTable.entry[top]);
    }
    return crc;
}

// One table lookup per byte.
std::uint16_t crc16(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return crc16_update(kCrcInit, data, n); }

// ---- The packet format ------------------------------------------------------
//  bytes 0-5   primary header, CCSDS style, big-endian:
//              version:3 | type:1 | secondary header flag:1 | APID:11
//              sequence flags:2 | sequence count:14
//              data length: bytes after the primary header, minus 1
//  bytes 6-9   secondary header: time in milliseconds since boot
//  bytes 10-   payload, 0 to kMaxPayload bytes
//  last 2      CRC-16 of every byte before it
constexpr std::size_t kPrimaryHeaderBytes = 6;
constexpr std::size_t kSecondaryHeaderBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kCrcBytes = 2;
constexpr std::size_t kPacketOverhead = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + kSecondaryHeaderBytes + kCrcBytes;   // 12
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPayload = 96;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacket = kPacketOverhead + kMaxPayload;   // 108
constexpr std::uint16_t kMaxApid = 0x7FF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSeqMask = 0x3FFF;
constexpr std::uint8_t kSeqUnsegmented = 3;

enum class PacketType : std::uint8_t { Telemetry = 0, Command = 1 };

struct PrimaryHeader {
    std::uint8_t version;       // 3 bits; always 0
    PacketType type;            // 1 bit
    bool has_secondary;         // 1 bit
    std::uint16_t apid;         // 11 bits
    std::uint8_t seq_flags;     // 2 bits; 3 means "not split"
    std::uint16_t seq_count;    // 14 bits
    std::uint16_t data_length;  // 16 bits
};

struct Packet {
    PrimaryHeader hdr;
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t payload_len;
    std::uint8_t payload[kMaxPayload];
};

// Packs the six header bytes. BadArg if a field does not fit its bits.
Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w) {
    if (w == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (h.version > 7 || h.apid > kMaxApid || h.seq_flags > 3 || h.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    const std::uint16_t word0 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.version << 13) | (static_cast<unsigned>(h.type) << 12) |
                                                           ((h.has_secondary ? 1u : 0u) << 11) | h.apid);
    const std::uint16_t word1 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.seq_flags << 14) | h.seq_count);
    w->u16(word0);
    w->u16(word1);
    w->u16(h.data_length);
    return w->status();
}

// Unpacks the six header bytes. Checks nothing but that they are there.
Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h) {
    if (r == nullptr || h == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint16_t word0 = 0, word1 = 0, length = 0;
    r->u16(&word0);
    r->u16(&word1);
    r->u16(&length);
    if (!r->ok()) return r->status();
    h->version = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0 >> 13);
    h->type = ((word0 >> 12) & 1u) ? PacketType::Command : PacketType::Telemetry;
    h->has_secondary = ((word0 >> 11) & 1u) != 0;
    h->apid = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word0 & kMaxApid);
    h->seq_flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1 >> 14);
    h->seq_count = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word1 & kSeqMask);
    h->data_length = length;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Writes p as a whole packet: header (data length and the secondary header
// flag worked out here), time, payload and CRC. *written is set only on Ok.
Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (out == nullptr || written == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.hdr.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (p.hdr.apid > kMaxApid || p.hdr.seq_flags > 3 || p.hdr.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.payload_len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    const std::size_t total = kPacketOverhead + p.payload_len;
    if (cap < total) return Status::NoSpace;
    PrimaryHeader h = p.hdr;
    h.has_secondary = true;
    h.data_length = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPrimaryHeaderBytes - 1);
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    const Status s = pack_primary(h, &w);
    if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
    w.u32(p.time_ms);
    w.bytes(p.payload, p.payload_len);
    w.u16(crc16(out, w.size()));
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Builds packets and numbers them: each APID has its own 14-bit sequence
// count, which starts at 0 and wraps from 16383 back to 0.
class PacketEncoder {
public:
    Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len,
                 std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
        if ((payload == nullptr && len > 0) || apid > kMaxApid) return Status::BadArg;
        if (len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        const std::uint16_t seq = found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
        if (found == nullptr && seq_.size() == seq_.capacity()) return Status::Full;
        Packet p{};
        p.hdr = {0, type, true, apid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
        p.time_ms = time_ms;
        p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        if (len > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload, payload, len);
        const Status s = encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        seq_.put(apid, static_cast<std::uint16_t>((seq + 1) & kSeqMask));   // only a sent packet uses a number
        ++built_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The count the next packet on apid will carry.
    std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const {
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        return found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
    }

    // Sets the next count for apid (ground tools use it to replay a pass).
    Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq) {
        if (apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        return seq_.put(apid, seq);
    }

    std::uint32_t packets_built() const { return built_; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> seq_;
    std::uint32_t built_ = 0;
};
--- hint
In `pack_primary`, test all four widths before writing anything. Build `word0` as `(h.version << 13) | (type << 12) | (sec << 11) | h.apid` in an `unsigned` expression, then cast to `std::uint16_t` and write it with `w->u16`.
--- hint
In `encode_packet`, after the checks: copy `p.hdr`, set `has_secondary = true` and `data_length = total - 7`, pack it with a `ByteWriter` over `out`, write the time and the payload, then `w.u16(crc16(out, w.size()))`.
--- hint
In `build`, look the APID up with `find`: a null pointer means "new, count 0", and then check `size() == capacity()` for `Full`. Put the count into the map (`put`) only after `encode_packet` returned `Ok`.

+++ practice | A housekeeping status word
--- task
A power unit reports its state in one 16-bit status word:

| bits | field | range |
|---|---|---|
| 15 to 14 | mode | 0 to 3 |
| 13 | heater on | 0 or 1 |
| 12 to 8 | fault code | 0 to 31 |
| 7 to 0 | counter | 0 to 255 |

```cpp fragment
struct PowerStatus {
    int mode;
    bool heater;
    int fault;
    int counter;
};
```

- `bool pack_status(const PowerStatus& s, std::uint16_t* out)`: pack the fields; return `false` and write nothing if a field is out of its range or `out` is null.
- `PowerStatus unpack_status(std::uint16_t w)`: the reverse.
--- starter
#include <cstdint>

struct PowerStatus {
    int mode;
    bool heater;
    int fault;
    int counter;
};

bool pack_status(const PowerStatus& s, std::uint16_t* out) {
    return false;
}

PowerStatus unpack_status(std::uint16_t w) {
    return {0, false, 0, 0};
}
--- solution
#include <cstdint>

struct PowerStatus {
    int mode;
    bool heater;
    int fault;
    int counter;
};

bool pack_status(const PowerStatus& s, std::uint16_t* out) {
    if (out == nullptr) return false;
    if (s.mode < 0 || s.mode > 3 || s.fault < 0 || s.fault > 31 || s.counter < 0 || s.counter > 255) return false;
    *out = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((s.mode << 14) | ((s.heater ? 1 : 0) << 13) | (s.fault << 8) | s.counter);
    return true;
}

PowerStatus unpack_status(std::uint16_t w) {
    return {(w >> 14) & 3, ((w >> 13) & 1) != 0, (w >> 8) & 31, w & 0xFF};
}
--- hint
Each field is shifted up to its lowest bit number: the mode by 14, the heater by 13, the fault by 8.
--- hint
To unpack, shift down by the same amount and mask with the field's largest value: 3, 1, 31, 255.
--- check test | Packing
[] { std::uint16_t w = 0; bool ok = pack_status({2, true, 5, 0x7F}, &w); return ok && w == 0xA57F; }()
--- check test | Unpacking
[] { PowerStatus s = unpack_status(0xFFFF); PowerStatus t = unpack_status(0x4203); return s.mode == 3 && s.heater && s.fault == 31 && s.counter == 255 && t.mode == 1 && !t.heater && t.fault == 2 && t.counter == 3; }()
--- check test | Out-of-range fields are refused
[] { std::uint16_t w = 1234; return !pack_status({4, false, 0, 0}, &w) && !pack_status({0, false, 32, 0}, &w) && !pack_status({0, false, 0, 256}, &w) && !pack_status({-1, false, 0, 0}, &w) && !pack_status({0, false, 0, 0}, nullptr) && w == 1234; }()
--- check test | Round trip of every mode and fault
[] { for (int m = 0; m < 4; m++) for (int f = 0; f < 32; f++) { std::uint16_t w; PowerStatus s = {m, f % 2 == 0, f, (m * 37 + f) % 256}; pack_status(s, &w); PowerStatus g = unpack_status(w); if (g.mode != m || g.fault != f || g.heater != s.heater || g.counter != s.counter) return false; } return true; }()

+++ practice | A quick look at a packet's address
--- task
A router on the ground only needs a packet's APID and type to decide where it goes, without decoding the rest. Write:

- `int apid_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n)`: the APID from the first two bytes of a space packet, or -1 if `p` is null, `n` is less than 6, or the version (the top 3 bits) is not 0.
- `int type_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n)`: 0 for telemetry, 1 for a command, or -1 under the same conditions.
--- starter
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

int apid_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n) {
    return p[1];
}

int type_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n) {
    return 0;
}
--- solution
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

static bool looks_valid(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n) {
    return p != nullptr && n >= 6 && (p[0] >> 5) == 0;
}

int apid_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n) {
    if (!looks_valid(p, n)) return -1;
    return ((p[0] << 8) | p[1]) & 0x7FF;
}

int type_of(const std::uint8_t* p, std::size_t n) {
    if (!looks_valid(p, n)) return -1;
    return (p[0] >> 4) & 1;
}
--- hint
The version is the top 3 bits of byte 0: `p[0] >> 5`.
--- hint
The APID is the low 11 bits of the first 16-bit word, so it needs the low 3 bits of byte 0 and all of byte 1.
--- check test | Telemetry on APID 0x021
[] { std::uint8_t p[6] = {0x08, 0x21, 0xC0, 0x05, 0x00, 0x06}; return apid_of(p, 6) == 0x021 && type_of(p, 6) == 0; }()
--- check test | A command on the largest APID
[] { std::uint8_t p[6] = {0x1F, 0xFF, 0xC0, 0x00, 0x00, 0x05}; return apid_of(p, 6) == 0x7FF && type_of(p, 6) == 1; }()
--- check test | Short, null, or a version that is not 0
[] { std::uint8_t p[6] = {0x28, 0x21, 0, 0, 0, 0}; std::uint8_t q[6] = {0x08, 0x21, 0, 0, 0, 0}; return apid_of(p, 6) == -1 && type_of(p, 6) == -1 && apid_of(q, 5) == -1 && apid_of(nullptr, 6) == -1 && type_of(nullptr, 9) == -1; }()

+++ practice | A CCSDS time code
--- task
Many missions stamp packets with a CCSDS unsegmented time code: 4 bytes of whole seconds and 2 bytes of fraction, where the fraction counts units of 1/65536 of a second, all big-endian.

- `bool time_encode(std::uint64_t ms, std::uint8_t out[6])`: seconds = `ms / 1000`; fraction = the leftover milliseconds × 65536 / 1000, rounded down. Return `false` if the seconds do not fit in 32 bits.
- `std::uint64_t time_decode(const std::uint8_t in[6])`: back to milliseconds: seconds × 1000 + fraction × 1000 / 65536, **rounded to the nearest** millisecond (a half rounds up).

So 1500 ms is encoded 00 00 00 01 80 00, and 80 00 decodes to 500 ms. Work in `std::uint64_t` so nothing overflows.
--- starter
#include <cstdint>

bool time_encode(std::uint64_t ms, std::uint8_t out[6]) {
    return false;
}

std::uint64_t time_decode(const std::uint8_t in[6]) {
    return 0;
}
--- solution
#include <cstdint>

bool time_encode(std::uint64_t ms, std::uint8_t out[6]) {
    const std::uint64_t sec = ms / 1000;
    if (sec > 0xFFFFFFFFull) return false;
    const std::uint64_t frac = (ms % 1000) * 65536 / 1000;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) out[i] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(sec >> (24 - 8 * i));
    out[4] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(frac >> 8);
    out[5] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(frac);
    return true;
}

std::uint64_t time_decode(const std::uint8_t in[6]) {
    std::uint64_t sec = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) sec = (sec << 8) | in[i];
    const std::uint64_t frac = (static_cast<std::uint64_t>(in[4]) << 8) | in[5];
    return sec * 1000 + (frac * 1000 + 32768) / 65536;   // + half a unit rounds to nearest
}
--- hint
The leftover milliseconds are `ms % 1000`; multiply by 65536 before dividing by 1000, so the division does not throw the precision away.
--- hint
To round `a / b` to the nearest whole number, compute `(a + b / 2) / b`.
--- check test | 1500 ms
[] { std::uint8_t b[6] = {}; bool ok = time_encode(1500, b); return ok && b[0] == 0 && b[3] == 1 && b[4] == 0x80 && b[5] == 0 && time_decode(b) == 1500; }()
--- check test | Every millisecond of a second survives the round trip
[] { std::uint8_t b[6]; for (std::uint64_t ms = 7000; ms < 8000; ms++) { time_encode(ms, b); if (time_decode(b) != ms) return false; } return true; }()
--- check test | A large time, and one too large
[] { std::uint8_t b[6] = {9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9}; bool big = time_encode(4294967295999ull, b) && b[0] == 0xFF && b[3] == 0xFF; bool too = !time_encode(4294967296000ull, b); return big && too; }()
--- check test | Decoding rounds to the nearest millisecond
[] { std::uint8_t a[6] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF}; std::uint8_t c[6] = {0, 0, 0, 2, 0x00, 0x21}; return time_decode(a) == 1000 && time_decode(c) == 2001; }()

+++ practice | The length field
--- task
Two small functions every CCSDS decoder needs:

- `int data_length_field(int payload_len)`: the value of the data length field for one of this project's packets (4-byte time, payload, 2-byte CRC after the primary header), or -1 if `payload_len` is negative or over 96.
- `long long total_from_header(const std::uint8_t h[6])`: the total packet size, header included, that a primary header announces: 6 + the data length field + 1. It must be right for the largest field, 0xFFFF, so do not compute it in 16 bits.
--- starter
#include <cstdint>

int data_length_field(int payload_len) {
    return payload_len + 6;
}

long long total_from_header(const std::uint8_t h[6]) {
    std::uint16_t len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h[4] << 8) | h[5]);
    std::uint16_t total = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len + 7);
    return total;
}
--- solution
#include <cstdint>

int data_length_field(int payload_len) {
    if (payload_len < 0 || payload_len > 96) return -1;
    return 4 + payload_len + 2 - 1;   // the bytes after the primary header, minus 1
}

long long total_from_header(const std::uint8_t h[6]) {
    const long long len = (h[4] << 8) | h[5];
    return 6 + len + 1;
}
--- hint
After the primary header come 4 + payload + 2 bytes. The field stores that number minus 1.
--- hint
0xFFFF + 7 does not fit in 16 bits. Do the addition in `long long`.
--- check test | The field for a few payloads
data_length_field(0) == 5 && data_length_field(1) == 6 && data_length_field(96) == 101
--- check test | Payloads out of range
data_length_field(-1) == -1 && data_length_field(97) == -1
--- check test | Totals, including the largest field
[] { std::uint8_t a[6] = {0x08, 0x21, 0xC0, 0x05, 0x00, 0x06}; std::uint8_t b[6] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF}; std::uint8_t c[6] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}; return total_from_header(a) == 13 && total_from_header(b) == 65542 && total_from_header(c) == 7; }()

+++ practice | Debug: gaps that are not there
--- task
The ground reports lost packets on APID 0x040 every time the spacecraft's radio buffer is busy, although nothing was actually lost. This builder numbers packets from a counter. Find why a refused build makes the ground think a packet was lost, and fix it: a count must be used only by a packet that was really built.
--- starter
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

struct Builder {
    std::uint16_t next_seq;   // 14 bits
};

// Writes a 6-byte header for a packet with n payload bytes (and no
// secondary header) into out. Returns the bytes written, or 0 if out is too small.
std::size_t build_header(Builder* b, std::uint16_t apid, std::size_t n, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap) {
    std::uint16_t seq = b->next_seq;
    b->next_seq = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b->next_seq + 1) & 0x3FFF);
    if (cap < 6 + n) return 0;
    out[0] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(apid >> 8);
    out[1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(apid);
    out[2] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0xC0 | (seq >> 8));
    out[3] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(seq);
    out[4] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((n - 1) >> 8);
    out[5] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(n - 1);
    return 6;
}
--- solution
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

struct Builder {
    std::uint16_t next_seq;   // 14 bits
};

// Writes a 6-byte header for a packet with n payload bytes (and no
// secondary header) into out. Returns the bytes written, or 0 if out is too small.
std::size_t build_header(Builder* b, std::uint16_t apid, std::size_t n, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap) {
    if (cap < 6 + n) return 0;   // refuse before using up a sequence count
    std::uint16_t seq = b->next_seq;
    b->next_seq = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b->next_seq + 1) & 0x3FFF);
    out[0] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(apid >> 8);
    out[1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(apid);
    out[2] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(0xC0 | (seq >> 8));
    out[3] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(seq);
    out[4] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((n - 1) >> 8);
    out[5] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(n - 1);
    return 6;
}
--- hint
Follow the counter through a call where `cap` is too small. What has already happened to it when the function returns 0?
--- hint
Check the capacity before touching `next_seq`.

--- check test | Successful builds number 7, then 8
