--- check test | The count still wraps at 16383
[] { Builder b = {16383}; std::uint8_t out[16]; build_header(&b, 0x40, 1, out, 16); return b.next_seq == 0 && out[2] == 0xFF && out[3] == 0xFF; }()

+++ practice | An idle packet that fills the frame
--- task
A radio frame must go out on time and always holds exactly `frame_size` bytes. When real packets fill only part of it, the rest is filled with one **idle packet**: APID 0x7FF, telemetry, no secondary header, sequence flags 3, sequence count 0, and a data field of bytes 0x55.

Write `int fill_idle(std::uint8_t* frame, int used, int frame_size)`: write an idle packet into `frame + used` that ends exactly at `frame_size`, and return its size. A space packet needs at least 7 bytes (6 of header and at least 1 of data), so:

- return 0 and write nothing if `used == frame_size` (nothing to fill);
- return -1 and write nothing if the gap is 1 to 6 bytes, if `used` is negative or over `frame_size`, if `frame` is null, or if the gap is over 65,542 bytes (the data length field cannot describe it).

The data length field holds the data field's size minus 1.
--- starter
#include <cstdint>

int fill_idle(std::uint8_t* frame, int used, int frame_size) {
    return 0;
}
--- solution
#include <cstdint>

int fill_idle(std::uint8_t* frame, int used, int frame_size) {
    if (frame == nullptr || used < 0 || used > frame_size) return -1;
    const int gap = frame_size - used;
    if (gap == 0) return 0;
    if (gap < 7 || gap > 65542) return -1;
    std::uint8_t* p = frame + used;
    const int data = gap - 6;
    const unsigned word0 = (0u << 13) | (0u << 12) | (0u << 11) | 0x7FFu;
    const unsigned word1 = (3u << 14) | 0u;
    const unsigned length = static_cast<unsigned>(data - 1);
    p[0] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0 >> 8);
    p[1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0);
    p[2] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1 >> 8);
    p[3] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1);
    p[4] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(length >> 8);
    p[5] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(length);
    for (int i = 0; i < data; i++) p[6 + i] = 0x55;
    return gap;
}
--- hint
The idle packet's size is the whole gap. Its data field is the gap minus the 6 header bytes, and the length field is that minus 1.
--- hint
The first word is just the APID, 0x07FF, because version, type and the flag are all 0. The second word is `3 << 14`, 0xC000.
--- check test | Fills a 10-byte gap
[] { std::uint8_t f[64] = {}; int n = fill_idle(f, 54, 64); std::uint8_t* p = f + 54; return n == 10 && p[0] == 0x07 && p[1] == 0xFF && p[2] == 0xC0 && p[3] == 0x00 && p[4] == 0x00 && p[5] == 0x03 && p[6] == 0x55 && p[9] == 0x55; }()
--- check test | The smallest idle packet: 7 bytes
[] { std::uint8_t f[20] = {}; int n = fill_idle(f, 13, 20); return n == 7 && f[18] == 0 && f[17] == 0 && f[19] == 0x55 && f[13 + 5] == 0x00; }()
--- check test | Nothing to fill, and gaps too small to fill
[] { std::uint8_t f[20] = {}; bool zero = fill_idle(f, 20, 20) == 0; bool small = fill_idle(f, 15, 20) == -1 && f[15] == 0; return zero && small && fill_idle(f, 19, 20) == -1; }()
--- check test | Bad arguments and the largest gap
[] { static std::uint8_t f[70000]; bool bad = fill_idle(nullptr, 0, 64) == -1 && fill_idle(f, -1, 64) == -1 && fill_idle(f, 65, 64) == -1 && fill_idle(f, 0, 65543) == -1; int n = fill_idle(f, 0, 65542); return bad && n == 65542 && f[4] == 0xFF && f[5] == 0xFF && f[65541] == 0x55; }()

=== cap-flight-06 | Milestone 6: a decoder that rejects bad packets, and a stream that resynchronises
--- teach
Last milestone's encoder writes perfect packets. The decoder lives on the other side of a radio link, where nothing is perfect: bits flip, bytes go missing, a receiver locks on halfway through a packet, and noise arrives that looks almost like data. This milestone builds the code that faces all of it: a **decoder** that accepts a packet only when every check passes, a **stream decoder** that finds packets in a river of bytes and gets back on track after damage, and a **sequence tracker** that notices which packets never arrived.

### Rule one: never trust a length

Everything in a received packet was written by someone else, possibly damaged on the way. The most dangerous field is the data length, because the decoder uses it to decide how far to read. A decoder that believes a damaged length reads past the end of its buffer. So the decoder checks the header in an order where **every read is proven safe before it happens**:

1. **Null pointers:** `BadArg`.
2. **At least 6 bytes**, or it cannot even read the header: `TooShort`.
3. **Version 0**, the only one this project speaks: `BadVersion`.
4. **The secondary header flag is 1**, since every packet of ours has the time: otherwise `BadType`.
5. **The length is possible:** the total 6 + data length + 1 must be at least 12, and the payload (total − 12) at most 96: otherwise `BadLength`.
6. **All the bytes are there:** at least `total` bytes: otherwise `TooShort`.
7. **The CRC** over the first `total − 2` bytes matches the last two: otherwise `BadCrc`.

Only then does it fill in the caller's `Packet`. On any failure the outputs are untouched, the same contract as the byte reader.

### Why this order

- **Cheap before expensive.** The CRC reads every byte; the version check reads one. Garbage is usually caught in the first few checks.
- **Each check makes the next one safe.** Step 6 can only be tested after step 5 has proven the length is sane, and step 7 reads up to `total`, which step 6 has just proven is inside the buffer.
- **Length problems before missing bytes.** `BadLength` says "this header is nonsense"; `TooShort` says "this might be fine, the rest has not arrived yet". A stream decoder must treat those two very differently, so the decoder reports a nonsense length first, before it could be mistaken for a packet still arriving.

**Why it is correct:** by induction over the checks, after check k every byte the decoder has read lies inside the buffer, and a packet that passes all seven has a sane length, all its bytes present, and a CRC that matches. By last milestone's CRC properties, any damage of one or two bits, or any burst of up to 16 bits, fails check 7 (or an earlier one).

### Packets in a stream

A radio does not deliver packets one at a time; it delivers a stream of bytes. If a packet's length field is damaged, where does the next packet start? Without help, nowhere: every later byte is misread.

The help is an **attached sync marker**: four fixed bytes, 1A CF FC 1D, sent before every packet. It is the [[same marker CCSDS uses|asm]] on real downlinks. A receiver that has lost its place scans for the marker and tries again from there.

The marker can also appear by chance inside a payload or in noise. That is fine: a false marker is followed by bytes that fail the decoder's checks, almost always the CRC, and the receiver simply moves on.

### The stream decoder

`StreamDecoder` keeps a buffer of 512 bytes. `feed` appends bytes (all or nothing: if they do not all fit, nothing is appended and the answer is `Full`). `next` tries to take one good packet out:

1. Find the first marker in the buffer. If there is none, throw away all but the last 3 bytes (they might be the start of a marker whose other bytes have not arrived) and answer `Empty`.
2. Throw away everything before the marker.
3. Try to decode the bytes after the marker.
   - `Ok`: remove the marker and the packet from the buffer, answer `Ok`.
   - `TooShort`: the packet has not fully arrived. Leave everything and answer `Empty`; the next `feed` brings more.
   - Any other failure: count it (`BadCrc` as a CRC error, anything else as a bad header), throw away **one byte**, the first byte of this marker, and go back to step 1.

Why only one byte on a failure, when the header claims to know how long the packet is? Because the header is exactly what may be damaged. A length field hit by noise can claim 60 bytes when the packet had 20, and skipping 60 bytes would throw away the next good packet with it. Dropping one byte and scanning again finds the very next marker, wherever it is.

Every byte thrown away that was not part of a good packet is counted in `bytes_skipped`. On the ground those counters tell the operators how healthy the link is.

**It always finishes.** Each pass of the loop either returns or throws away at least one byte, and the buffer holds at most 512, so `next` makes at most 513 passes. Under the no-unbounded-loops rule, the loop carries that bound explicitly.

**Cost:** finding the marker is a scan, O(n) for n buffered bytes, and throwing bytes away shifts the rest down with `memmove`, also O(n). A burst of garbage can cost O(n²) steps in the worst case, with n at most 512: a fixed bound of a few hundred thousand byte operations, known before launch. A ring-buffer version would avoid the shifting at the price of more complex code; at 512 bytes the simple version wins.

### Which packets never arrived?

Each APID numbers its packets 0, 1, 2, … and wraps at 16384. The **sequence tracker** remembers the last count seen on each APID, in a `StaticMap`, and for each new packet computes how many counts were skipped:

```text
missed = (seq - last - 1) mod 16384
```

With last = 9 and seq = 12, packets 10 and 11 are missing: 2. Across the wrap, last = 16383 and seq = 1 gives (1 − 16383 − 1) mod 16384 = 1: packet 0 is missing. The mod makes the wrap disappear, and `& 0x3FFF` computes it, since 16384 is a power of two and the bitwise AND keeps the low 14 bits, even of a negative `int`.

The first packet on an APID misses nothing: there is nothing to compare it with. The same count twice in a row is a **duplicate**, which radios and retransmissions do produce; it is reported as `Duplicate` and counts as no loss.

The formula has a blind spot. A packet from the past (count 9 after count 10) looks like 16,382 lost packets, and exactly 16,384 lost packets look like none. Longer counters shrink the blind spot but cannot remove it: that is the price of [[any counter that wraps|wraparound]].

### How to test it

- the golden vector from last milestone, decoded field by field;
- every truncation, 0 to 12 bytes of it: always `TooShort`;
- one test per rejection, and a check that the order holds when two things are wrong at once;
- flip every single bit of a good packet, one at a time: the decoder must never say `Ok`;
- streams with garbage before, between and after packets; a corrupted packet between two good ones; bytes fed one at a time, so markers and packets arrive in pieces; a false marker followed by junk;
- sequence counts with a gap, across the wrap, duplicated, and on separate APIDs.

### Where it is used

- Every ground station decodes CCSDS frames this way: find the marker, check, extract packets, count gaps.
- Serial protocols such as HDLC use a flag byte in the same role as the marker; Ethernet begins each frame with a fixed preamble.
- [[Fuzzing|fuzzing]] tools hammer decoders with damaged input, because decoders are where attackers and radio noise both get in.

**Watch out:** throwing away the bytes you might still need. When there is no marker in the buffer, it is tempting to empty it completely, but the last three bytes may be the start of a marker whose fourth byte arrives with the next `feed`. Clear them and the packet after them is lost, but only when the bytes happen to arrive split at exactly that point, so the bug hides in every test that feeds whole packets. Feeding one byte at a time finds it.

::: context asm The marker in real downlinks
CCSDS calls 1A CF FC 1D the Attached Sync Marker. It was chosen because its bits correlate badly with shifted copies of themselves, so a receiver sliding along a noisy bit stream sees a sharp match at exactly one position. Real radios look for it at the bit level, before the bytes are even aligned, and then read fixed-length transfer frames that carry packets inside. This project puts a marker before each packet instead, which keeps the idea and drops the frame layer.
:::

::: context wraparound Counters that go round
Any counter with a fixed number of bits eventually wraps. The fix is not a wider counter but arithmetic that expects the wrap: compare with the difference modulo the counter's range, and trust it only while the true difference is less than half the range. TCP does this with 32-bit sequence numbers, and the Linux kernel's time comparisons do it with jiffies. Here, if more than 8,191 packets in a row can be lost, a 14-bit count cannot tell you how many.
:::

::: context fuzzing Throwing garbage on purpose
A fuzzer runs a program on millions of inputs made by mutating valid ones: flipping bits, cutting lengths, repeating fields. It watches for crashes, hangs and memory errors. Tools such as AFL and libFuzzer, combined with AddressSanitizer, have found thousands of bugs in image decoders, network stacks and file parsers. The single-bit-flip check in this milestone is the smallest possible fuzzer, and it already covers every one-bit error a radio can make.
:::
--- task
Write the decoding side. The starter has the constants.

1. `Status decode_packet(const std::uint8_t* in, std::size_t len, Packet* out, std::size_t* consumed)`: the seven checks, in the lesson's order and with its status codes. On success fill every field of `*out` (the header as unpacked, the time, `payload_len` and the payload bytes), set `*consumed` to the packet's total size, and return `Ok`. Bytes after the packet are allowed and ignored. On failure do not touch `*out` or `*consumed`.
2. `Status frame_packet(const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written)`: write the 4 marker bytes and then the `len` packet bytes; set `*written` to `len + 4`. `BadArg` for a null pointer or `len` of 0; `NoSpace` if `cap` is too small.
3. `class StreamDecoder` with a 512-byte buffer (`kStreamBufferBytes`):
   - `Status feed(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n)`: append; `BadArg` for null `data` with `n` over 0; `Full` if the bytes do not all fit, and then nothing is appended.
   - `Status next(Packet* out)`: the algorithm in the lesson. `Ok` with a packet, or `Empty` when no whole good packet is buffered. `BadArg` for a null `out`. Never loop more than 513 times.
   - `packets()` (good packets returned), `crc_errors()` (failures with `BadCrc`), `bad_headers()` (all other failures after a marker), `bytes_skipped()` (bytes thrown away that were not part of a good packet), `buffered()` (bytes waiting in the buffer).
4. `class SequenceTracker`, with a `StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32>` of the last count per APID:
   - `Status observe(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq, std::uint16_t* missed)`: `BadArg` for a null `missed`, an APID over 0x7FF or a count over 0x3FFF. The first packet on an APID: `*missed` = 0, `Ok` (or the map's `Full` if it already holds 32 APIDs). The same count as the last one: `*missed` = 0, count a duplicate, return `Duplicate`. Otherwise `*missed` = `(seq - last - 1) & 0x3FFF`, add it to the total, remember `seq`, `Ok`.
   - `total_missed()` and `duplicates()`.
--- starter
// ============================================================================
// ORBIT flight software core
// Rules, as on a real spacecraft:
//   - no heap allocation after start-up: fixed-size pools and static arrays
//   - no exceptions, no recursion
//   - every function checks its inputs and returns a status code
// ============================================================================
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// ---- Status codes: the project's whole error vocabulary ---------------------
// The numbers go into acknowledgement packets, so never reorder them.
enum class Status : std::uint8_t {
    Ok = 0,
    NotImpl,      // a stub: not written yet
    BadArg,       // an input is null or out of range
    Full,         // a fixed-capacity container has no room
    Empty,        // nothing to take out
    NotFound,     // no such key, id or handle
    NoSpace,      // an output buffer is too small, or a pool is used up
    Duplicate,    // the same thing twice
    OutOfRange,   // a result does not fit its type
    NotReady,     // called before set-up finished
    TooShort,     // fewer bytes than the format needs
    BadVersion,   // a packet version we do not speak
    BadType,      // the wrong kind of packet
    BadLength,    // a length field that cannot be right
    BadCrc,       // the checksum does not match
    UnknownApid,  // a packet for an application we do not have
    BadOpcode,    // no such command
    BadArgs,      // a command's arguments are wrong
    Forbidden,    // not allowed in the current mode
    Overrun,      // a frame ran out of time
};

const char* status_name(Status s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Status::Ok: return "OK";
        case Status::NotImpl: return "NOT_IMPL";
        case Status::BadArg: return "BAD_ARG";
        case Status::Full: return "FULL";
        case Status::Empty: return "EMPTY";
        case Status::NotFound: return "NOT_FOUND";
        case Status::NoSpace: return "NO_SPACE";
        case Status::Duplicate: return "DUPLICATE";
        case Status::OutOfRange: return "OUT_OF_RANGE";
        case Status::NotReady: return "NOT_READY";
        case Status::TooShort: return "TOO_SHORT";
        case Status::BadVersion: return "BAD_VERSION";
        case Status::BadType: return "BAD_TYPE";
        case Status::BadLength: return "BAD_LENGTH";
        case Status::BadCrc: return "BAD_CRC";
        case Status::UnknownApid: return "UNKNOWN_APID";
        case Status::BadOpcode: return "BAD_OPCODE";
        case Status::BadArgs: return "BAD_ARGS";
        case Status::Forbidden: return "FORBIDDEN";
        case Status::Overrun: return "OVERRUN";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// ---- Heap watch: counts every operator new, so the checks can prove that ----
// ---- the flight code never touches the heap. Leave it as it is. -------------
static long long g_heap_allocs = 0;

void* operator new(std::size_t n) {
    ++g_heap_allocs;
    void* p = std::malloc(n == 0 ? 1 : n);
    if (p == nullptr) std::abort();
    return p;
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { std::free(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { std::free(p); }

long long heap_allocs() { return g_heap_allocs; }

// ---- RingBuffer: a first-in, first-out queue of fixed capacity --------------
// Invariant: 0 <= count_ <= N, and the items, oldest first, sit at
// (head_ + 0) % N, (head_ + 1) % N, ..., (head_ + count_ - 1) % N.
template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class RingBuffer {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a ring buffer needs room for at least one item");

public:
    // Adds v at the back. Full when there is no room: nothing changes.
    Status push(const T& v) {
        if (count_ == N) return Status::Full;
        items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Adds v at the back; when full, the oldest item is dropped to make room.
    // Returns true when an item was dropped.
    bool push_overwrite(const T& v) {
        if (count_ < N) {
            items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
            ++count_;
            return false;
        }
        items_[head_] = v;          // the oldest slot becomes the newest
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        ++dropped_;
        return true;
    }

    // Takes the oldest item out into *out. Empty when there is none.
    Status pop(T* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        --count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest item into *out without taking it out.
    Status peek(T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the i-th oldest item (0 is the oldest) into *out.
    Status at(std::size_t i, T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (i >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = items_[(head_ + i) % N];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    void clear() {
        head_ = 0;
        count_ = 0;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return count_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    bool empty() const { return count_ == 0; }
    bool full() const { return count_ == N; }
    std::uint32_t dropped() const { return dropped_; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::size_t head_ = 0;       // index of the oldest item
    std::size_t count_ = 0;      // how many items are held
    std::uint32_t dropped_ = 0;  // items lost to push_overwrite
};

// ---- Pool: N fixed blocks, handed out and taken back in O(1) ----------------
// A handle names a block by its index and the block's generation. Releasing a
// block bumps its generation, so an old handle to it stops working.
struct Handle {
    std::uint16_t index;
    std::uint16_t gen;   // 0 never names a live block
};

constexpr Handle kNoHandle = {0xFFFF, 0};

template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class Pool {
    static_assert(N > 0 && N < 0xFFFF, "a pool holds 1 to 65534 blocks");

public:
    Pool() { reset(); }

    // Every block free again; every old handle stops working.
    void reset() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            next_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(i + 1);   // N marks the end
            gen_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[i] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[i] + 1);
            used_[i] = false;
        }
        free_head_ = 0;
        in_use_ = 0;
    }

    // Takes a free block, clears it to T{} and writes its handle.
    // The most recently released block is handed out first.
    Status acquire(Handle* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (free_head_ == N) {
            ++failures_;
            return Status::NoSpace;
        }
        const std::uint16_t i = free_head_;
        free_head_ = next_[i];
        used_[i] = true;
        items_[i] = T{};
        ++in_use_;
        if (in_use_ > high_water_) high_water_ = in_use_;
        *out = {i, gen_[i]};
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Gives a block back. A stale, foreign or doubled handle is refused.
    Status release(Handle h) {
        if (!valid(h)) return Status::BadArg;
        used_[h.index] = false;
        gen_[h.index] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[h.index] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[h.index] + 1);
        next_[h.index] = free_head_;
        free_head_ = h.index;
        --in_use_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    bool valid(Handle h) const { return h.index < N && h.gen != 0 && used_[h.index] && gen_[h.index] == h.gen; }

    T* get(Handle h) { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }
    const T* get(Handle h) const { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }

    std::size_t in_use() const { return in_use_; }
    std::size_t available() const { return N - in_use_; }
    std::size_t high_water() const { return high_water_; }
    std::uint32_t failures() const { return failures_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t next_[N] = {};   // free list, threaded through the indexes
    std::uint16_t gen_[N] = {};
    bool used_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t free_head_ = 0;  // N when no block is free
    std::size_t in_use_ = 0;
    std::size_t high_water_ = 0;   // the most blocks ever in use at once
    std::uint32_t failures_ = 0;   // acquires refused because none was free
};

// ---- Packet buffers and queues that share one pool --------------------------
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacketBytes = 128;
constexpr std::size_t kBufferCount = 24;

struct PacketBuffer {
    std::uint8_t bytes[kMaxPacketBytes];
    std::uint16_t len;
};

using BufferPool = Pool<PacketBuffer, kBufferCount>;

// A FIFO of packets. The bytes live in blocks of a shared pool; the queue
// itself holds only handles, so moving a packet never copies 128 bytes twice.
template <std::size_t Depth>
class PacketQueue {
public:
    explicit PacketQueue(BufferPool* pool) : pool_(pool) {}

    // Copies a packet in. NoSpace when the pool is used up, Full when this
    // queue is at its depth; either way nothing is queued and no block leaks.
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || bytes == nullptr || len == 0 || len > kMaxPacketBytes) return Status::BadArg;
        if (fifo_.full()) return Status::Full;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = pool_->acquire(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        std::memcpy(b->bytes, bytes, len);
        b->len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        fifo_.push(h);   // cannot fail: checked for room above
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest packet out and frees its block. If it does not fit
    // in cap bytes it stays queued and the result is NoSpace.
    Status take(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || out == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;   // cannot happen while the invariant holds
        if (b->len > cap) return Status::NoSpace;
        std::memcpy(out, b->bytes, b->len);
        *len = b->len;
        fifo_.pop(&h);
        pool_->release(h);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The length of the oldest packet, without taking it.
    Status front_len(std::size_t* len) const {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;
        *len = b->len;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return fifo_.size(); }
    bool empty() const { return fifo_.empty(); }
    static constexpr std::size_t depth() { return Depth; }

private:
    BufferPool* pool_;
    RingBuffer<Handle, Depth> fifo_;
};

// ---- StaticMap: a hash map of fixed capacity, open addressing ---------------
// Keys are unsigned integers (APIDs, opcodes, parameter ids). A key's home
// slot is key % N; collisions probe forward one slot at a time, wrapping.
// Erased slots become tombstones, so a search never stops early at a gap
// that used to hold something. Every loop runs at most N times.
template <typename K, typename V, std::size_t N>
class StaticMap {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a map needs at least one slot");

public:
    StaticMap() { clear(); }

    void clear() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) state_[i] = Slot::Empty;
        size_ = 0;
        last_probes_ = 0;
    }

    // Inserts key, or overwrites its value if it is already there.
    // Full when the key is new and no empty slot or tombstone is left.
    Status put(K key, const V& value) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at != N) {
            values_[at] = value;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        // Not present: reuse the first tombstone on the key's path, or the
        // first empty slot. Both are on the path locate() just walked.
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        for (std::size_t probes = 0; probes < N; ++probes) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) {
                state_[i] = Slot::Used;
                keys_[i] = key;
                values_[i] = value;
                ++size_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        return Status::Full;
    }

    Status get(K key, V* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = values_[at];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    V* find(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }
    const V* find(K key) const {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }

    bool contains(K key) const { return locate(key) != N; }

    Status erase(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        state_[at] = Slot::Tomb;
        --size_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Writes up to max keys into out, smallest first; returns how many.
    // Insertion sort into the caller's array: no heap, no recursion.
    std::size_t sorted_keys(K* out, std::size_t max) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return 0;
        std::size_t n = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) continue;
            const K k = keys_[i];
            if (n < max) {
                std::size_t j = n++;
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            } else if (max > 0 && k < out[max - 1]) {
                std::size_t j = max - 1;   // k beats the largest kept key
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            }
        }
        return n;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    // Slots examined by the last put, get, find, contains or erase.
    std::size_t last_probes() const { return last_probes_; }

private:
    enum class Slot : std::uint8_t { Empty, Used, Tomb };

    static std::size_t home(K key) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(key % N); }

    // The slot holding key, or N. Stops at an empty slot or after N probes;
    // a tombstone does not stop it.
    std::size_t locate(K key) const {
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        std::size_t probes = 0;
        while (probes < N) {
            ++probes;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Empty) break;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Used && keys_[i] == key) {
                last_probes_ = probes;
                return i;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        last_probes_ = probes;
        return N;
    }

    K keys_[N] = {};
    V values_[N] = {};
    Slot state_[N] = {};
    std::size_t size_ = 0;
    mutable std::size_t last_probes_ = 0;
};

// ---- Big-endian byte writing and reading, with a sticky error ---------------
// Network byte order: the most significant byte goes first. After the first
// write or read that does not fit, the object stays failed: every later call
// returns the same error and changes nothing, so a caller can do a whole
// run of calls and check ok() once at the end.
class ByteWriter {
public:
    ByteWriter(std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t cap) : buf_(buf), cap_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : cap) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t v) { return put(&v, 1); }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[2] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 2);
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[4] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 24), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 16),
                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 4);
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t v) { return u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(v)); }
    Status bytes(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (src == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        return put(src, n);
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return len_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > cap_ - len_) return fail(Status::NoSpace);   // len_ <= cap_ always, so no wrap
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, src, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t cap_;
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

class ByteReader {
public:
    ByteReader(const std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t len) : buf_(buf), len_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : len) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[1];
        const Status s = take(b, 1, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = b[0];
        return s;
    }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[2];
        const Status s = take(b, 2, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b[0] << 8) | b[1]);
        return s;
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[4];
        const Status s = take(b, 4, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            *v = (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[0]) << 24) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[1]) << 16) |
                 (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[2]) << 8) | static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[3]);
        }
        return s;
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t* v) {
        std::uint32_t u = 0;
        const Status s = u32(v == nullptr ? nullptr : &u);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::int32_t>(u);   // two's complement, defined since C++20
        return s;
    }
    Status bytes(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (dst == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status skip(std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t pos() const { return pos_; }
    std::size_t remaining() const { return len_ - pos_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status take(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n, bool have_out) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (!have_out) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    const std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t len_;
    std::size_t pos_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

// ---- CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE -----------------------------------------------------
// Polynomial 0x1021 (x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1), start value 0xFFFF, bits taken
// most significant first, no final XOR. crc16("123456789") is 0x29B1.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcInit = 0xFFFF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcPoly = 0x1021;

// One bit at a time: 8 shift-and-maybe-XOR steps per byte. The reference.
std::uint16_t crc16_bitwise(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return kCrcInit;
    std::uint16_t crc = kCrcInit;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ (data[i] << 8));
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

// The 256 answers to "what do 8 steps do to this top byte", worked out by
// the compiler, so the table costs nothing at start-up and sits in ROM.
struct CrcTable {
    std::uint16_t entry[256];
};

constexpr CrcTable make_crc_table() {
    CrcTable t{};
    for (int b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
        std::uint16_t crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b << 8);
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
        t.entry[b] = crc;
    }
    return t;
}

constexpr CrcTable kCrcTable = make_crc_table();

// Continues a CRC over more bytes: crc16_update(crc16(a), b) == crc16(a then b).
std::uint16_t crc16_update(std::uint16_t crc, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return crc;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t top = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((crc >> 8) ^ data[i]);
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((crc << 8) ^ kCrcTable.entry[top]);
    }
    return crc;
}

// One table lookup per byte.
std::uint16_t crc16(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return crc16_update(kCrcInit, data, n); }

// ---- The packet format ------------------------------------------------------
//  bytes 0-5   primary header, CCSDS style, big-endian:
//              version:3 | type:1 | secondary header flag:1 | APID:11
//              sequence flags:2 | sequence count:14
//              data length: bytes after the primary header, minus 1
//  bytes 6-9   secondary header: time in milliseconds since boot
//  bytes 10-   payload, 0 to kMaxPayload bytes
//  last 2      CRC-16 of every byte before it
constexpr std::size_t kPrimaryHeaderBytes = 6;
constexpr std::size_t kSecondaryHeaderBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kCrcBytes = 2;
constexpr std::size_t kPacketOverhead = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + kSecondaryHeaderBytes + kCrcBytes;   // 12
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPayload = 96;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacket = kPacketOverhead + kMaxPayload;   // 108
constexpr std::uint16_t kMaxApid = 0x7FF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSeqMask = 0x3FFF;
constexpr std::uint8_t kSeqUnsegmented = 3;

enum class PacketType : std::uint8_t { Telemetry = 0, Command = 1 };

struct PrimaryHeader {
    std::uint8_t version;       // 3 bits; always 0
    PacketType type;            // 1 bit
    bool has_secondary;         // 1 bit
    std::uint16_t apid;         // 11 bits
    std::uint8_t seq_flags;     // 2 bits; 3 means "not split"
    std::uint16_t seq_count;    // 14 bits
    std::uint16_t data_length;  // 16 bits
};

struct Packet {
    PrimaryHeader hdr;
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t payload_len;
    std::uint8_t payload[kMaxPayload];
};

// Packs the six header bytes. BadArg if a field does not fit its bits.
Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w) {
    if (w == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (h.version > 7 || h.apid > kMaxApid || h.seq_flags > 3 || h.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    const std::uint16_t word0 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.version << 13) | (static_cast<unsigned>(h.type) << 12) |
                                                           ((h.has_secondary ? 1u : 0u) << 11) | h.apid);
    const std::uint16_t word1 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.seq_flags << 14) | h.seq_count);
    w->u16(word0);
    w->u16(word1);
    w->u16(h.data_length);
    return w->status();
}

// Unpacks the six header bytes. Checks nothing but that they are there.
Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h) {
    if (r == nullptr || h == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint16_t word0 = 0, word1 = 0, length = 0;
    r->u16(&word0);
    r->u16(&word1);
    r->u16(&length);
    if (!r->ok()) return r->status();
    h->version = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0 >> 13);
    h->type = ((word0 >> 12) & 1u) ? PacketType::Command : PacketType::Telemetry;
    h->has_secondary = ((word0 >> 11) & 1u) != 0;
    h->apid = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word0 & kMaxApid);
    h->seq_flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1 >> 14);
    h->seq_count = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word1 & kSeqMask);
    h->data_length = length;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Writes p as a whole packet: header (data length and the secondary header
// flag worked out here), time, payload and CRC. *written is set only on Ok.
Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (out == nullptr || written == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.hdr.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (p.hdr.apid > kMaxApid || p.hdr.seq_flags > 3 || p.hdr.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.payload_len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    const std::size_t total = kPacketOverhead + p.payload_len;
    if (cap < total) return Status::NoSpace;
    PrimaryHeader h = p.hdr;
    h.has_secondary = true;
    h.data_length = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPrimaryHeaderBytes - 1);
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    const Status s = pack_primary(h, &w);
    if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
    w.u32(p.time_ms);
    w.bytes(p.payload, p.payload_len);
    w.u16(crc16(out, w.size()));
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Builds packets and numbers them: each APID has its own 14-bit sequence
// count, which starts at 0 and wraps from 16383 back to 0.
class PacketEncoder {
public:
    Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len,
                 std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
        if ((payload == nullptr && len > 0) || apid > kMaxApid) return Status::BadArg;
        if (len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        const std::uint16_t seq = found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
        if (found == nullptr && seq_.size() == seq_.capacity()) return Status::Full;
        Packet p{};
        p.hdr = {0, type, true, apid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
        p.time_ms = time_ms;
        p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        if (len > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload, payload, len);
        const Status s = encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        seq_.put(apid, static_cast<std::uint16_t>((seq + 1) & kSeqMask));   // only a sent packet uses a number
        ++built_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The count the next packet on apid will carry.
    std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const {
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        return found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
    }

    // Sets the next count for apid (ground tools use it to replay a pass).
    Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq) {
        if (apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        return seq_.put(apid, seq);
    }

    std::uint32_t packets_built() const { return built_; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> seq_;
    std::uint32_t built_ = 0;
};

// ---- Decoding: trust nothing that came over the radio -----------------------
Status decode_packet(const std::uint8_t* in, std::size_t len, Packet* out, std::size_t* consumed) { return Status::NotImpl; }

// ---- Framing: packets on a byte stream, each after a sync marker ------------
constexpr std::uint8_t kSyncMarker[4] = {0x1A, 0xCF, 0xFC, 0x1D};
constexpr std::size_t kSyncBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kStreamBufferBytes = 512;

Status frame_packet(const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) { return Status::NotImpl; }

class StreamDecoder {
public:
    Status feed(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return Status::NotImpl; }
    Status next(Packet* out) { return Status::NotImpl; }

    std::uint32_t packets() const { return 0; }
    std::uint32_t crc_errors() const { return 0; }
    std::uint32_t bad_headers() const { return 0; }
    std::uint32_t bytes_skipped() const { return 0; }
    std::size_t buffered() const { return 0; }

private:
    std::uint8_t buf_[kStreamBufferBytes] = {};
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
};

// ---- Sequence tracking: which packets never arrived -------------------------
class SequenceTracker {
public:
    Status observe(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq, std::uint16_t* missed) { return Status::NotImpl; }
    std::uint32_t total_missed() const { return 0xFFFFFFFFu; }
    std::uint32_t duplicates() const { return 0xFFFFFFFFu; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> last_;
};
