        if (id == nullptr || t.name == nullptr || t.fn == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (!valid_period(t.period) || t.offset >= t.period) return Status::BadArg;
        if (t.budget_us == 0 || t.budget_us > kMinorFrameUs) return Status::BadArg;
        if (built_) return Status::Forbidden;   // the schedule is fixed once built
        if (count_ == kMaxTasks) return Status::Full;
        tasks_[count_] = t;
        stats_[count_] = {0, 0, 0, 0, true};
        *id = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(count_);
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Builds the frame tables and proves them: in every minor frame, the
    // budgets of the tasks due must add up to at most kMinorFrameUs.
    // Overrun (and nothing built) if a frame is overbooked.
    Status build() {
        if (built_) return Status::Ok;
        // Priority order: a stable insertion sort of the ids by period.
        std::uint8_t order[kMaxTasks];
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            std::size_t j = i;
            while (j > 0 && tasks_[order[j - 1]].period > tasks_[i].period) {
                order[j] = order[j - 1];
                --j;
            }
            order[j] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i);
        }
        std::uint8_t table[kFramesPerMajor][kMaxTasks];
        std::uint8_t lens[kFramesPerMajor] = {};
        for (std::uint8_t f = 0; f < kFramesPerMajor; ++f) {
            std::uint32_t booked = 0;
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < count_; ++k) {
                const TaskSpec& t = tasks_[order[k]];
                if (f % t.period != t.offset) continue;
                booked += t.budget_us;
                table[f][lens[f]++] = order[k];
            }
            if (booked > kMinorFrameUs) return Status::Overrun;
        }
        std::memcpy(table_, table, sizeof table_);
        std::memcpy(lens_, lens, sizeof lens_);
        built_ = true;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Runs the tasks due in this minor frame, highest priority first.
    // Before starting a task, its whole budget must still fit in the frame;
    // if not, it is skipped this time. Returns Overrun if the frame used
    // more than kMinorFrameUs in the end, else Ok.
    Status run_frame() {
        if (!built_) return Status::NotReady;
        const std::uint8_t f = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(tick_ % kFramesPerMajor);
        const std::uint32_t now_ms = tick_ * (kMinorFrameUs / 1000);
        std::uint32_t used = 0;
        for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k < lens_[f]; ++k) {
            const std::uint8_t id = table_[f][k];
            const TaskSpec& t = tasks_[id];
            TaskStats& st = stats_[id];
            if (!st.enabled) continue;
            if (used + t.budget_us > kMinorFrameUs) {
                ++st.skips;
                if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvTaskSkipped, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(used));
                continue;
            }
            const std::uint32_t us = t.fn(t.ctx, tick_);
            ++st.runs;
            if (us > st.max_us) st.max_us = us;
            if (us > t.budget_us) {
                ++st.budget_overruns;
                if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvTaskOverrun, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(us));
            }
            used += us;
        }
        last_frame_us_ = used;
        ++tick_;
        if (used > kMinorFrameUs) {
            ++frame_overruns_;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvFrameOverrun, 0, static_cast<std::int32_t>(used));
            return Status::Overrun;
        }
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Status set_enabled(std::uint8_t id, bool on) {
        if (id >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        stats_[id].enabled = on;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Status find(const char* name, std::uint8_t* id) const {
        if (name == nullptr || id == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            if (std::strcmp(tasks_[i].name, name) == 0) {
                *id = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i);
                return Status::Ok;
            }
        }
        return Status::NotFound;
    }

    // Safe mode: only essential tasks keep running.
    void shed_nonessential() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            if (!tasks_[i].essential) stats_[i].enabled = false;
        }
    }
    void enable_all() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) stats_[i].enabled = true;
    }

    // The ids due in minor frame f, in the order they run; returns how many.
    std::uint8_t frame_tasks(std::uint8_t f, std::uint8_t* ids, std::uint8_t max) const {
        if (!built_ || f >= kFramesPerMajor || ids == nullptr) return 0;
        std::uint8_t n = 0;
        for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k < lens_[f] && n < max; ++k) ids[n++] = table_[f][k];
        return n;
    }

    const TaskStats* stats(std::uint8_t id) const { return id < count_ ? &stats_[id] : nullptr; }
    const char* task_name(std::uint8_t id) const { return id < count_ ? tasks_[id].name : "?"; }
    std::size_t task_count() const { return count_; }
    std::uint32_t tick() const { return tick_; }
    std::uint32_t frame_overruns() const { return frame_overruns_; }
    std::uint32_t last_frame_us() const { return last_frame_us_; }
    bool built() const { return built_; }

private:
    TaskSpec tasks_[kMaxTasks] = {};
    TaskStats stats_[kMaxTasks] = {};
    std::size_t count_ = 0;
    std::uint8_t table_[kFramesPerMajor][kMaxTasks] = {};
    std::uint8_t lens_[kFramesPerMajor] = {};
    bool built_ = false;
    std::uint32_t tick_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t frame_overruns_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t last_frame_us_ = 0;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
};

// ---- Modes ------------------------------------------------------------------
enum class Mode : std::uint8_t { Boot = 0, Nominal = 1, Safe = 2 };

const char* mode_name(Mode m) {
    switch (m) {
        case Mode::Boot: return "BOOT";
        case Mode::Nominal: return "NOMINAL";
        case Mode::Safe: return "SAFE";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvModeChange = 0x0301;

using ModeListener = void (*)(void* ctx, Mode from, Mode to);

// Legal moves: Boot -> Nominal, Boot -> Safe, Nominal -> Safe, Safe -> Nominal.
// Nothing goes back to Boot. Asking for the mode you are in is Ok and
// changes nothing.
class ModeManager {
public:
    void attach_log(EventLog* log) { log_ = log; }
    void listen(ModeListener fn, void* ctx) {
        listener_ = fn;
        listener_ctx_ = ctx;
    }

    Status request(Mode to, std::uint32_t now_ms) {
        if (to != Mode::Boot && to != Mode::Nominal && to != Mode::Safe) return Status::BadArg;
        if (to == mode_) return Status::Ok;
        if (to == Mode::Boot) return Status::Forbidden;
        const Mode from = mode_;
        mode_ = to;
        entered_ms_ = now_ms;
        ++transitions_;
        if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvModeChange, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(from), static_cast<std::int32_t>(to));
        if (listener_ != nullptr) listener_(listener_ctx_, from, to);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Mode mode() const { return mode_; }
    std::uint32_t entered_ms() const { return entered_ms_; }
    std::uint32_t transitions() const { return transitions_; }

private:
    Mode mode_ = Mode::Boot;
    std::uint32_t entered_ms_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t transitions_ = 0;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
    ModeListener listener_ = nullptr;
    void* listener_ctx_ = nullptr;
};

// ---- Commands ---------------------------------------------------------------
// A command is a Command-type packet to kCommandApid whose payload is one
// opcode byte followed by exactly that command's argument bytes.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCommandApid = 0x010;
constexpr std::uint16_t kAckApid = 0x011;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxCommands = 32;

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdAccepted = 0x0302;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdRejected = 0x0303;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdFailed = 0x0304;

using CommandFn = Status (*)(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t now_ms);

struct CommandDef {
    std::uint8_t opcode;
    const char* name;
    std::uint8_t arg_bytes;
    bool allowed_in_safe;
    CommandFn fn;
    void* ctx;
};

// What the ground hears back about one command.
struct Ack {
    std::uint16_t seq;      // the command packet's sequence count
    std::uint8_t opcode;    // 0 if it never got that far
    Status status;
};

class CommandHandler {
public:
    void attach(ModeManager* modes, EventLog* log) {
        modes_ = modes;
        log_ = log;
    }

    Status add(const CommandDef& def) {
        if (def.name == nullptr || def.fn == nullptr || def.arg_bytes > kMaxPayload - 1) return Status::BadArg;
        if (table_.contains(def.opcode)) return Status::Duplicate;
        return table_.put(def.opcode, def);
    }

    // Decodes, validates and runs one command, in this order:
    //   decode (its status) -> Command type (BadType) -> APID (UnknownApid)
    //   -> an opcode byte (BadArgs) -> known opcode (BadOpcode)
    //   -> exact argument length (BadArgs) -> allowed in this mode (Forbidden)
    //   -> run it. The ack always says how far it got.
    Status handle(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len, std::uint32_t now_ms, Ack* ack) {
        if (bytes == nullptr || ack == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        *ack = {0, 0, Status::Ok};
        Packet p;
        std::size_t used = 0;
        Status s = decode_packet(bytes, len, &p, &used);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            ack->seq = p.hdr.seq_count;
            if (p.hdr.type != PacketType::Command) s = Status::BadType;
            else if (p.hdr.apid != kCommandApid) s = Status::UnknownApid;
            else if (p.payload_len < 1) s = Status::BadArgs;
        }
        const CommandDef* def = nullptr;
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            ack->opcode = p.payload[0];
            def = table_.find(p.payload[0]);
            if (def == nullptr) s = Status::BadOpcode;
            else if (p.payload_len - 1u != def->arg_bytes) s = Status::BadArgs;
            else if (modes_ != nullptr && modes_->mode() == Mode::Safe && !def->allowed_in_safe) s = Status::Forbidden;
        }
        if (s != Status::Ok) {
            ++rejected_;
            ack->status = s;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdRejected, ack->opcode, static_cast<std::int32_t>(s));
            return s;
        }
        ++accepted_;
        ByteReader args(p.payload + 1, def->arg_bytes);
        s = def->fn(def->ctx, &args, now_ms);
        ack->status = s;
        if (s != Status::Ok) {
            ++failed_;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdFailed, def->opcode, static_cast<std::int32_t>(s));
        } else if (log_ != nullptr) {
            log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdAccepted, def->opcode, 0);
        }
        return s;
    }

    void reset_counters() { accepted_ = rejected_ = failed_ = 0; }
    std::uint32_t accepted() const { return accepted_; }   // passed every check
    std::uint32_t rejected() const { return rejected_; }   // failed a check
    std::uint32_t failed() const { return failed_; }       // accepted, but running it failed
    const CommandDef* lookup(std::uint8_t opcode) const { return table_.find(opcode); }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint8_t, CommandDef, kMaxCommands> table_;
    ModeManager* modes_ = nullptr;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
    std::uint32_t accepted_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t rejected_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t failed_ = 0;
};

// The ack packet's payload: seq (2 bytes), opcode, status code.
Status encode_ack(const Ack& ack, PacketEncoder* enc, std::uint32_t now_ms, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (enc == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t payload[4];
    ByteWriter w(payload, sizeof payload);
    w.u16(ack.seq);
    w.u8(ack.opcode);
    w.u8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ack.status));
    return enc->build(PacketType::Telemetry, kAckApid, now_ms, payload, w.size(), out, cap, written);
}

// Ground side: a command packet with the given sequence count.
Status build_command(std::uint16_t seq, std::uint8_t opcode, const std::uint8_t* args, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t time_ms,
                     std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if ((args == nullptr && n > 0) || n > kMaxPayload - 1 || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    Packet p{};
    p.hdr = {0, PacketType::Command, true, kCommandApid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
    p.time_ms = time_ms;
    p.payload[0] = opcode;
    if (n > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload + 1, args, n);
    p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(n + 1);
    return encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
}

// ---- The standard commands ----------------------------------------------------
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpNoop = 0x01;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpSetMode = 0x02;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpResetCounters = 0x03;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpSetLimits = 0x04;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpEnableTask = 0x05;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpDisableTask = 0x06;

Status cmd_noop(void*, ByteReader*, std::uint32_t) { return Status::Ok; }

// One byte: the mode wanted (0, 1 or 2). ctx: the ModeManager.
Status cmd_set_mode(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t now_ms) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t m = 0;
    if (args->u8(&m) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    if (m > 2) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<ModeManager*>(ctx)->request(static_cast<Mode>(m), now_ms);
}

// No bytes. ctx: the CommandHandler whose counters go back to 0.
Status cmd_reset_counters(void* ctx, ByteReader*, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    static_cast<CommandHandler*>(ctx)->reset_counters();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// The monitors a SET_LIMITS command can reach.
struct MonitorBank {
    LimitMonitor* monitors;
    std::uint8_t count;
};

// 17 bytes: monitor index, then red_low, yellow_low, yellow_high, red_high
// as big-endian int32. ctx: a MonitorBank.
Status cmd_set_limits(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    const MonitorBank* bank = static_cast<const MonitorBank*>(ctx);
    std::uint8_t which = 0;
    Limits l{};
    args->u8(&which);
    args->i32(&l.red_low);
    args->i32(&l.yellow_low);
    args->i32(&l.yellow_high);
    args->i32(&l.red_high);
    if (!args->ok()) return Status::BadArgs;
    if (which >= bank->count) return Status::NotFound;
    if (!limits_valid(l)) return Status::BadArgs;
    return bank->monitors[which].set_limits(l);
}

// One byte: the task id. ctx: the Scheduler.
Status cmd_enable_task(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t id = 0;
    if (args->u8(&id) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<Scheduler*>(ctx)->set_enabled(id, true);
}

Status cmd_disable_task(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t id = 0;
    if (args->u8(&id) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<Scheduler*>(ctx)->set_enabled(id, false);
}

// ---- Redundant sensors: a primary and a backup ------------------------------
// Isolation takes a failed unit out of use and switches to its partner.
class SensorPair {
public:
    Status configure(std::uint16_t primary, std::uint16_t backup) {
        if (primary == backup) return Status::BadArg;
        unit_[0] = primary;
        unit_[1] = backup;
        failed_[0] = failed_[1] = false;
        active_ = 0;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Marks unit failed. If it was the active one and its partner is still
    // good, switches to the partner. NotFound if the unit is not in this
    // pair; NoSpace if there is no good unit left to switch to.
    Status isolate(std::uint16_t unit) {
        int k = -1;
        if (unit == unit_[0]) k = 0;
        else if (unit == unit_[1]) k = 1;
        if (k < 0) return Status::NotFound;
        failed_[k] = true;
        if (k != active_) return Status::Ok;   // the spare failed: keep flying on the active one
        if (failed_[1 - k]) return Status::NoSpace;
        active_ = 1 - k;
        ++switches_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Ground says a unit is good again.
    Status restore(std::uint16_t unit) {
        if (unit == unit_[0]) failed_[0] = false;
        else if (unit == unit_[1]) failed_[1] = false;
        else return Status::NotFound;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::uint16_t active() const { return unit_[active_]; }
    bool failed(std::uint16_t unit) const {
        return (unit == unit_[0] && failed_[0]) || (unit == unit_[1] && failed_[1]);
    }
    std::uint32_t switches() const { return switches_; }

private:
    std::uint16_t unit_[2] = {0, 1};
    bool failed_[2] = {false, false};
    int active_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t switches_ = 0;
};

// ---- Fault detection, isolation and recovery (FDIR) ---------------------------
enum class FaultId : std::uint8_t { SensorStuck = 0, LimitRed = 1, TaskOverrun = 2, FrameOverrun = 3, UplinkErrors = 4 };
constexpr std::size_t kFaultKinds = 5;

enum class Response : std::uint8_t { LogOnly, Isolate, Recover, SafeMode };

const char* response_name(Response r) {
    switch (r) {
        case Response::LogOnly: return "LOG";
        case Response::Isolate: return "ISOLATE";
        case Response::Recover: return "RECOVER";
        case Response::SafeMode: return "SAFE_MODE";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// Respond with `first` for the first `budget` reports of this fault; after
// that, with `then`. A budget of 0 goes straight to `then`.
struct FaultRule {
    FaultId id;
    Response first;
    std::uint8_t budget;
    Response then;
};

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvFault = 0x0401;       // source: fault id, value: the unit
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvResponse = 0x0402;    // source: fault id, value: the response taken
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvEscalated = 0x0403;   // source: fault id, value: the response that failed

// The unit-specific actions, supplied by whoever owns the units.
struct FaultHooks {
    Status (*isolate)(void* ctx, FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit);
    Status (*recover)(void* ctx, FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit);
    void* ctx;
};

class FaultManager {
public:
    void attach(ModeManager* modes, EventLog* log, FaultHooks hooks) {
        modes_ = modes;
        log_ = log;
        hooks_ = hooks;
    }

    Status set_rule(const FaultRule& r) {
        const std::size_t k = static_cast<std::size_t>(r.id);
        if (k >= kFaultKinds) return Status::BadArg;
        rules_[k] = r;
        has_rule_[k] = true;
        used_[k] = 0;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // A monitor confirmed fault id on unit. Picks the response by the rule
    // and its budget, carries it out and writes it to *taken. If an Isolate
    // or Recover action fails, escalates at once to safe mode.
    Status report(FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit, std::uint32_t now_ms, Response* taken) {
        const std::size_t k = static_cast<std::size_t>(id);
        if (k >= kFaultKinds || taken == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (!has_rule_[k]) return Status::NotFound;
        ++count_[k];
        latched_ = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(latched_ | (1u << k));
        note(now_ms, kEvFault, id, unit);
        const FaultRule& r = rules_[k];
        Response resp = r.then;
        if (used_[k] < r.budget) {
            resp = r.first;
            ++used_[k];
        }
        Status s = act(resp, id, unit, now_ms);
        if (s != Status::Ok && resp != Response::SafeMode) {
            note(now_ms, kEvEscalated, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(resp));
            resp = Response::SafeMode;
            s = act(resp, id, unit, now_ms);
        }
        note(now_ms, kEvResponse, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(resp));
        *taken = resp;
        return s;
    }

    // Ground clears a fault: the latch goes and its budget starts again.
    Status clear(FaultId id) {
        const std::size_t k = static_cast<std::size_t>(id);
        if (k >= kFaultKinds) return Status::BadArg;
        latched_ = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(latched_ & ~(1u << k));
        used_[k] = 0;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::uint16_t latched() const { return latched_; }
    std::uint32_t count(FaultId id) const {
        const std::size_t k = static_cast<std::size_t>(id);
        return k < kFaultKinds ? count_[k] : 0;
    }
    std::uint32_t safe_entries() const { return safe_entries_; }

private:
    Status act(Response r, FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit, std::uint32_t now_ms) {
        switch (r) {
            case Response::LogOnly: return Status::Ok;
            case Response::Isolate:
                return hooks_.isolate == nullptr ? Status::NotImpl : hooks_.isolate(hooks_.ctx, id, unit);
            case Response::Recover:
                return hooks_.recover == nullptr ? Status::NotImpl : hooks_.recover(hooks_.ctx, id, unit);
            case Response::SafeMode:
                if (modes_ == nullptr) return Status::NotReady;
                if (modes_->mode() != Mode::Safe) ++safe_entries_;
                return modes_->request(Mode::Safe, now_ms);
        }
        return Status::BadArg;
    }
    void note(std::uint32_t now_ms, std::uint16_t ev, FaultId id, std::int32_t value) {
        if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, ev, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(id), value);
    }

    FaultRule rules_[kFaultKinds] = {};
    bool has_rule_[kFaultKinds] = {};
    std::uint8_t used_[kFaultKinds] = {};
    std::uint32_t count_[kFaultKinds] = {};
    std::uint16_t latched_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t safe_entries_ = 0;
    ModeManager* modes_ = nullptr;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
    FaultHooks hooks_ = {nullptr, nullptr, nullptr};
};

// Ground command: CLEAR_FAULT, one byte (the fault id). ctx: the FaultManager.
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpClearFault = 0x07;

Status cmd_clear_fault(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t id = 0;
    if (args->u8(&id) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    if (id >= kFaultKinds) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<FaultManager*>(ctx)->clear(static_cast<FaultId>(id));
}

// ---- Housekeeping: the spacecraft's health, once a second -------------------
constexpr std::uint16_t kHkApid = 0x020;
constexpr std::size_t kHkSensors = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kHkBytes = 36;

struct HkReport {
    Mode mode;
    std::uint16_t faults_latched;   // bit k: FaultId k is latched
    std::uint32_t uptime_s;
    std::uint16_t frame_overruns;
    std::uint16_t cmds_accepted;
    std::uint16_t cmds_rejected;
    std::uint16_t events;
    std::uint8_t pool_high_water;
    std::uint16_t tm_dropped;
    std::uint8_t gyro_active;       // the unit id in use
    std::int32_t sensor[kHkSensors];
    std::uint8_t flags;             // bit i: sensor i stuck; bit 4+i: sensor i in red
};

// Counters are 32-bit on board and 16-bit in the report: they stop at
// 65535 instead of wrapping, so a big number never reads as a small one.
std::uint16_t sat16(std::uint32_t v) { return v > 0xFFFFu ? 0xFFFFu : static_cast<std::uint16_t>(v); }
std::uint8_t sat8(std::size_t v) { return v > 0xFFu ? 0xFFu : static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v); }

// The fixed layout, big-endian, in the order the struct lists the fields.
Status hk_serialize(const HkReport& r, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* n) {
    if (out == nullptr || n == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (cap < kHkBytes) return Status::NoSpace;
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    w.u8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(r.mode));
    w.u16(r.faults_latched);
    w.u32(r.uptime_s);
    w.u16(r.frame_overruns);
    w.u16(r.cmds_accepted);
    w.u16(r.cmds_rejected);
    w.u16(r.events);
    w.u8(r.pool_high_water);
    w.u16(r.tm_dropped);
    w.u8(r.gyro_active);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kHkSensors; ++i) w.i32(r.sensor[i]);
    w.u8(r.flags);
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *n = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Ground side. BadLength unless exactly kHkBytes; BadArg for a mode byte
// that is not a mode. *out is left alone on failure.
Status hk_parse(const std::uint8_t* in, std::size_t n, HkReport* out) {
    if (in == nullptr || out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (n != kHkBytes) return Status::BadLength;
    ByteReader r(in, n);
    HkReport h{};
    std::uint8_t mode = 0;
    r.u8(&mode);
    if (mode > 2) return Status::BadArg;
    h.mode = static_cast<Mode>(mode);
    r.u16(&h.faults_latched);
    r.u32(&h.uptime_s);
    r.u16(&h.frame_overruns);
    r.u16(&h.cmds_accepted);
    r.u16(&h.cmds_rejected);
    r.u16(&h.events);
    r.u8(&h.pool_high_water);
    r.u16(&h.tm_dropped);
    r.u8(&h.gyro_active);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kHkSensors; ++i) r.i32(&h.sensor[i]);
    r.u8(&h.flags);
    if (!r.ok()) return r.status();
    *out = h;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Three lines for the ground display. Returns what snprintf returns.
int hk_format(const HkReport& r, char* buf, std::size_t cap) {
    if (buf == nullptr) return -1;
    return std::snprintf(buf, cap,
                         "mode=%s uptime=%us faults=0x%04X\n"
                         "cmds ok=%u rejected=%u overruns=%u events=%u pool_hw=%u dropped=%u gyro=%u\n"
                         "sensors %d %d %d %d flags=0x%02X",
                         mode_name(r.mode), static_cast<unsigned>(r.uptime_s), static_cast<unsigned>(r.faults_latched),
                         static_cast<unsigned>(r.cmds_accepted), static_cast<unsigned>(r.cmds_rejected),
                         static_cast<unsigned>(r.frame_overruns), static_cast<unsigned>(r.events),
                         static_cast<unsigned>(r.pool_high_water), static_cast<unsigned>(r.tm_dropped),
                         static_cast<unsigned>(r.gyro_active), static_cast<int>(r.sensor[0]), static_cast<int>(r.sensor[1]),
                         static_cast<int>(r.sensor[2]), static_cast<int>(r.sensor[3]), static_cast<unsigned>(r.flags));
}

// ---- The downlink: two queues, one pool, a byte budget per frame ------------
constexpr std::size_t kDownlinkBytesPerFrame = 300;

class Downlink {
public:
    explicit Downlink(BufferPool* pool) : urgent_(pool), routine_(pool) {}

    // Queues a packet. A packet that cannot be queued is dropped and
    // counted; the status says why.
    Status send(const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, bool urgent) {
        const Status s = urgent ? urgent_.put(pkt, len) : routine_.put(pkt, len);
        if (s == Status::Full || s == Status::NoSpace) ++dropped_;
        return s;
    }

    // Writes queued packets into out, each after the sync marker: urgent
    // ones first, oldest first within a queue. Stops before the first
    // packet whose framed size would pass `budget` or `cap` bytes, so a
    // packet is never split. Returns the bytes written.
    std::size_t pump(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t budget) {
        if (out == nullptr) return 0;
        const std::size_t limit = budget < cap ? budget : cap;
        std::size_t used = 0;
        for (std::size_t guard = 0; guard < kBufferCount; ++guard) {
            const bool from_urgent = !urgent_.empty();
            if (!from_urgent && routine_.empty()) break;
            std::size_t len = 0;
            if (from_urgent) urgent_.front_len(&len); else routine_.front_len(&len);
            if (used + kSyncBytes + len > limit) break;
            std::memcpy(out + used, kSyncMarker, kSyncBytes);
            std::size_t got = 0;
            if (from_urgent) urgent_.take(out + used + kSyncBytes, len, &got); else routine_.take(out + used + kSyncBytes, len, &got);
            used += kSyncBytes + got;
            ++sent_;
        }
        return used;
    }

    std::uint32_t sent() const { return sent_; }
    std::uint32_t dropped() const { return dropped_; }
    std::size_t queued() const { return urgent_.size() + routine_.size(); }

private:
    PacketQueue<8> urgent_;
    PacketQueue<16> routine_;
    std::uint32_t sent_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t dropped_ = 0;
};

// ---- The flight system: every part, wired together --------------------------
// The mission's configuration, as the systems engineers wrote it down.
constexpr std::size_t kSensorCount = 4;
constexpr std::uint16_t kUnitBusV = 0;
constexpr std::uint16_t kUnitBattT = 1;
constexpr std::uint16_t kUnitGyroA = 2;
constexpr std::uint16_t kUnitGyroB = 3;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSensorTmApid = 0x021;
constexpr std::uint16_t kScienceApid = 0x030;
constexpr std::uint16_t kStuckWindow = 20;
constexpr std::uint8_t kPersistSet = 5;
constexpr std::uint8_t kPersistClear = 10;
constexpr std::size_t kUplinkDepth = 8;
constexpr std::size_t kCommandsPerFrame = 2;
constexpr std::uint32_t kUplinkErrorLimit = 3;   // bad command packets in one second

const SensorConfig kSensorConfigs[kSensorCount] = {
    {"BUS_V", kUnitBusV, {0, 8, 1}, 3500, 6, 11u},             // mV: 3500 counts is 28.0 V
    {"BATT_T", kUnitBattT, {-50000, 25, 1}, 2800, 4, 22u},     // m°C: 2800 counts is 20.0 °C
    {"GYRO_A", kUnitGyroA, {-20480, 10, 1}, 2048, 3, 33u},     // m°/s: 2048 counts is 0
    {"GYRO_B", kUnitGyroB, {-20480, 10, 1}, 2048, 3, 44u},
};

const Limits kSensorLimits[kSensorCount] = {
    {24000, 26000, 31000, 33000},
    {-5000, 0, 35000, 45000},
    {-5000, -2000, 2000, 5000},
    {-5000, -2000, 2000, 5000},
};

struct TaskPlan {
    const char* name;
    std::uint8_t period;
    std::uint8_t offset;
    std::uint32_t budget_us;
    std::uint32_t cost_us;   // what it normally uses
    bool essential;
};

// Task ids are their places in this table.
constexpr std::uint8_t kTaskSense = 0, kTaskMonitor = 1, kTaskCommand = 2, kTaskDownlink = 3;
constexpr std::uint8_t kTaskScience = 4, kTaskTelemetry = 5, kTaskHk = 6, kTaskFdir = 7;
constexpr std::size_t kTaskCount = 8;

const TaskPlan kTaskPlan[kTaskCount] = {
    {"SENSE", 1, 0, 20000, 12000, true},
    {"MONITOR", 1, 0, 10000, 6000, true},
    {"COMMAND", 1, 0, 10000, 3000, true},
    {"DOWNLINK", 1, 0, 5000, 2000, true},
    {"SCIENCE", 2, 1, 30000, 20000, false},
    {"TELEMETRY", 5, 2, 15000, 8000, false},
    {"HK", 10, 3, 15000, 9000, true},
    {"FDIR", 10, 4, 10000, 4000, true},
};

const FaultRule kFaultRules[kFaultKinds] = {
    {FaultId::SensorStuck, Response::Isolate, 255, Response::SafeMode},
    {FaultId::LimitRed, Response::SafeMode, 0, Response::SafeMode},
    {FaultId::TaskOverrun, Response::Recover, 2, Response::Isolate},
    {FaultId::FrameOverrun, Response::LogOnly, 255, Response::SafeMode},
    {FaultId::UplinkErrors, Response::LogOnly, 255, Response::LogOnly},
};

class FlightSystem {
public:
    FlightSystem() : downlink_(&pool_) {}

    // Start-up: the only time anything is configured. Ends in Nominal mode.
    Status init() {
        if (ready_) return Status::Ok;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSensorCount; ++i) {
            Status s = sensors_[i].configure(kSensorConfigs[i]);
            if (s == Status::Ok) s = limits_[i].configure(kSensorLimits[i], kPersistSet, kPersistClear);
            if (s == Status::Ok) s = stuck_[i].configure(kStuckWindow);
            if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        }
        Status s = gyro_.configure(kUnitGyroA, kUnitGyroB);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        modes_.attach_log(&log_);
        modes_.listen(&FlightSystem::on_mode, this);
        sched_.attach_log(&log_);
        cmds_.attach(&modes_, &log_);
        faults_.attach(&modes_, &log_, {&FlightSystem::isolate_hook, &FlightSystem::recover_hook, this});
        for (std::size_t k = 0; k < kFaultKinds && s == Status::Ok; ++k) s = faults_.set_rule(kFaultRules[k]);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        const TaskFn fns[kTaskCount] = {&task_sense, &task_monitor, &task_command, &task_downlink,
                                        &task_science, &task_telemetry, &task_hk, &task_fdir};
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kTaskCount; ++i) {
            const TaskPlan& p = kTaskPlan[i];
            std::uint8_t id = 0;
            s = sched_.add({p.name, fns[i], this, p.period, p.offset, p.budget_us, p.essential}, &id);
            if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        }
        s = sched_.build();
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        bank_ = {limits_, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(kSensorCount)};
        const CommandDef defs[] = {
            {kOpNoop, "NOOP", 0, true, &cmd_noop, nullptr},
            {kOpSetMode, "SET_MODE", 1, true, &cmd_set_mode, &modes_},
            {kOpResetCounters, "RESET_COUNTERS", 0, true, &cmd_reset_counters, &cmds_},
            {kOpSetLimits, "SET_LIMITS", 17, false, &cmd_set_limits, &bank_},
            {kOpEnableTask, "ENABLE_TASK", 1, false, &cmd_enable_task, &sched_},
            {kOpDisableTask, "DISABLE_TASK", 1, true, &cmd_disable_task, &sched_},
            {kOpClearFault, "CLEAR_FAULT", 1, true, &cmd_clear_fault, &faults_},
        };
        for (const CommandDef& d : defs) {
            s = cmds_.add(d);
            if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        }
        ready_ = true;
        return modes_.request(Mode::Nominal, 0);
    }

    // One minor frame.
    Status step() {
        if (!ready_) return Status::NotReady;
        radio_len_ = 0;
        return sched_.run_frame();
    }

    // Ground to spacecraft: queues a command packet for the COMMAND task.
    Status uplink(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len) {
        if (bytes == nullptr || len == 0 || len > kMaxPacketBytes) return Status::BadArg;
        PacketBuffer b{};
        std::memcpy(b.bytes, bytes, len);
        b.len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        return uplink_.push(b);
    }

    // The bytes the DOWNLINK task sent during the last frame.
    const std::uint8_t* radio() const { return radio_; }
    std::size_t radio_len() const { return radio_len_; }

    // ---- Fault injection, for testing on the ground ----
    Status inject_sensor(std::uint16_t unit, SensorFault f, std::int32_t param) {
        if (unit >= kSensorCount) return Status::NotFound;
        if (f == SensorFault::None) {
            sensors_[unit].sim().clear_fault();
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        return sensors_[unit].sim().inject(f, param);
    }
    // The task reports `us` microseconds for its next `runs` runs.
    Status inject_overrun(std::uint8_t task, std::uint32_t us, std::uint32_t runs) {
        if (task >= kTaskCount) return Status::NotFound;
        overrun_us_[task] = us;
        overrun_runs_[task] = runs;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    // The next n packets sent get one bit of their CRC flipped.
    void corrupt_downlink(std::uint32_t n) { corrupt_pending_ = n; }

    HkReport hk() const {
        HkReport r{};
        r.mode = modes_.mode();
        r.faults_latched = faults_.latched();
        r.uptime_s = now_ms() / 1000;
        r.frame_overruns = sat16(sched_.frame_overruns());
        r.cmds_accepted = sat16(cmds_.accepted());
        r.cmds_rejected = sat16(cmds_.rejected());
        r.events = sat16(log_.total());
        r.pool_high_water = sat8(pool_.high_water());
        r.tm_dropped = sat16(downlink_.dropped());
        r.gyro_active = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(gyro_.active());
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSensorCount; ++i) {
            r.sensor[i] = sensors_[i].filtered();
            if (stuck_[i].stuck()) r.flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(r.flags | (1u << i));
            if (is_red(limits_[i].state())) r.flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(r.flags | (1u << (4 + i)));
        }
        return r;
    }

    std::uint32_t now_ms() const { return sched_.tick() * (kMinorFrameUs / 1000); }
    const ModeManager& modes() const { return modes_; }
    const Scheduler& sched() const { return sched_; }
    const CommandHandler& cmds() const { return cmds_; }
    const FaultManager& faults() const { return faults_; }
    const EventLog& events() const { return log_; }
    const SensorPair& gyro() const { return gyro_; }
    const SensorChannel& sensor(std::size_t i) const { return sensors_[i < kSensorCount ? i : 0]; }
    const LimitMonitor& limit(std::size_t i) const { return limits_[i < kSensorCount ? i : 0]; }
    const Downlink& downlink() const { return downlink_; }
    std::uint32_t uplink_errors() const { return uplink_errors_; }
    std::uint32_t packets_sent() const { return tm_.packets_built(); }

private:
    // What a task reports: its normal cost, or an injected overrun.
    std::uint32_t cost(std::uint8_t task) {
        if (overrun_runs_[task] > 0) {
            --overrun_runs_[task];
            return overrun_us_[task];
        }
        return kTaskPlan[task].cost_us;
    }

    // Builds a packet and queues it for the downlink.
    void send_tm(std::uint16_t apid, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len, bool urgent) {
        std::uint8_t pkt[kMaxPacket];
        std::size_t n = 0;
        if (tm_.build(PacketType::Telemetry, apid, now_ms(), payload, len, pkt, sizeof pkt, &n) != Status::Ok) return;
        if (corrupt_pending_ > 0) {
            --corrupt_pending_;
            pkt[n - 1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(pkt[n - 1] ^ 0x01);
        }
        downlink_.send(pkt, n, urgent);
    }

    static std::uint32_t task_sense(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        for (std::uint16_t i = 0; i < kSensorCount; ++i) {
            fs->sensors_[i].sample(nullptr);
            bool became = false, back = false;
            fs->stuck_[i].update(fs->sensors_[i].last_raw(), &became, &back);
            if (back) fs->log_.record(fs->now_ms(), kEvSensorUnstuck, i, fs->sensors_[i].last_raw());
            if (became) {
                fs->log_.record(fs->now_ms(), kEvSensorStuck, i, fs->sensors_[i].last_raw());
                Response r;
                fs->faults_.report(FaultId::SensorStuck, i, fs->now_ms(), &r);
            }
        }
        return fs->cost(kTaskSense);
    }

    static std::uint32_t task_monitor(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        const std::uint16_t watched[3] = {kUnitBusV, kUnitBattT, fs->gyro_.active()};
        for (std::uint16_t unit : watched) {
            bool changed = false;
            const std::int32_t v = fs->sensors_[unit].filtered();
            fs->limits_[unit].update(v, &changed);
            if (!changed) continue;
            const LimitState st = fs->limits_[unit].state();
            const std::uint16_t ev = st == LimitState::Nominal ? kEvLimitNominal : (is_red(st) ? kEvLimitRed : kEvLimitYellow);
            fs->log_.record(fs->now_ms(), ev, unit, v);
            if (is_red(st)) {
                Response r;
                fs->faults_.report(FaultId::LimitRed, unit, fs->now_ms(), &r);
            }
        }
        return fs->cost(kTaskMonitor);
    }

    static std::uint32_t task_command(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        std::uint32_t extra = 0;
        for (std::size_t k = 0; k < kCommandsPerFrame; ++k) {
            PacketBuffer b;
            if (fs->uplink_.pop(&b) != Status::Ok) break;
            Ack ack;
            const Status s = fs->cmds_.handle(b.bytes, b.len, fs->now_ms(), &ack);
            if (s == Status::TooShort || s == Status::BadVersion || s == Status::BadType ||
                s == Status::BadLength || s == Status::BadCrc) {
                ++fs->uplink_errors_;
            }
            std::uint8_t pkt[kMaxPacket];
            std::size_t n = 0;
            if (encode_ack(ack, &fs->tm_, fs->now_ms(), pkt, sizeof pkt, &n) == Status::Ok) {
                if (fs->corrupt_pending_ > 0) {
                    --fs->corrupt_pending_;
                    pkt[n - 1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(pkt[n - 1] ^ 0x01);
                }
                fs->downlink_.send(pkt, n, true);
            }
            extra += 1000;
        }
        return fs->cost(kTaskCommand) + extra;
    }

    static std::uint32_t task_downlink(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        fs->radio_len_ = fs->downlink_.pump(fs->radio_, sizeof fs->radio_, kDownlinkBytesPerFrame);
        return fs->cost(kTaskDownlink);
    }

    // Science: the four filtered values, big-endian int32.
    static std::uint32_t task_science(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        std::uint8_t payload[16];
        ByteWriter w(payload, sizeof payload);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSensorCount; ++i) w.i32(fs->sensors_[i].filtered());
        fs->send_tm(kScienceApid, payload, w.size(), false);
        return fs->cost(kTaskScience);
    }

    // Sensor telemetry: each sensor's raw count (2 bytes) and limit state (1 byte).
    static std::uint32_t task_telemetry(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        std::uint8_t payload[12];
        ByteWriter w(payload, sizeof payload);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kSensorCount; ++i) {
            w.u16(fs->sensors_[i].last_raw());
            w.u8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(fs->limits_[i].state()));
        }
        fs->send_tm(kSensorTmApid, payload, w.size(), false);
        return fs->cost(kTaskTelemetry);
    }

    static std::uint32_t task_hk(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        std::uint8_t payload[kHkBytes];
        std::size_t n = 0;
        if (hk_serialize(fs->hk(), payload, sizeof payload, &n) == Status::Ok) fs->send_tm(kHkApid, payload, n, false);
        return fs->cost(kTaskHk);
    }

    // Once a second: turn counters that grew into faults.
    static std::uint32_t task_fdir(void* ctx, std::uint32_t) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        Response r;
        const std::uint32_t overruns = fs->sched_.frame_overruns();
        if (overruns != fs->seen_frame_overruns_) {
            fs->seen_frame_overruns_ = overruns;
            fs->faults_.report(FaultId::FrameOverrun, 0, fs->now_ms(), &r);
        }
        for (std::uint8_t id = 0; id < kTaskCount; ++id) {
            const std::uint32_t n = fs->sched_.stats(id)->budget_overruns;
            if (n != fs->seen_task_overruns_[id]) {
                fs->seen_task_overruns_[id] = n;
                fs->faults_.report(FaultId::TaskOverrun, id, fs->now_ms(), &r);
            }
        }
        if (fs->uplink_errors_ - fs->seen_uplink_errors_ >= kUplinkErrorLimit) {
            fs->faults_.report(FaultId::UplinkErrors, 0, fs->now_ms(), &r);
        }
        fs->seen_uplink_errors_ = fs->uplink_errors_;
        return fs->cost(kTaskFdir);
    }

    // Isolation: a stuck gyro hands over to its partner; an overrunning
    // task that is not essential is switched off. Anything else cannot be
    // isolated, and the fault manager escalates.
    static Status isolate_hook(void* ctx, FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        if (id == FaultId::SensorStuck) {
            if (unit != kUnitGyroA && unit != kUnitGyroB) return Status::NotFound;
            return fs->gyro_.isolate(unit);
        }
        if (id == FaultId::TaskOverrun) {
            if (unit >= kTaskCount || kTaskPlan[unit].essential) return Status::Forbidden;
            fs->task_isolated_[unit] = true;
            return fs->sched_.set_enabled(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(unit), false);
        }
        return Status::NotImpl;
    }

    // Recovery: restarting a task clears whatever made it overrun.
    static Status recover_hook(void* ctx, FaultId id, std::uint16_t unit) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        if (id != FaultId::TaskOverrun || unit >= kTaskCount) return Status::NotImpl;
        fs->overrun_runs_[unit] = 0;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Safe mode sheds the tasks that are not essential; leaving it brings
    // them back, except the ones fault management switched off.
    static void on_mode(void* ctx, Mode, Mode to) {
        FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);
        if (to == Mode::Safe) {
            fs->sched_.shed_nonessential();
            return;
        }
        fs->sched_.enable_all();
        for (std::uint8_t id = 0; id < kTaskCount; ++id) {
            if (fs->task_isolated_[id]) fs->sched_.set_enabled(id, false);
        }
    }

    EventLog log_;
    ModeManager modes_;
    Scheduler sched_;
    CommandHandler cmds_;
    FaultManager faults_;
    SensorChannel sensors_[kSensorCount];
    LimitMonitor limits_[kSensorCount];
    StuckMonitor stuck_[kSensorCount];
    SensorPair gyro_;
    MonitorBank bank_ = {nullptr, 0};
    BufferPool pool_;
    Downlink downlink_;
    PacketEncoder tm_;
    RingBuffer<PacketBuffer, kUplinkDepth> uplink_;
    std::uint8_t radio_[kDownlinkBytesPerFrame] = {};
    std::size_t radio_len_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t overrun_us_[kTaskCount] = {};
    std::uint32_t overrun_runs_[kTaskCount] = {};
    bool task_isolated_[kTaskCount] = {};
    std::uint32_t corrupt_pending_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t uplink_errors_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t seen_frame_overruns_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t seen_task_overruns_[kTaskCount] = {};
    std::uint32_t seen_uplink_errors_ = 0;
    bool ready_ = false;
};
--- hint
Write the helpers first: `cost(task)` for the injected overruns, and `send_tm(apid, payload, len, urgent)`, which builds a packet at `now_ms()`, corrupts it if a corruption is pending, and gives it to the downlink. Every telemetry task then takes a few lines.
--- hint
Each task, hook and the listener is a `static` member function whose first line is `FlightSystem* fs = static_cast<FlightSystem*>(ctx);`. In `init`, pass `this` as every context, and write the task functions into a local array in `kTaskPlan` order, so the loop that adds tasks can use `fns[i]`.
--- hint
The fault hooks are passed as one `FaultHooks` value: `{&FlightSystem::isolate_hook, &FlightSystem::recover_hook, this}`. The command table is easiest as a local array of seven `CommandDef`s added in a loop.

[] { static BufferPool pool; static Downlink d(&pool); std::uint8_t a[10] = {1}; std::uint8_t b[10] = {2}; std::uint8_t c[10] = {3}; d.send(a, 10, false); d.send(b, 10, true); d.send(c, 10, false); std::uint8_t out[300]; std::size_t n = d.pump(out, sizeof out, 300); return n == 42 && out[0] == 0x1A && out[3] == 0x1D && out[4] == 2 && out[18] == 1 && out[32] == 3 && d.sent() == 3 && d.queued() == 0 && pool.in_use() == 0; }()
--- check test | Still works (milestone 12): The budget is never passed and packets are never split
[] { static BufferPool pool; static Downlink d(&pool); std::uint8_t p[96] = {}; for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) d.send(p, 96, false); std::uint8_t out[400]; std::size_t n1 = d.pump(out, sizeof out, 300); std::size_t n2 = d.pump(out, sizeof out, 99); std::size_t n3 = d.pump(out, sizeof out, 100); return n1 == 300 && n2 == 0 && n3 == 100 && d.queued() == 0 && d.sent() == 4; }()

+++ practice | A member function behind a C callback
--- task
A timer library calls back through a plain function pointer with a context, C style. Write a class whose own member counts the calls:

```cpp fragment
using Callback = void (*)(void* ctx, int code);

struct Timer {
    Callback cb;
    void* ctx;
    void fire(int code) { if (cb != nullptr) cb(ctx, code); }
};
```

Write `class Counter` with:

- `void attach(Timer* t)`: make `t` call this object (store a function and `this`).
- `int calls() const` and `int last_code() const` (0 before any call).
- a private **static** member function that the timer calls, which forwards to the object.
--- starter
using Callback = void (*)(void* ctx, int code);

struct Timer {
    Callback cb;
    void* ctx;
    void fire(int code) { if (cb != nullptr) cb(ctx, code); }
};

class Counter {
public:
    void attach(Timer* t) {}
    int calls() const { return 0; }
    int last_code() const { return 0; }
};
--- solution
using Callback = void (*)(void* ctx, int code);

struct Timer {
    Callback cb;
    void* ctx;
    void fire(int code) { if (cb != nullptr) cb(ctx, code); }
};

class Counter {
public:
    void attach(Timer* t) {
        if (t == nullptr) return;
        t->cb = &Counter::on_fire;
        t->ctx = this;
    }
    int calls() const { return calls_; }
    int last_code() const { return last_; }

private:
    // A static member: no hidden this, so it converts to a plain function pointer.
    static void on_fire(void* ctx, int code) {
        Counter* self = static_cast<Counter*>(ctx);
        self->calls_++;
        self->last_ = code;
    }

    int calls_ = 0;
    int last_ = 0;
};
--- hint
A non-static member function has a hidden `this` parameter, so it cannot be stored in `Callback`. A static one can.
--- hint
Pass `this` as the context, and cast it back to `Counter*` inside the static function.
--- check test | Calls reach the object
[] { Timer t = {nullptr, nullptr}; Counter c; c.attach(&t); t.fire(3); t.fire(7); return c.calls() == 2 && c.last_code() == 7; }()
--- check test | Two counters, two timers
[] { Timer a = {nullptr, nullptr}, b = {nullptr, nullptr}; Counter x, y; x.attach(&a); y.attach(&b); a.fire(1); b.fire(2); b.fire(4); return x.calls() == 1 && y.calls() == 2 && y.last_code() == 4 && x.last_code() == 1; }()
--- check test | Before any call, and a null timer
[] { Counter c; c.attach(nullptr); return c.calls() == 0 && c.last_code() == 0; }()

+++ practice | Start-up order from dependencies
--- task
Each of `n` components (up to 16) must be initialised after the components it depends on. `deps[i][j]` is `true` when component `i` depends on component `j`.

Write `int init_order(const bool deps[16][16], int n, int* order)`: fill `order` with an order in which to initialise all `n` components, and return `n`. Use Kahn's algorithm without recursion: repeatedly pick, among the components not yet placed whose dependencies are all placed, the one with the **smallest** index. Return -1 if there is a cycle (some components can never be placed), or if `n` is not 0 to 16 or a pointer is null while `n` is more than 0.
--- starter
int init_order(const bool deps[16][16], int n, int* order) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) order[i] = i;
    return n;
}
--- solution
int init_order(const bool deps[16][16], int n, int* order) {
    if (n < 0 || n > 16 || (n > 0 && (deps == nullptr || order == nullptr))) return -1;
    bool placed[16] = {};
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        int pick = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < n && pick < 0; i++) {
            if (placed[i]) continue;
            bool ready = true;
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {
                if (deps[i][j] && !placed[j]) ready = false;
            }
            if (ready) pick = i;
        }
        if (pick < 0) return -1;   // everything left waits on something left: a cycle
        placed[pick] = true;
        order[k] = pick;
    }
    return n;
}
--- hint
Each round, scan the components from index 0 and take the first one that is not placed and whose dependencies are all placed.
--- hint
If a round finds nothing to place while some remain, they depend on each other in a cycle.
--- check test | The log before the scheduler before the tasks
[] { static bool d[16][16] = {}; d[0][2] = true; d[1][0] = true; d[1][2] = true; int o[16]; int n = init_order(d, 3, o); return n == 3 && o[0] == 2 && o[1] == 0 && o[2] == 1; }()
--- check test | No dependencies: index order
[] { static bool d[16][16] = {}; int o[16]; init_order(d, 4, o); return o[0] == 0 && o[1] == 1 && o[2] == 2 && o[3] == 3; }()
--- check test | A cycle is refused
[] { static bool d[16][16] = {}; d[0][1] = true; d[1][2] = true; d[2][0] = true; int o[16]; return init_order(d, 3, o) == -1; }()
--- check test | Bad input and no components
[] { static bool d[16][16] = {}; int o[16]; return init_order(d, 17, o) == -1 && init_order(nullptr, 2, o) == -1 && init_order(d, 0, nullptr) == 0; }()

+++ practice | A RAM map
--- task
Static objects are placed in RAM one after another, each at the next address that is a multiple of its alignment, as struct fields are. Given the objects' sizes and alignments in placement order, write:

```cpp fragment
long long ram_map(const long long* size, const long long* align, int n, long long* offset, long long ram);
```

It fills `offset[i]` with each object's start address (the first starts at 0) and returns the total bytes used (the end of the last object). Return -1 if the total is more than `ram`, if a pointer is null while `n` is more than 0, or if a size is negative or an alignment is not a power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, …).

An address `a` rounded up to a power of two `p` is `(a + p - 1) & ~(p - 1)`.
--- starter
long long ram_map(const long long* size, const long long* align, int n, long long* offset, long long ram) {
    long long at = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        offset[i] = at;
        at += size[i];
    }
    return at;
}
--- solution
long long ram_map(const long long* size, const long long* align, int n, long long* offset, long long ram) {
    if (n > 0 && (size == nullptr || align == nullptr || offset == nullptr)) return -1;
    long long at = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const long long p = align[i];
        if (size[i] < 0 || p < 1 || (p & (p - 1)) != 0) return -1;
        at = (at + p - 1) & ~(p - 1);   // round up to the alignment
        offset[i] = at;
        at += size[i];
    }
    return at > ram ? -1 : at;
}
--- hint
A power of two has exactly one 1 bit, so `p & (p - 1)` is 0 for it (and `p` must be at least 1).
--- hint
Round the running address up before placing each object, then add its size.
--- check test | Padding between objects
[] { long long s[3] = {3, 8, 2}; long long a[3] = {1, 8, 2}; long long o[3]; long long t = ram_map(s, a, 3, o, 1000); return t == 18 && o[0] == 0 && o[1] == 8 && o[2] == 16; }()
--- check test | Too big for the RAM
[] { long long s[2] = {60000, 10000}; long long a[2] = {4, 4}; long long o[2]; return ram_map(s, a, 2, o, 65536) == -1 && ram_map(s, a, 2, o, 70000) == 70000; }()
--- check test | Bad alignments and sizes
[] { long long s[1] = {4}; long long bad[1] = {3}; long long zero[1] = {0}; long long neg[1] = {-1}; long long a1[1] = {1}; long long o[1]; return ram_map(s, bad, 1, o, 100) == -1 && ram_map(s, zero, 1, o, 100) == -1 && ram_map(neg, a1, 1, o, 100) == -1 && ram_map(nullptr, a1, 1, o, 100) == -1 && ram_map(nullptr, nullptr, 0, nullptr, 0) == 0; }()

+++ practice | A pipeline that stops at the first failure
--- task
A data path is a list of stages, each a function that takes a value, may change it, and returns 0 for success or an error code. Run them in order:

```cpp fragment
using Stage = int (*)(int* value);
```

Write `int run_pipeline(const Stage* stages, int n, int* value, int* failed_at)`: call each stage on `*value` in order and stop at the first that returns non-zero; return that code, and set `*failed_at` to its index. If all succeed, return 0 and set `*failed_at` to -1. A null stage counts as failing with code 99. Return -1 (and change nothing) if `value` or `failed_at` is null, or `stages` is null while `n` is more than 0.
--- starter
using Stage = int (*)(int* value);

int run_pipeline(const Stage* stages, int n, int* value, int* failed_at) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) stages[i](value);
    *failed_at = -1;
    return 0;
}
--- solution
using Stage = int (*)(int* value);

int run_pipeline(const Stage* stages, int n, int* value, int* failed_at) {
    if (value == nullptr || failed_at == nullptr || (stages == nullptr && n > 0)) return -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const int code = stages[i] == nullptr ? 99 : stages[i](value);
        if (code != 0) {
            *failed_at = i;
            return code;
        }
    }
    *failed_at = -1;
    return 0;
}
--- hint
Check each stage's result straight after calling it; do not call the next one after a failure.
--- hint
Test the stage pointer for null before calling it.
--- check test | All stages run
[] { Stage s[3] = {[](int* v) { *v += 1; return 0; }, [](int* v) { *v *= 10; return 0; }, [](int* v) { *v -= 3; return 0; }}; int v = 4, at = 7; return run_pipeline(s, 3, &v, &at) == 0 && v == 47 && at == -1; }()
--- check test | Stops at the first failure
[] { Stage s[3] = {[](int* v) { *v += 1; return 0; }, [](int*) { return 5; }, [](int* v) { *v = 0; return 0; }}; int v = 1, at = 7; return run_pipeline(s, 3, &v, &at) == 5 && at == 1 && v == 2; }()
--- check test | A null stage
[] { Stage s[2] = {nullptr, [](int* v) { *v = 0; return 0; }}; int v = 9, at = 7; return run_pipeline(s, 2, &v, &at) == 99 && at == 0 && v == 9; }()
--- check test | Bad arguments and no stages
[] { int v = 1, at = 7; return run_pipeline(nullptr, 2, &v, &at) == -1 && run_pipeline(nullptr, 0, nullptr, &at) == -1 && at == 7 && run_pipeline(nullptr, 0, &v, &at) == 0 && at == -1; }()

+++ practice | Debug: the wrong task switched off
--- task
The ground sent DISABLE_TASK for the science task, id `TASK_SCIENCE`, but the telemetry task stopped instead. The ids are defined as positions in the plan table, but `setup` adds the tasks in a different order, so the scheduler numbers them differently. Fix `setup` so every task's scheduler id equals its constant.
--- starter
#include <cstring>

enum { TASK_SENSE = 0, TASK_SCIENCE = 1, TASK_TELEMETRY = 2, TASK_COUNT = 3 };

struct Plan {
    const char* name;
    int period;
};

const Plan kPlan[TASK_COUNT] = {{"SENSE", 1}, {"SCIENCE", 2}, {"TELEMETRY", 5}};

struct Sched {
    const char* names[8];
    int count;
    int add(const char* name) { names[count] = name; return count++; }
};

// Adds the plan's tasks; afterwards, sched.names[TASK_X] must be task X's name.
void setup(Sched* s) {
    s->count = 0;
    s->add(kPlan[TASK_SENSE].name);
    s->add(kPlan[TASK_TELEMETRY].name);
    s->add(kPlan[TASK_SCIENCE].name);
}
--- solution
#include <cstring>

enum { TASK_SENSE = 0, TASK_SCIENCE = 1, TASK_TELEMETRY = 2, TASK_COUNT = 3 };

struct Plan {
    const char* name;
    int period;
};

const Plan kPlan[TASK_COUNT] = {{"SENSE", 1}, {"SCIENCE", 2}, {"TELEMETRY", 5}};

struct Sched {
    const char* names[8];
    int count;
    int add(const char* name) { names[count] = name; return count++; }
};

// Adds the plan's tasks; afterwards, sched.names[TASK_X] must be task X's name.
void setup(Sched* s) {
    s->count = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < TASK_COUNT; i++) s->add(kPlan[i].name);   // table order, so ids match the constants
}
--- hint
The scheduler gives ids in the order tasks are added. In which order does `setup` add them?
--- hint
Add them in a loop over the table, so the order can never drift from the constants again.
--- check test | Science is where its id says
[] { Sched s; setup(&s); return std::strcmp(s.names[TASK_SCIENCE], "SCIENCE") == 0 && std::strcmp(s.names[TASK_TELEMETRY], "TELEMETRY") == 0; }()
--- check test | All three, and no more
[] { Sched s; setup(&s); return s.count == 3 && std::strcmp(s.names[TASK_SENSE], "SENSE") == 0; }()
--- check test | Setting up twice starts again
[] { Sched s; setup(&s); setup(&s); return s.count == 3 && std::strcmp(s.names[1], "SCIENCE") == 0; }()

+++ practice | Checking the configuration at start-up
--- task
Before configuring anything, flight software checks its tables. A sensor table row is:

```cpp fragment
struct Row {
    int id;
    const char* name;
    int gain_den;
    int base_raw;
    int red_low, yellow_low, yellow_high, red_high;
};
```

Write `int check_table(const Row* rows, int n, int* bad_row)`. Check the rows in order and stop at the first problem: return its code and set `*bad_row` to the row's index. The checks for row `i`, in order: `1` a null or empty name; `2` `gain_den` 0 or less; `3` `base_raw` outside 0 to 4095; `4` limits not in order (`red_low <= yellow_low <= yellow_high <= red_high`); `5` an id already used by an earlier row; `6` a name already used by an earlier row (compare with `std::strcmp`). If every row is fine, return 0 and set `*bad_row` to -1. Return -1 if `bad_row` is null, or `rows` is null while `n` is more than 0.
--- starter
struct Row {
    int id;
    const char* name;
    int gain_den;
    int base_raw;
    int red_low, yellow_low, yellow_high, red_high;
};

int check_table(const Row* rows, int n, int* bad_row) {
    *bad_row = -1;
    return 0;
}
--- solution
#include <cstring>

struct Row {
    int id;
    const char* name;
    int gain_den;
    int base_raw;
    int red_low, yellow_low, yellow_high, red_high;
};

static int check_row(const Row* rows, int i) {
    const Row& r = rows[i];
    if (r.name == nullptr || r.name[0] == '\0') return 1;
    if (r.gain_den <= 0) return 2;
    if (r.base_raw < 0 || r.base_raw > 4095) return 3;
    if (!(r.red_low <= r.yellow_low && r.yellow_low <= r.yellow_high && r.yellow_high <= r.red_high)) return 4;
    for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        if (rows[j].id == r.id) return 5;
    }
    for (int j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        if (std::strcmp(rows[j].name, r.name) == 0) return 6;
    }
    return 0;
}

int check_table(const Row* rows, int n, int* bad_row) {
    if (bad_row == nullptr || (rows == nullptr && n > 0)) return -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const int code = check_row(rows, i);
        if (code != 0) {
            *bad_row = i;
            return code;
        }
    }
    *bad_row = -1;
    return 0;
}
--- hint
Check one row completely, in the given order, before moving to the next; the earlier rows have already passed, so their names are safe to compare.
--- hint
Duplicates only need a look at the rows before the current one.
--- check test | A good table
[] { Row t[2] = {{0, "BUS_V", 1, 3500, 24000, 26000, 31000, 33000}, {1, "BATT_T", 1, 2800, -5000, 0, 35000, 45000}}; int b = 7; return check_table(t, 2, &b) == 0 && b == -1; }()
--- check test | The first problem wins
[] { Row t[3] = {{0, "A", 1, 100, 0, 1, 2, 3}, {1, "B", 0, 5000, 0, 1, 2, 3}, {2, "", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; int b = 7; return check_table(t, 3, &b) == 2 && b == 1; }()
--- check test | Each kind of problem
[] { int b; Row n1[1] = {{0, nullptr, 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; Row n3[1] = {{0, "A", 1, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; Row n4[1] = {{0, "A", 1, 1, 0, 3, 2, 3}}; Row n5[2] = {{4, "A", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}, {4, "B", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; Row n6[2] = {{4, "A", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}, {5, "A", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; return check_table(n1, 1, &b) == 1 && check_table(n3, 1, &b) == 3 && check_table(n4, 1, &b) == 4 && check_table(n5, 2, &b) == 5 && b == 1 && check_table(n6, 2, &b) == 6; }()
--- check test | Bad input and an empty table
[] { int b = 7; Row t[1] = {{0, "A", 1, 1, 0, 1, 2, 3}}; return check_table(t, 1, nullptr) == -1 && check_table(nullptr, 1, &b) == -1 && check_table(nullptr, 0, &b) == 0 && b == -1; }()

=== cap-flight-14 | Milestone 14: a simulated hour, with faults injected from a script
--- teach
The flight system runs, one frame at a time, and every part has been tested alone and wired together. What is left is the test that flight teams trust most: fly it. This milestone reads a **scenario** from standard input, a script of faults and ground commands at given seconds, flies a full simulated hour (36,000 minor frames) with a **ground station** listening to the radio, prints every event as it happens, and ends with a summary. The checks give it a script that breaks things on purpose and compare what it prints, line by line, with what the specification says must happen.

### Why a whole hour

Unit tests prove each part does what its author meant. Long runs find what nobody meant: a counter that wraps after 40 minutes, an event log that overflows on a busy second, a recovery that works once but not twice, a sequence gap that only appears when two faults overlap. Real missions run their flight software for days on a test bench, with scripted faults, before launch. Here an hour takes a few hundredths of a second, because [[time is simulated|sim-time]] and nothing waits.

### A scenario is a script

Each line of a scenario is a second, a verb and its arguments:

```text
# comments and blank lines are ignored
45 bias BATT_T 200
90 cmd DISABLE_TASK TELEMETRY
```

The verbs: `stuck`, `dead` and `clear` a sensor; `bias` a sensor by some counts; `spike` a sensor for some samples; `overrun` a task with a cost in microseconds for some runs; `corrupt` the next n downlinked packets; `garble` the next n commands sent; and `cmd`, followed by a command name and its arguments in words. Seconds run from 0 to 3599 and never go down from one line to the next, so the scenario can be applied with a single cursor moving forward.

A script in a file, rather than faults hard-coded in a test, is how test teams work: the same flight code runs many scenarios, and a new failure found in orbit becomes a new script. It is also how this milestone meets the rule "use stdin for injected scenarios".

### Parsing it without trusting it

A scenario is input, so the parser treats it like a packet: every word checked, nothing assumed. Each line is copied into a fixed buffer of 160 characters, cut into at most 8 words with the C library's [[word splitter|strtok]], `strtok`, and parsed into an `Injection` struct, a fixed record that holds everything any verb needs. Names are looked up in the configuration tables (`find_name`), numbers are read with `strtol` and range-checked (`parse_int`), and a command's arguments are packed into bytes exactly as the ground would send them, with a `ByteWriter`. The first bad line stops the parse and its number is reported, so whoever wrote the script can fix it. The whole scenario lives in a fixed array of 64 injections: no heap, even on the ground side of the test.

### The ground station

The ground station is the other end of the radio. Each frame it is handed the bytes the downlink task sent, feeds them to milestone 6's stream decoder, and for every good packet:

- runs the sequence tracker, so lost packets show up as gaps;
- if it is housekeeping, parses it with `hk_parse` and keeps the latest report;
- if it is an acknowledgement, counts it as an ACK (status `OK`) or a NAK (anything else).

It also sends commands: it builds each with `build_command` and its own sequence count, starting at 0, and uplinks it. A `garble` in the scenario makes it flip a bit of the next few commands' CRC on the way, as a noisy uplink would.

### One hour, frame by frame

`run_hour` initialises the flight system, then, for each of the 36,000 ticks:

1. applies every injection whose second is due, `second × 10 == tick`, in script order, just before the frame;
2. runs the frame;
3. hands the radio bytes to the ground station;
4. prints every event recorded since the last print, oldest first, one line each (so the first frame also prints the switch to `Nominal` that start-up recorded).

Printing reads the flight event log directly, the way a test bench reads a debug port. Each frame records only a handful of events, so the new ones are always among the 64 the log holds.

### Turning numbers into words

The flight side stores events as numbers. The ground side keeps a **dictionary**, here a set of small name functions and one `format_event`, that turns them into lines such as:

```text
t=900.4 FAULT UPLINK_ERRORS unit=0
t=1262.0 MODE SAFE -> NOMINAL
```

The time is seconds with one decimal, because frames are 100 ms apart. Keeping the words on the ground means the flight code never carries strings for its events, and the wording can improve without a software upload.

### Checking that it responded exactly as specified

The checks compare the whole printed transcript with the expected one. That sounds brittle, and it is meant to be: every line is a requirement. A stuck gyro must be isolated at the sample the persistence rules predict, not "sometime soon"; a garbled command must be rejected and counted; three uplink errors in one second must raise a fault at the next FDIR run; safe mode must shed its tasks and the ground's `SET_MODE` must restore them. An integration test that only checks "no crash" would pass a system that did none of this.

The summary ends with the number of heap allocations made during the hour, measured with milestone 1's heap watch. It must be 0: the first rule of the project, proven over 36,000 frames.

### How to test it

- the parser: each verb, comments, blank lines, errors with their line numbers, seconds out of range or going down, too many lines;
- `format_event` for each kind of event, and an unknown id;
- the ground station on its own: acknowledgements, housekeeping, gaps;
- `run_hour` quietly (with a null output) on small scenarios, checking the final state;
- and the full hour from standard input, compared line by line.

### Where it is used

- Flight teams run hardware-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop simulations with scripted fault scenarios before launch, and replay real anomalies from orbit on the ground.
- [[Regression testing|golden-transcript]] by comparing whole outputs with approved ones is common in compilers, databases and games, where a behaviour change anywhere shows up as a changed line.
- Chaos engineering at internet companies injects failures on purpose into running systems, the same idea at a larger scale.

**Watch out:** the unit of time. Scenario lines are in **seconds**, the scheduler counts **ticks** of 100 ms. Comparing `second == tick` applies a fault planned for second 600 at second 60, and every response in the transcript arrives ten times too early. Convert once, in one place: an injection is due when `second * 10 == tick`.

::: context sim-time Time that does not pass
The simulated hour takes a few hundredths of a second because nothing in it waits: the scheduler moves from one frame to the next as soon as the tasks return, and each task reports the time it would have taken. Test benches call this running faster than real time. The same flight code can also be run against a real clock, one frame every 100 ms, which is needed when real hardware is in the loop. Designing time as an input, rather than reading a clock deep inside the code, is what makes both possible.
:::

::: context strtok Cutting a line into words
`strtok` from the C library splits a text into tokens in place: it writes a zero byte over each separator and returns a pointer to each word in turn. It keeps its position in a hidden static variable, so two splits cannot be interleaved and it is not safe with threads; `strtok_r` fixes that on POSIX systems. Here, one line is split completely before the next, in a single thread, so plain `strtok` is fine. Because it writes into the text, each line is first copied into a local buffer.
:::

::: context golden-transcript Approving an output once
Golden-output testing, also called snapshot or approval testing, runs a program on a fixed input and compares everything it prints with a stored output that a person has checked and approved. When the output changes, the test fails, and a person decides whether the change is a bug or an improvement to approve. It catches changes nobody thought to write a specific check for. Its weakness is noise: outputs that include times or random numbers must be made deterministic first, which is why everything in this project is seeded and simulated.
:::
--- task
The starter adds the ground's dictionary (`fault_name`, `unit_name`, `task_label`, `opcode_name`, `status_of`, `mode_of`, `response_of`), the scenario types (`Action`, `Injection`, `Scenario`) and two helpers, `find_name` and `parse_int`. Write:

1. `class GroundStation`:
   - `void receive(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t n)`: nothing for null or empty input. Otherwise feed the bytes to its `StreamDecoder` and take out every good packet (at most 512): run its `SequenceTracker` on the APID and count; if the APID is `kHkApid` and `hk_parse` succeeds, keep the report and count it; if the APID is `kAckApid` and the payload is 4 bytes, count an ACK when the status byte (the 4th) is 0 and a NAK otherwise.
   - `Status command(FlightSystem* fs, std::uint8_t opcode, const std::uint8_t* args, std::size_t n, bool garble)`: `BadArg` for a null `fs`. Build the command with its own next sequence count (starting at 0, wrapping at 16384) and time `fs->now_ms()`; if building fails return that; otherwise use up the count, flip the lowest bit of the last byte if `garble`, and return `fs->uplink(...)`.
   - `rx()`, `seq()`, `last_hk()`, `hk_count()`, `acks()`, `naks()`.
2. `int format_event(const Event& e, char* buf, std::size_t cap)`: -1 for a null `buf`; otherwise `snprintf` `"t=<seconds>.<tenths> <what>"` and return its result, where seconds is `time_ms / 1000`, tenths is `(time_ms % 1000) / 100`, and `<what>` depends on the id (U is `unit_name(source)`, T is `task_label(source)`, F is `fault_name(source)`, V is the value as a signed number):

| id | what |
|---|---|
| `kEvLimitNominal`, `kEvLimitYellow`, `kEvLimitRed` | `LIMIT_NOMINAL U value=V`, `LIMIT_YELLOW U value=V`, `LIMIT_RED U value=V` |
| `kEvSensorStuck`, `kEvSensorUnstuck` | `SENSOR_STUCK U raw=V`, `SENSOR_UNSTUCK U raw=V` |
| `kEvFrameOverrun` | `FRAME_OVERRUN used_us=V` |
| `kEvTaskOverrun`, `kEvTaskSkipped` | `TASK_OVERRUN T used_us=V`, `TASK_SKIPPED T` |
| `kEvModeChange` | `MODE <mode_of(source)> -> <mode_of(value)>` |
| `kEvCmdAccepted` | `CMD_OK <opcode_name(source)>` |
| `kEvCmdRejected`, `kEvCmdFailed` | `CMD_REJECTED <opcode_name(source)> <status_of(value)>`, the same with `CMD_FAILED` |
| `kEvFault` | `FAULT F unit=V` |
| `kEvResponse`, `kEvEscalated` | `RESPONSE F <response_of(value)>`, `ESCALATED F <response_of(value)> failed` |
| anything else | `EVENT 0x<id as 4 hex digits in capitals> source=<source> value=V` |

3. `Status parse_line(char* line, Injection* inj)`: cut `line` into words with `std::strtok(…, " \t\r")` (at most 8), and parse one scenario line into `*inj` (cleared first), returning `BadArg` for anything wrong: fewer than 2 words; a second that is not a number from 0 to 3599; an unknown verb, sensor, task, command name or mode; a wrong number of words; a bad number. The forms, and what they set (`second` always):
   - `stuck|dead|clear <SENSOR>`: action `Sensor`, `target` the unit, `fault` `Stuck`, `Dead` or `None`.
   - `bias <SENSOR> <counts>`, `spike <SENSOR> <samples>`: the same with `fault` `Bias` or `Spike` and `a` the number (a spike needs at least 1 sample).
   - `overrun <TASK> <us> <runs>`: action `Overrun`, `target` the task id, `a` the microseconds, `b` the runs (neither negative).
   - `corrupt <n>`, `garble <n>`: action `Corrupt` or `Garble`, `a` = n (not negative).
   - `cmd NOOP`, `cmd RESET_COUNTERS`: action `Command`, `target` the opcode, no arguments.
   - `cmd SET_MODE NOMINAL|SAFE`: one argument byte, the mode's number.
   - `cmd ENABLE_TASK <TASK>`, `cmd DISABLE_TASK <TASK>`: one argument byte, the task id.
   - `cmd CLEAR_FAULT <n>`: one argument byte, n from 0 to 255.
   - `cmd SET_LIMITS <SENSOR> <red_low> <yellow_low> <yellow_high> <red_high>`: 17 argument bytes: the unit, then the four numbers as big-endian `i32`.
   Sensor names are those of `kSensorConfigs`, task names those of `kTaskPlan`.
4. `Status parse_scenario(const char* text, Scenario* sc, std::size_t* bad_line)`: `BadArg` for a null pointer. Set the count and `*bad_line` to 0, then go through the text line by line (lines end at `'\n'`; a last line without one still counts), numbering lines from 1. A line of 160 characters or more is `BadArg`. After leading spaces, tabs and `'\r'`, an empty line or one starting with `#` is skipped. Otherwise, if 64 injections are already held, return `Full`; parse the line into the next injection; if it fails, or its second is less than the previous injection's, return `BadArg`. On any failure, set `*bad_line` to the line's number.
5. `void apply(const Injection& inj, FlightSystem* fs, GroundStation* gs, std::uint32_t* garble_left)`: `Sensor` → `inject_sensor`; `Overrun` → `inject_overrun`; `Corrupt` → `corrupt_downlink`; `Garble` → set `*garble_left` to `a`; `Command` → send it through the ground station, garbled if `*garble_left` is above 0 (and then lower it by one).
6. `Status run_hour(const Scenario& sc, FlightSystem* fs, GroundStation* gs, std::FILE* out)`: `BadArg` for null pointers; `init` the system (return its status on failure); then for each tick from 0 to 35,999: apply, in order, every injection with `second * 10 == tick`; `step`; give the radio bytes to the ground station; and, unless `out` is null, print with `std::fprintf` every event recorded since the last print, oldest first, formatted by `format_event`, one per line. The first frame's print therefore also includes the mode change that `init` recorded. Return `Ok`.
7. `void print_summary(const FlightSystem& fs, const GroundStation& gs, long long heap_used, std::FILE* out)`: prints `--- end of hour ---`, then `hk_format` of `fs.hk()`, then `ground: packets=P crc_errors=C missed=M hk=H acks=A naks=N` (the decoder's packets and CRC errors, the tracker's total missed, and the station's counts), then `heap allocations during the hour: X`, each on its own line.
8. `int mission_main()`: read standard input (up to 8,191 bytes) into a static buffer; parse it into `g_scenario`; if that fails, print `scenario error on line N` and return 1. Otherwise note `heap_allocs()`, run the hour on `g_flight` and `g_ground` with `stdout`, print the summary with the allocations made during the run, and return 0.

The checks run `mission_main` on the scenario in the input box below and compare every line it prints.
--- starter
// ============================================================================
// ORBIT flight software core
// Rules, as on a real spacecraft:
//   - no heap allocation after start-up: fixed-size pools and static arrays
//   - no exceptions, no recursion
//   - every function checks its inputs and returns a status code
// ============================================================================
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// ---- Status codes: the project's whole error vocabulary ---------------------
// The numbers go into acknowledgement packets, so never reorder them.
enum class Status : std::uint8_t {
    Ok = 0,
    NotImpl,      // a stub: not written yet
    BadArg,       // an input is null or out of range
    Full,         // a fixed-capacity container has no room
    Empty,        // nothing to take out
    NotFound,     // no such key, id or handle
    NoSpace,      // an output buffer is too small, or a pool is used up
    Duplicate,    // the same thing twice
    OutOfRange,   // a result does not fit its type
    NotReady,     // called before set-up finished
    TooShort,     // fewer bytes than the format needs
    BadVersion,   // a packet version we do not speak
    BadType,      // the wrong kind of packet
    BadLength,    // a length field that cannot be right
    BadCrc,       // the checksum does not match
    UnknownApid,  // a packet for an application we do not have
    BadOpcode,    // no such command
    BadArgs,      // a command's arguments are wrong
    Forbidden,    // not allowed in the current mode
    Overrun,      // a frame ran out of time
};

const char* status_name(Status s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Status::Ok: return "OK";
        case Status::NotImpl: return "NOT_IMPL";
        case Status::BadArg: return "BAD_ARG";
        case Status::Full: return "FULL";
        case Status::Empty: return "EMPTY";
        case Status::NotFound: return "NOT_FOUND";
        case Status::NoSpace: return "NO_SPACE";
        case Status::Duplicate: return "DUPLICATE";
        case Status::OutOfRange: return "OUT_OF_RANGE";
