        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ (data[i] << 8));
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

// The 256 answers to "what do 8 steps do to this top byte", worked out by
// the compiler, so the table costs nothing at start-up and sits in ROM.
struct CrcTable {
    std::uint16_t entry[256];
};

constexpr CrcTable make_crc_table() {
    CrcTable t{};
    for (int b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
        std::uint16_t crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b << 8);
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
        t.entry[b] = crc;
    }
    return t;
}

constexpr CrcTable kCrcTable = make_crc_table();

// Continues a CRC over more bytes: crc16_update(crc16(a), b) == crc16(a then b).
std::uint16_t crc16_update(std::uint16_t crc, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return crc;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t top = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((crc >> 8) ^ data[i]);
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((crc << 8) ^ kCrcTable.entry[top]);
    }
    return crc;
}

// One table lookup per byte.
std::uint16_t crc16(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return crc16_update(kCrcInit, data, n); }

// ---- The packet format ------------------------------------------------------
//  bytes 0-5   primary header, CCSDS style, big-endian:
//              version:3 | type:1 | secondary header flag:1 | APID:11
//              sequence flags:2 | sequence count:14
//              data length: bytes after the primary header, minus 1
//  bytes 6-9   secondary header: time in milliseconds since boot
//  bytes 10-   payload, 0 to kMaxPayload bytes
//  last 2      CRC-16 of every byte before it
constexpr std::size_t kPrimaryHeaderBytes = 6;
constexpr std::size_t kSecondaryHeaderBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kCrcBytes = 2;
constexpr std::size_t kPacketOverhead = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + kSecondaryHeaderBytes + kCrcBytes;   // 12
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPayload = 96;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacket = kPacketOverhead + kMaxPayload;   // 108
constexpr std::uint16_t kMaxApid = 0x7FF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSeqMask = 0x3FFF;
constexpr std::uint8_t kSeqUnsegmented = 3;

enum class PacketType : std::uint8_t { Telemetry = 0, Command = 1 };

struct PrimaryHeader {
    std::uint8_t version;       // 3 bits; always 0
    PacketType type;            // 1 bit
    bool has_secondary;         // 1 bit
    std::uint16_t apid;         // 11 bits
    std::uint8_t seq_flags;     // 2 bits; 3 means "not split"
    std::uint16_t seq_count;    // 14 bits
    std::uint16_t data_length;  // 16 bits
};

struct Packet {
    PrimaryHeader hdr;
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t payload_len;
    std::uint8_t payload[kMaxPayload];
};

// Packs the six header bytes. BadArg if a field does not fit its bits.
Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w) {
    if (w == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (h.version > 7 || h.apid > kMaxApid || h.seq_flags > 3 || h.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    const std::uint16_t word0 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.version << 13) | (static_cast<unsigned>(h.type) << 12) |
                                                           ((h.has_secondary ? 1u : 0u) << 11) | h.apid);
    const std::uint16_t word1 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.seq_flags << 14) | h.seq_count);
    w->u16(word0);
    w->u16(word1);
    w->u16(h.data_length);
    return w->status();
}

// Unpacks the six header bytes. Checks nothing but that they are there.
Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h) {
    if (r == nullptr || h == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint16_t word0 = 0, word1 = 0, length = 0;
    r->u16(&word0);
    r->u16(&word1);
    r->u16(&length);
    if (!r->ok()) return r->status();
    h->version = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0 >> 13);
    h->type = ((word0 >> 12) & 1u) ? PacketType::Command : PacketType::Telemetry;
    h->has_secondary = ((word0 >> 11) & 1u) != 0;
    h->apid = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word0 & kMaxApid);
    h->seq_flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1 >> 14);
    h->seq_count = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word1 & kSeqMask);
    h->data_length = length;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Writes p as a whole packet: header (data length and the secondary header
// flag worked out here), time, payload and CRC. *written is set only on Ok.
Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (out == nullptr || written == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.hdr.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (p.hdr.apid > kMaxApid || p.hdr.seq_flags > 3 || p.hdr.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.payload_len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    const std::size_t total = kPacketOverhead + p.payload_len;
    if (cap < total) return Status::NoSpace;
    PrimaryHeader h = p.hdr;
    h.has_secondary = true;
    h.data_length = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPrimaryHeaderBytes - 1);
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    const Status s = pack_primary(h, &w);
    if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
    w.u32(p.time_ms);
    w.bytes(p.payload, p.payload_len);
    w.u16(crc16(out, w.size()));
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Builds packets and numbers them: each APID has its own 14-bit sequence
// count, which starts at 0 and wraps from 16383 back to 0.
class PacketEncoder {
public:
    Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len,
                 std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
        if ((payload == nullptr && len > 0) || apid > kMaxApid) return Status::BadArg;
        if (len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        const std::uint16_t seq = found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
        if (found == nullptr && seq_.size() == seq_.capacity()) return Status::Full;
        Packet p{};
        p.hdr = {0, type, true, apid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
        p.time_ms = time_ms;
        p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        if (len > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload, payload, len);
        const Status s = encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        seq_.put(apid, static_cast<std::uint16_t>((seq + 1) & kSeqMask));   // only a sent packet uses a number
        ++built_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The count the next packet on apid will carry.
    std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const {
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        return found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
    }

    // Sets the next count for apid (ground tools use it to replay a pass).
    Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq) {
        if (apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        return seq_.put(apid, seq);
    }

    std::uint32_t packets_built() const { return built_; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> seq_;
    std::uint32_t built_ = 0;
};

// ---- Decoding: trust nothing that came over the radio -----------------------
// Checks in this order, and stops at the first failure:
//   null pointer -> BadArg; under 6 bytes -> TooShort; version -> BadVersion;
//   no secondary header -> BadType; length field too small or payload too
//   big -> BadLength; fewer bytes than the length says -> TooShort;
//   CRC -> BadCrc. On any failure *out and *consumed are left alone.
Status decode_packet(const std::uint8_t* in, std::size_t len, Packet* out, std::size_t* consumed) {
    if (in == nullptr || out == nullptr || consumed == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (len < kPrimaryHeaderBytes) return Status::TooShort;
    ByteReader r(in, len);
    PrimaryHeader h;
    unpack_primary(&r, &h);
    if (h.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (!h.has_secondary) return Status::BadType;
    const std::size_t total = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + static_cast<std::size_t>(h.data_length) + 1;
    if (total < kPacketOverhead || total - kPacketOverhead > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    if (len < total) return Status::TooShort;
    const std::uint16_t stored = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((in[total - 2] << 8) | in[total - 1]);
    if (crc16(in, total - kCrcBytes) != stored) return Status::BadCrc;
    out->hdr = h;
    r.u32(&out->time_ms);
    out->payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPacketOverhead);
    r.bytes(out->payload, out->payload_len);
    *consumed = total;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// ---- Framing: packets on a byte stream, each after a sync marker ------------
constexpr std::uint8_t kSyncMarker[4] = {0x1A, 0xCF, 0xFC, 0x1D};
constexpr std::size_t kSyncBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kStreamBufferBytes = 512;

// Writes the sync marker and then the packet's bytes.
Status frame_packet(const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (pkt == nullptr || out == nullptr || written == nullptr || len == 0) return Status::BadArg;
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    w.bytes(kSyncMarker, kSyncBytes);
    w.bytes(pkt, len);
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Pulls whole packets out of a stream that may hold noise, cut packets and
// corrupted packets. Bytes that are not part of a good packet are skipped
// and counted; the decoder never gives up and never waits on garbage.
class StreamDecoder {
public:
    // Appends bytes. Full if they do not all fit: then nothing is appended.
    Status feed(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
        if (data == nullptr && n > 0) return Status::BadArg;
        if (n > kStreamBufferBytes - len_) return Status::Full;
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, data, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Ok: *out holds the next good packet. Empty: no whole packet yet.
    Status next(Packet* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        for (std::size_t guard = 0; guard <= kStreamBufferBytes; ++guard) {   // each pass drops at least 1 byte or returns
            const std::size_t at = find_sync();
            if (at == len_) {
                // No marker. Keep the last 3 bytes: they may be the start of one.
                const std::size_t keep = len_ < kSyncBytes - 1 ? len_ : kSyncBytes - 1;
                drop(len_ - keep);
                return Status::Empty;
            }
            drop(at);
            if (len_ < kSyncBytes + kPrimaryHeaderBytes) return Status::Empty;
            std::size_t used = 0;
            const Status s = decode_packet(buf_ + kSyncBytes, len_ - kSyncBytes, out, &used);
            if (s == Status::Ok) {
                drop_good(kSyncBytes + used);
                ++packets_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            if (s == Status::TooShort) return Status::Empty;   // wait for the rest
            if (s == Status::BadCrc) ++crc_errors_; else ++bad_headers_;
            drop(1);   // step past this marker and look for the next
        }
        return Status::Empty;
    }

    std::uint32_t packets() const { return packets_; }
    std::uint32_t crc_errors() const { return crc_errors_; }
    std::uint32_t bad_headers() const { return bad_headers_; }
    std::uint32_t bytes_skipped() const { return skipped_; }
    std::size_t buffered() const { return len_; }

private:
    std::size_t find_sync() const {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i + kSyncBytes <= len_; ++i) {
            if (std::memcmp(buf_ + i, kSyncMarker, kSyncBytes) == 0) return i;
        }
        return len_;
    }
    void drop(std::size_t n) {
        skipped_ += static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n);
        drop_good(n);
    }
    void drop_good(std::size_t n) {
        std::memmove(buf_, buf_ + n, len_ - n);
        len_ -= n;
    }

    std::uint8_t buf_[kStreamBufferBytes] = {};
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t packets_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t crc_errors_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t bad_headers_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t skipped_ = 0;
};

// ---- Sequence tracking: which packets never arrived -------------------------
class SequenceTracker {
public:
    // Records a packet. *missed is how many counts were skipped since the
    // last packet on this APID (mod 16384); the first packet misses none.
    // The same count twice in a row is Duplicate, and counts as no loss.
    Status observe(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq, std::uint16_t* missed) {
        if (missed == nullptr || apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        std::uint16_t* last = last_.find(apid);
        if (last == nullptr) {
            const Status s = last_.put(apid, seq);
            if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
            *missed = 0;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        if (seq == *last) {
            *missed = 0;
            ++duplicates_;
            return Status::Duplicate;
        }
        *missed = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((seq - *last - 1) & kSeqMask);
        total_missed_ += *missed;
        *last = seq;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::uint32_t total_missed() const { return total_missed_; }
    std::uint32_t duplicates() const { return duplicates_; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> last_;
    std::uint32_t total_missed_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t duplicates_ = 0;
};

// ---- Calibration: raw ADC counts to engineering units -----------------------
// Engineering values are whole numbers of milli-units (millivolts,
// millidegrees...), so every machine computes exactly the same bits.
struct Calibration {
    std::int32_t offset_milli;   // the value at raw 0
    std::int32_t gain_num;       // milli-units per count, as a fraction
    std::int32_t gain_den;
};

// value = offset + raw * num / den, in 64-bit, the division truncating
// toward zero. BadArg if den <= 0 or out is null; OutOfRange if the value
// does not fit in 32 bits (then *out is left alone).
Status calibrate(std::uint16_t raw, const Calibration& cal, std::int32_t* out) {
    if (out == nullptr || cal.gain_den <= 0) return Status::BadArg;
    const std::int64_t v = static_cast<std::int64_t>(cal.offset_milli) +
                           static_cast<std::int64_t>(raw) * cal.gain_num / cal.gain_den;
    if (v < INT32_MIN || v > INT32_MAX) return Status::OutOfRange;
    *out = static_cast<std::int32_t>(v);
    return Status::Ok;
}

// ---- Filters ----------------------------------------------------------------
// The mean of the last N values, kept as a running sum: O(1) a sample.
template <std::size_t N>
class MovingAverage {
public:
    // Adds v and returns the mean of the values in the window, truncated
    // toward zero. The window holds fewer than N values until N have come.
    std::int32_t push(std::int32_t v) {
        if (window_.full()) {
            std::int32_t oldest = 0;
            window_.pop(&oldest);
            sum_ -= oldest;
        }
        window_.push(v);
        sum_ += v;
        return static_cast<std::int32_t>(sum_ / static_cast<std::int64_t>(window_.size()));
    }
    std::size_t count() const { return window_.size(); }
    void reset() {
        window_.clear();
        sum_ = 0;
    }

private:
    RingBuffer<std::int32_t, N> window_;
    std::int64_t sum_ = 0;   // 64 bits: N values of up to 2^31 each cannot overflow it
};

// The median of the last three values: one wild sample never gets through.
class Median3 {
public:
    std::int32_t push(std::int32_t v) {
        a_ = b_;
        b_ = c_;
        c_ = v;
        if (seen_ < 3) ++seen_;
        if (seen_ < 3) return v;   // not enough history yet
        const std::int32_t lo = a_ < b_ ? a_ : b_;
        const std::int32_t hi = a_ < b_ ? b_ : a_;
        return c_ < lo ? lo : (c_ > hi ? hi : c_);
    }
    void reset() { a_ = b_ = c_ = 0; seen_ = 0; }

private:
    std::int32_t a_ = 0, b_ = 0, c_ = 0;   // oldest to newest
    int seen_ = 0;
};

// ---- A simulated sensor, with faults that can be injected -------------------
// A 12-bit ADC: raw values 0 to 4095. Noise comes from a seeded generator,
// so a run is the same every time.
constexpr std::uint16_t kAdcMax = 4095;

enum class SensorFault : std::uint8_t { None, Stuck, Bias, Spike, Dead };

class SimSensor {
public:
    Status configure(std::uint16_t base, std::uint16_t noise, std::uint32_t seed) {
        if (base > kAdcMax || noise > 512) return Status::BadArg;
        base_ = base;
        noise_ = noise;
        state_ = seed;
        fault_ = SensorFault::None;
        last_ = base;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The next raw sample.
    std::uint16_t read() {
        state_ = state_ * 1664525u + 1013904223u;   // a linear congruential generator
        const std::int32_t span = 2 * noise_ + 1;
        std::int32_t v = base_ + static_cast<std::int32_t>((state_ >> 16) % static_cast<std::uint32_t>(span)) - noise_;
        switch (fault_) {
            case SensorFault::None: break;
            case SensorFault::Stuck: return last_;   // frozen at the last good value
            case SensorFault::Bias: v += param_; break;
            case SensorFault::Spike:
                if (param_ > 0) {
                    --param_;
                    if (param_ == 0) fault_ = SensorFault::None;
                    return kAdcMax;
                }
                break;
            case SensorFault::Dead: return 0;
        }
        last_ = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(v < 0 ? 0 : (v > kAdcMax ? kAdcMax : v));
        return last_;
    }

    // Stuck: frozen at the last value read. Bias: adds param counts.
    // Spike: the next param samples read 4095. Dead: reads 0.
    Status inject(SensorFault f, std::int32_t param) {
        if (f == SensorFault::Spike && param <= 0) return Status::BadArg;
        fault_ = f;
        param_ = param;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    void clear_fault() { fault_ = SensorFault::None; }
    SensorFault fault() const { return fault_; }
    void set_base(std::uint16_t base) { base_ = base > kAdcMax ? kAdcMax : base; }

private:
    std::int32_t base_ = 0;
    std::int32_t noise_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t state_ = 1;
    SensorFault fault_ = SensorFault::None;
    std::int32_t param_ = 0;
    std::uint16_t last_ = 0;
};

// ---- A sensor channel: read, calibrate, then filter -------------------------
struct SensorConfig {
    const char* name;
    std::uint16_t id;
    Calibration cal;
    std::uint16_t base_raw;
    std::uint16_t noise_raw;
    std::uint32_t seed;
};

class SensorChannel {
public:
    Status configure(const SensorConfig& cfg) {
        if (cfg.name == nullptr || cfg.cal.gain_den <= 0) return Status::BadArg;
        const Status s = sim_.configure(cfg.base_raw, cfg.noise_raw, cfg.seed);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        cfg_ = cfg;
        median_.reset();
        average_.reset();
        samples_ = 0;
        errors_ = 0;
        ready_ = true;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // One sample: raw -> calibrated -> median of 3 -> mean of 8.
    Status sample(std::int32_t* filtered_out) {
        if (!ready_) return Status::NotReady;
        last_raw_ = sim_.read();
        std::int32_t v = 0;
        const Status s = calibrate(last_raw_, cfg_.cal, &v);
        if (s != Status::Ok) {
            ++errors_;
            return s;
        }
        last_value_ = v;
        filtered_ = average_.push(median_.push(v));
        ++samples_;
        if (filtered_out != nullptr) *filtered_out = filtered_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    const char* name() const { return ready_ ? cfg_.name : "?"; }
    std::uint16_t id() const { return cfg_.id; }
    std::uint16_t last_raw() const { return last_raw_; }
    std::int32_t last_value() const { return last_value_; }
    std::int32_t filtered() const { return filtered_; }
    std::uint32_t samples() const { return samples_; }
    std::uint32_t errors() const { return errors_; }
    SimSensor& sim() { return sim_; }

private:
    SensorConfig cfg_ = {};
    SimSensor sim_;
    Median3 median_;
    MovingAverage<8> average_;
    std::uint16_t last_raw_ = 0;
    std::int32_t last_value_ = 0;
    std::int32_t filtered_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t samples_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t errors_ = 0;
    bool ready_ = false;
};

// ---- Events: what happened, when, and to what -------------------------------
// The flight side stores numbers only; the ground turns ids into words.
struct Event {
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t id;
    std::uint16_t source;   // the sensor, task or unit it is about
    std::int32_t value;
};

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvLimitNominal = 0x0101;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvLimitYellow = 0x0102;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvLimitRed = 0x0103;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvSensorStuck = 0x0104;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvSensorUnstuck = 0x0105;

// The newest 64 events. When full, the oldest is dropped: the latest
// history matters most, and logging must never fail or block.
class EventLog {
public:
    void record(std::uint32_t time_ms, std::uint16_t id, std::uint16_t source, std::int32_t value) {
        ring_.push_overwrite({time_ms, id, source, value});
        ++total_;
    }
    // The i-th oldest event still held.
    Status at(std::size_t i, Event* out) const { return ring_.at(i, out); }
    std::size_t size() const { return ring_.size(); }
    std::uint32_t total() const { return total_; }        // every event ever recorded
    std::uint32_t lost() const { return ring_.dropped(); }
    // How many held events have this id.
    std::size_t count(std::uint16_t id) const {
        std::size_t n = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ring_.size(); ++i) {
            Event e;
            if (ring_.at(i, &e) == Status::Ok && e.id == id) ++n;
        }
        return n;
    }

private:
    RingBuffer<Event, 64> ring_;
    std::uint32_t total_ = 0;
};

// ---- Limits -----------------------------------------------------------------
struct Limits {
    std::int32_t red_low;
    std::int32_t yellow_low;
    std::int32_t yellow_high;
    std::int32_t red_high;
};

bool limits_valid(const Limits& l) {
    return l.red_low <= l.yellow_low && l.yellow_low <= l.yellow_high && l.yellow_high <= l.red_high;
}

enum class LimitState : std::uint8_t { Nominal, YellowLow, YellowHigh, RedLow, RedHigh };

const char* limit_state_name(LimitState s) {
    switch (s) {
        case LimitState::Nominal: return "NOMINAL";
        case LimitState::YellowLow: return "YELLOW_LOW";
        case LimitState::YellowHigh: return "YELLOW_HIGH";
        case LimitState::RedLow: return "RED_LOW";
        case LimitState::RedHigh: return "RED_HIGH";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// A value equal to a limit is still inside it.
LimitState classify(std::int32_t v, const Limits& l) {
    if (v < l.red_low) return LimitState::RedLow;
    if (v > l.red_high) return LimitState::RedHigh;
    if (v < l.yellow_low) return LimitState::YellowLow;
    if (v > l.yellow_high) return LimitState::YellowHigh;
    return LimitState::Nominal;
}

bool is_red(LimitState s) { return s == LimitState::RedLow || s == LimitState::RedHigh; }

// ---- A limit monitor with persistence ---------------------------------------
// One noisy sample must not raise an alarm, and one good sample must not
// clear it. Three run counters, each "samples in a row":
//   red_run      samples in red (either side)
//   yellow_run   samples outside yellow, red included
//   nominal_run  samples inside yellow
// After each sample the reported state becomes, in this order of priority:
//   red (the side of this sample)    if red_run     >= set_count
//   yellow (the side of this sample) if yellow_run  >= set_count
//   Nominal                          if nominal_run >= clear_count
//   otherwise it stays as it was.
class LimitMonitor {
public:
    Status configure(const Limits& l, std::uint8_t set_count, std::uint8_t clear_count) {
        if (!limits_valid(l) || set_count == 0 || clear_count == 0) return Status::BadArg;
        limits_ = l;
        set_count_ = set_count;
        clear_count_ = clear_count;
        red_run_ = yellow_run_ = nominal_run_ = 0;
        state_ = LimitState::Nominal;
        ready_ = true;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // New limits from the ground: the runs start again, the state is kept.
    Status set_limits(const Limits& l) {
        if (!ready_) return Status::NotReady;
        if (!limits_valid(l)) return Status::BadArg;
        limits_ = l;
        red_run_ = yellow_run_ = nominal_run_ = 0;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Feeds one value. *changed says whether the reported state changed.
    Status update(std::int32_t value, bool* changed) {
        if (changed == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        *changed = false;
        if (!ready_) return Status::NotReady;
        if (!enabled_) return Status::Ok;
        const LimitState raw = classify(value, limits_);
        red_run_ = is_red(raw) ? bump(red_run_) : 0;
        yellow_run_ = raw != LimitState::Nominal ? bump(yellow_run_) : 0;
        nominal_run_ = raw == LimitState::Nominal ? bump(nominal_run_) : 0;
        const bool high = value > limits_.yellow_high;
        LimitState next = state_;
        if (red_run_ >= set_count_) next = high ? LimitState::RedHigh : LimitState::RedLow;
        else if (yellow_run_ >= set_count_) next = high ? LimitState::YellowHigh : LimitState::YellowLow;
        else if (nominal_run_ >= clear_count_) next = LimitState::Nominal;
        if (next != state_) {
            state_ = next;
            *changed = true;
        }
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // A disabled monitor ignores values and reports Nominal from then on.
    void enable(bool on) {
        enabled_ = on;
        if (!on) {
            state_ = LimitState::Nominal;
            red_run_ = yellow_run_ = nominal_run_ = 0;
        }
    }
    bool enabled() const { return enabled_; }
    LimitState state() const { return state_; }
    const Limits& limits() const { return limits_; }

private:
    static std::uint8_t bump(std::uint8_t n) { return n == 255 ? n : static_cast<std::uint8_t>(n + 1); }   // saturate

    Limits limits_ = {};
    std::uint8_t set_count_ = 1;
    std::uint8_t clear_count_ = 1;
    std::uint8_t red_run_ = 0;
    std::uint8_t yellow_run_ = 0;
    std::uint8_t nominal_run_ = 0;
    LimitState state_ = LimitState::Nominal;
    bool enabled_ = true;
    bool ready_ = false;
};

// ---- A stuck-sensor monitor -------------------------------------------------
// Real noise moves the last bits of an ADC all the time. The same raw value
// `window` times in a row means the sensor has frozen.
class StuckMonitor {
public:
    Status configure(std::uint16_t window) {
        if (window < 2) return Status::BadArg;
        window_ = window;
        run_ = 0;
        stuck_ = false;
        ready_ = true;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // *became_stuck is true only on the sample that makes it stuck;
    // *came_back only on the first different value after that.
    Status update(std::uint16_t raw, bool* became_stuck, bool* came_back) {
        if (became_stuck == nullptr || came_back == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        *became_stuck = false;
        *came_back = false;
        if (!ready_) return Status::NotReady;
        if (run_ > 0 && raw == last_) {
            if (run_ < window_) ++run_;
        } else {
            run_ = 1;
            if (stuck_) {
                stuck_ = false;
                *came_back = true;
            }
        }
        last_ = raw;
        if (!stuck_ && run_ >= window_) {
            stuck_ = true;
            *became_stuck = true;
        }
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    bool stuck() const { return stuck_; }

private:
    std::uint16_t window_ = 2;
    std::uint16_t run_ = 0;
    std::uint16_t last_ = 0;
    bool stuck_ = false;
    bool ready_ = false;
};

// ---- The cyclic executive ---------------------------------------------------
// Time is cut into minor frames of 100 ms (10 Hz); 10 minor frames make a
// major frame of 1 s, after which the pattern repeats. A task runs every
// `period` minor frames (1, 2, 5 or 10), in frames where
// tick % period == offset. Inside a frame, tasks run in rate-monotonic
// order: the shorter the period, the higher the priority; equal periods run
// in the order they were added.
constexpr std::uint32_t kMinorFrameUs = 100000;
constexpr std::uint8_t kFramesPerMajor = 10;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxTasks = 16;

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvFrameOverrun = 0x0201;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvTaskOverrun = 0x0202;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvTaskSkipped = 0x0203;

// A task does its work and returns the microseconds it used. In this
// simulation the number is the task's own report; on a real board the
// executive would read a hardware timer.
using TaskFn = std::uint32_t (*)(void* ctx, std::uint32_t tick);

struct TaskSpec {
    const char* name;
    TaskFn fn;
    void* ctx;
    std::uint8_t period;
    std::uint8_t offset;
    std::uint32_t budget_us;   // the most time it may take
    bool essential;            // still runs in safe mode
};

struct TaskStats {
    std::uint32_t runs;
    std::uint32_t skips;            // not started: its budget no longer fitted
    std::uint32_t budget_overruns;  // ran longer than its budget
    std::uint32_t max_us;
    bool enabled;
};

bool valid_period(std::uint8_t p) { return p == 1 || p == 2 || p == 5 || p == 10; }

class Scheduler {
public:
    void attach_log(EventLog* log) { log_ = log; }

    // Registers a task; *id gets its number (0, 1, 2 ... in the order added).
    Status add(const TaskSpec& t, std::uint8_t* id) {
        if (id == nullptr || t.name == nullptr || t.fn == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (!valid_period(t.period) || t.offset >= t.period) return Status::BadArg;
        if (t.budget_us == 0 || t.budget_us > kMinorFrameUs) return Status::BadArg;
        if (built_) return Status::Forbidden;   // the schedule is fixed once built
        if (count_ == kMaxTasks) return Status::Full;
        tasks_[count_] = t;
        stats_[count_] = {0, 0, 0, 0, true};
        *id = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(count_);
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Builds the frame tables and proves them: in every minor frame, the
    // budgets of the tasks due must add up to at most kMinorFrameUs.
    // Overrun (and nothing built) if a frame is overbooked.
    Status build() {
        if (built_) return Status::Ok;
        // Priority order: a stable insertion sort of the ids by period.
        std::uint8_t order[kMaxTasks];
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            std::size_t j = i;
            while (j > 0 && tasks_[order[j - 1]].period > tasks_[i].period) {
                order[j] = order[j - 1];
                --j;
            }
            order[j] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i);
        }
        std::uint8_t table[kFramesPerMajor][kMaxTasks];
        std::uint8_t lens[kFramesPerMajor] = {};
        for (std::uint8_t f = 0; f < kFramesPerMajor; ++f) {
            std::uint32_t booked = 0;
            for (std::size_t k = 0; k < count_; ++k) {
                const TaskSpec& t = tasks_[order[k]];
                if (f % t.period != t.offset) continue;
                booked += t.budget_us;
                table[f][lens[f]++] = order[k];
            }
            if (booked > kMinorFrameUs) return Status::Overrun;
        }
        std::memcpy(table_, table, sizeof table_);
        std::memcpy(lens_, lens, sizeof lens_);
        built_ = true;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Runs the tasks due in this minor frame, highest priority first.
    // Before starting a task, its whole budget must still fit in the frame;
    // if not, it is skipped this time. Returns Overrun if the frame used
    // more than kMinorFrameUs in the end, else Ok.
    Status run_frame() {
        if (!built_) return Status::NotReady;
        const std::uint8_t f = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(tick_ % kFramesPerMajor);
        const std::uint32_t now_ms = tick_ * (kMinorFrameUs / 1000);
        std::uint32_t used = 0;
        for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k < lens_[f]; ++k) {
            const std::uint8_t id = table_[f][k];
            const TaskSpec& t = tasks_[id];
            TaskStats& st = stats_[id];
            if (!st.enabled) continue;
            if (used + t.budget_us > kMinorFrameUs) {
                ++st.skips;
                if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvTaskSkipped, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(used));
                continue;
            }
            const std::uint32_t us = t.fn(t.ctx, tick_);
            ++st.runs;
            if (us > st.max_us) st.max_us = us;
            if (us > t.budget_us) {
                ++st.budget_overruns;
                if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvTaskOverrun, id, static_cast<std::int32_t>(us));
            }
            used += us;
        }
        last_frame_us_ = used;
        ++tick_;
        if (used > kMinorFrameUs) {
            ++frame_overruns_;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvFrameOverrun, 0, static_cast<std::int32_t>(used));
            return Status::Overrun;
        }
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Status set_enabled(std::uint8_t id, bool on) {
        if (id >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        stats_[id].enabled = on;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Status find(const char* name, std::uint8_t* id) const {
        if (name == nullptr || id == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            if (std::strcmp(tasks_[i].name, name) == 0) {
                *id = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i);
                return Status::Ok;
            }
        }
        return Status::NotFound;
    }

    // Safe mode: only essential tasks keep running.
    void shed_nonessential() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) {
            if (!tasks_[i].essential) stats_[i].enabled = false;
        }
    }
    void enable_all() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count_; ++i) stats_[i].enabled = true;
    }

    // The ids due in minor frame f, in the order they run; returns how many.
    std::uint8_t frame_tasks(std::uint8_t f, std::uint8_t* ids, std::uint8_t max) const {
        if (!built_ || f >= kFramesPerMajor || ids == nullptr) return 0;
        std::uint8_t n = 0;
        for (std::uint8_t k = 0; k < lens_[f] && n < max; ++k) ids[n++] = table_[f][k];
        return n;
    }

    const TaskStats* stats(std::uint8_t id) const { return id < count_ ? &stats_[id] : nullptr; }
    const char* task_name(std::uint8_t id) const { return id < count_ ? tasks_[id].name : "?"; }
    std::size_t task_count() const { return count_; }
    std::uint32_t tick() const { return tick_; }
    std::uint32_t frame_overruns() const { return frame_overruns_; }
    std::uint32_t last_frame_us() const { return last_frame_us_; }
    bool built() const { return built_; }

private:
    TaskSpec tasks_[kMaxTasks] = {};
    TaskStats stats_[kMaxTasks] = {};
    std::size_t count_ = 0;
    std::uint8_t table_[kFramesPerMajor][kMaxTasks] = {};
    std::uint8_t lens_[kFramesPerMajor] = {};
    bool built_ = false;
    std::uint32_t tick_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t frame_overruns_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t last_frame_us_ = 0;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
};

// ---- Modes ------------------------------------------------------------------
enum class Mode : std::uint8_t { Boot = 0, Nominal = 1, Safe = 2 };

const char* mode_name(Mode m) {
    switch (m) {
        case Mode::Boot: return "BOOT";
        case Mode::Nominal: return "NOMINAL";
        case Mode::Safe: return "SAFE";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvModeChange = 0x0301;

using ModeListener = void (*)(void* ctx, Mode from, Mode to);

// Legal moves: Boot -> Nominal, Boot -> Safe, Nominal -> Safe, Safe -> Nominal.
// Nothing goes back to Boot. Asking for the mode you are in is Ok and
// changes nothing.
class ModeManager {
public:
    void attach_log(EventLog* log) { log_ = log; }
    void listen(ModeListener fn, void* ctx) {
        listener_ = fn;
        listener_ctx_ = ctx;
    }

    Status request(Mode to, std::uint32_t now_ms) {
        if (to != Mode::Boot && to != Mode::Nominal && to != Mode::Safe) return Status::BadArg;
        if (to == mode_) return Status::Ok;
        if (to == Mode::Boot) return Status::Forbidden;
        const Mode from = mode_;
        mode_ = to;
        entered_ms_ = now_ms;
        ++transitions_;
        if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvModeChange, static_cast<std::uint16_t>(from), static_cast<std::int32_t>(to));
        if (listener_ != nullptr) listener_(listener_ctx_, from, to);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    Mode mode() const { return mode_; }
    std::uint32_t entered_ms() const { return entered_ms_; }
    std::uint32_t transitions() const { return transitions_; }

private:
    Mode mode_ = Mode::Boot;
    std::uint32_t entered_ms_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t transitions_ = 0;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
    ModeListener listener_ = nullptr;
    void* listener_ctx_ = nullptr;
};

// ---- Commands ---------------------------------------------------------------
// A command is a Command-type packet to kCommandApid whose payload is one
// opcode byte followed by exactly that command's argument bytes.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCommandApid = 0x010;
constexpr std::uint16_t kAckApid = 0x011;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxCommands = 32;

constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdAccepted = 0x0302;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdRejected = 0x0303;
constexpr std::uint16_t kEvCmdFailed = 0x0304;

using CommandFn = Status (*)(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t now_ms);

struct CommandDef {
    std::uint8_t opcode;
    const char* name;
    std::uint8_t arg_bytes;
    bool allowed_in_safe;
    CommandFn fn;
    void* ctx;
};

// What the ground hears back about one command.
struct Ack {
    std::uint16_t seq;      // the command packet's sequence count
    std::uint8_t opcode;    // 0 if it never got that far
    Status status;
};

class CommandHandler {
public:
    void attach(ModeManager* modes, EventLog* log) {
        modes_ = modes;
        log_ = log;
    }

    Status add(const CommandDef& def) {
        if (def.name == nullptr || def.fn == nullptr || def.arg_bytes > kMaxPayload - 1) return Status::BadArg;
        if (table_.contains(def.opcode)) return Status::Duplicate;
        return table_.put(def.opcode, def);
    }

    // Decodes, validates and runs one command, in this order:
    //   decode (its status) -> Command type (BadType) -> APID (UnknownApid)
    //   -> an opcode byte (BadArgs) -> known opcode (BadOpcode)
    //   -> exact argument length (BadArgs) -> allowed in this mode (Forbidden)
    //   -> run it. The ack always says how far it got.
    Status handle(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len, std::uint32_t now_ms, Ack* ack) {
        if (bytes == nullptr || ack == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        *ack = {0, 0, Status::Ok};
        Packet p;
        std::size_t used = 0;
        Status s = decode_packet(bytes, len, &p, &used);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            ack->seq = p.hdr.seq_count;
            if (p.hdr.type != PacketType::Command) s = Status::BadType;
            else if (p.hdr.apid != kCommandApid) s = Status::UnknownApid;
            else if (p.payload_len < 1) s = Status::BadArgs;
        }
        const CommandDef* def = nullptr;
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            ack->opcode = p.payload[0];
            def = table_.find(p.payload[0]);
            if (def == nullptr) s = Status::BadOpcode;
            else if (p.payload_len - 1u != def->arg_bytes) s = Status::BadArgs;
            else if (modes_ != nullptr && modes_->mode() == Mode::Safe && !def->allowed_in_safe) s = Status::Forbidden;
        }
        if (s != Status::Ok) {
            ++rejected_;
            ack->status = s;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdRejected, ack->opcode, static_cast<std::int32_t>(s));
            return s;
        }
        ++accepted_;
        ByteReader args(p.payload + 1, def->arg_bytes);
        s = def->fn(def->ctx, &args, now_ms);
        ack->status = s;
        if (s != Status::Ok) {
            ++failed_;
            if (log_ != nullptr) log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdFailed, def->opcode, static_cast<std::int32_t>(s));
        } else if (log_ != nullptr) {
            log_->record(now_ms, kEvCmdAccepted, def->opcode, 0);
        }
        return s;
    }

    void reset_counters() { accepted_ = rejected_ = failed_ = 0; }
    std::uint32_t accepted() const { return accepted_; }   // passed every check
    std::uint32_t rejected() const { return rejected_; }   // failed a check
    std::uint32_t failed() const { return failed_; }       // accepted, but running it failed
    const CommandDef* lookup(std::uint8_t opcode) const { return table_.find(opcode); }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint8_t, CommandDef, kMaxCommands> table_;
    ModeManager* modes_ = nullptr;
    EventLog* log_ = nullptr;
    std::uint32_t accepted_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t rejected_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t failed_ = 0;
};

// The ack packet's payload: seq (2 bytes), opcode, status code.
Status encode_ack(const Ack& ack, PacketEncoder* enc, std::uint32_t now_ms, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (enc == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t payload[4];
    ByteWriter w(payload, sizeof payload);
    w.u16(ack.seq);
    w.u8(ack.opcode);
    w.u8(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ack.status));
    return enc->build(PacketType::Telemetry, kAckApid, now_ms, payload, w.size(), out, cap, written);
}

// Ground side: a command packet with the given sequence count.
Status build_command(std::uint16_t seq, std::uint8_t opcode, const std::uint8_t* args, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t time_ms,
                     std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if ((args == nullptr && n > 0) || n > kMaxPayload - 1 || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    Packet p{};
    p.hdr = {0, PacketType::Command, true, kCommandApid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
    p.time_ms = time_ms;
    p.payload[0] = opcode;
    if (n > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload + 1, args, n);
    p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(n + 1);
    return encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
}

// ---- The standard commands ----------------------------------------------------
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpNoop = 0x01;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpSetMode = 0x02;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpResetCounters = 0x03;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpSetLimits = 0x04;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpEnableTask = 0x05;
constexpr std::uint8_t kOpDisableTask = 0x06;

Status cmd_noop(void*, ByteReader*, std::uint32_t) { return Status::Ok; }

// One byte: the mode wanted (0, 1 or 2). ctx: the ModeManager.
Status cmd_set_mode(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t now_ms) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t m = 0;
    if (args->u8(&m) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    if (m > 2) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<ModeManager*>(ctx)->request(static_cast<Mode>(m), now_ms);
}

// No bytes. ctx: the CommandHandler whose counters go back to 0.
Status cmd_reset_counters(void* ctx, ByteReader*, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    static_cast<CommandHandler*>(ctx)->reset_counters();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// The monitors a SET_LIMITS command can reach.
struct MonitorBank {
    LimitMonitor* monitors;
    std::uint8_t count;
};

// 17 bytes: monitor index, then red_low, yellow_low, yellow_high, red_high
// as big-endian int32. ctx: a MonitorBank.
Status cmd_set_limits(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    const MonitorBank* bank = static_cast<const MonitorBank*>(ctx);
    std::uint8_t which = 0;
    Limits l{};
    args->u8(&which);
    args->i32(&l.red_low);
    args->i32(&l.yellow_low);
    args->i32(&l.yellow_high);
    args->i32(&l.red_high);
    if (!args->ok()) return Status::BadArgs;
    if (which >= bank->count) return Status::NotFound;
    if (!limits_valid(l)) return Status::BadArgs;
    return bank->monitors[which].set_limits(l);
}

// One byte: the task id. ctx: the Scheduler.
Status cmd_enable_task(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t id = 0;
    if (args->u8(&id) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<Scheduler*>(ctx)->set_enabled(id, true);
}

Status cmd_disable_task(void* ctx, ByteReader* args, std::uint32_t) {
    if (ctx == nullptr || args == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint8_t id = 0;
    if (args->u8(&id) != Status::Ok) return Status::BadArgs;
    return static_cast<Scheduler*>(ctx)->set_enabled(id, false);
}

// ---- Time-tagged commands ---------------------------------------------------
constexpr std::size_t kTimedSlots = 16;

class TimedQueue {
public:
    Status schedule(std::uint32_t at_ms, const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, std::uint32_t now_ms) { return Status::NotImpl; }
    std::size_t release(std::uint32_t now_ms, CommandHandler* h, Ack* acks, std::size_t max) { return 0; }
    std::size_t size() const { return 0; }
    Status next_time(std::uint32_t* at_ms) const { return Status::NotImpl; }
};
--- solution
// ============================================================================
// ORBIT flight software core
// Rules, as on a real spacecraft:
//   - no heap allocation after start-up: fixed-size pools and static arrays
//   - no exceptions, no recursion
//   - every function checks its inputs and returns a status code
// ============================================================================
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

// ---- Status codes: the project's whole error vocabulary ---------------------
// The numbers go into acknowledgement packets, so never reorder them.
enum class Status : std::uint8_t {
    Ok = 0,
    NotImpl,      // a stub: not written yet
    BadArg,       // an input is null or out of range
    Full,         // a fixed-capacity container has no room
    Empty,        // nothing to take out
    NotFound,     // no such key, id or handle
    NoSpace,      // an output buffer is too small, or a pool is used up
    Duplicate,    // the same thing twice
    OutOfRange,   // a result does not fit its type
    NotReady,     // called before set-up finished
    TooShort,     // fewer bytes than the format needs
    BadVersion,   // a packet version we do not speak
    BadType,      // the wrong kind of packet
    BadLength,    // a length field that cannot be right
    BadCrc,       // the checksum does not match
    UnknownApid,  // a packet for an application we do not have
    BadOpcode,    // no such command
    BadArgs,      // a command's arguments are wrong
    Forbidden,    // not allowed in the current mode
    Overrun,      // a frame ran out of time
};

const char* status_name(Status s) {
    switch (s) {
        case Status::Ok: return "OK";
        case Status::NotImpl: return "NOT_IMPL";
        case Status::BadArg: return "BAD_ARG";
        case Status::Full: return "FULL";
        case Status::Empty: return "EMPTY";
        case Status::NotFound: return "NOT_FOUND";
        case Status::NoSpace: return "NO_SPACE";
        case Status::Duplicate: return "DUPLICATE";
        case Status::OutOfRange: return "OUT_OF_RANGE";
        case Status::NotReady: return "NOT_READY";
        case Status::TooShort: return "TOO_SHORT";
        case Status::BadVersion: return "BAD_VERSION";
        case Status::BadType: return "BAD_TYPE";
        case Status::BadLength: return "BAD_LENGTH";
        case Status::BadCrc: return "BAD_CRC";
        case Status::UnknownApid: return "UNKNOWN_APID";
        case Status::BadOpcode: return "BAD_OPCODE";
        case Status::BadArgs: return "BAD_ARGS";
        case Status::Forbidden: return "FORBIDDEN";
        case Status::Overrun: return "OVERRUN";
    }
    return "UNKNOWN";
}

// ---- Heap watch: counts every operator new, so the checks can prove that ----
// ---- the flight code never touches the heap. Leave it as it is. -------------
static long long g_heap_allocs = 0;

void* operator new(std::size_t n) {
    ++g_heap_allocs;
    void* p = std::malloc(n == 0 ? 1 : n);
    if (p == nullptr) std::abort();
    return p;
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { std::free(p); }
void operator delete(void* p, std::size_t) noexcept { std::free(p); }

long long heap_allocs() { return g_heap_allocs; }

// ---- RingBuffer: a first-in, first-out queue of fixed capacity --------------
// Invariant: 0 <= count_ <= N, and the items, oldest first, sit at
// (head_ + 0) % N, (head_ + 1) % N, ..., (head_ + count_ - 1) % N.
template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class RingBuffer {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a ring buffer needs room for at least one item");

public:
    // Adds v at the back. Full when there is no room: nothing changes.
    Status push(const T& v) {
        if (count_ == N) return Status::Full;
        items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
        ++count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Adds v at the back; when full, the oldest item is dropped to make room.
    // Returns true when an item was dropped.
    bool push_overwrite(const T& v) {
        if (count_ < N) {
            items_[(head_ + count_) % N] = v;
            ++count_;
            return false;
        }
        items_[head_] = v;          // the oldest slot becomes the newest
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        ++dropped_;
        return true;
    }

    // Takes the oldest item out into *out. Empty when there is none.
    Status pop(T* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        head_ = (head_ + 1) % N;
        --count_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest item into *out without taking it out.
    Status peek(T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (count_ == 0) return Status::Empty;
        *out = items_[head_];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the i-th oldest item (0 is the oldest) into *out.
    Status at(std::size_t i, T* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (i >= count_) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = items_[(head_ + i) % N];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    void clear() {
        head_ = 0;
        count_ = 0;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return count_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    bool empty() const { return count_ == 0; }
    bool full() const { return count_ == N; }
    std::uint32_t dropped() const { return dropped_; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::size_t head_ = 0;       // index of the oldest item
    std::size_t count_ = 0;      // how many items are held
    std::uint32_t dropped_ = 0;  // items lost to push_overwrite
};

// ---- Pool: N fixed blocks, handed out and taken back in O(1) ----------------
// A handle names a block by its index and the block's generation. Releasing a
// block bumps its generation, so an old handle to it stops working.
struct Handle {
    std::uint16_t index;
    std::uint16_t gen;   // 0 never names a live block
};

constexpr Handle kNoHandle = {0xFFFF, 0};

template <typename T, std::size_t N>
class Pool {
    static_assert(N > 0 && N < 0xFFFF, "a pool holds 1 to 65534 blocks");

public:
    Pool() { reset(); }

    // Every block free again; every old handle stops working.
    void reset() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            next_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(i + 1);   // N marks the end
            gen_[i] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[i] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[i] + 1);
            used_[i] = false;
        }
        free_head_ = 0;
        in_use_ = 0;
    }

    // Takes a free block, clears it to T{} and writes its handle.
    // The most recently released block is handed out first.
    Status acquire(Handle* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        if (free_head_ == N) {
            ++failures_;
            return Status::NoSpace;
        }
        const std::uint16_t i = free_head_;
        free_head_ = next_[i];
        used_[i] = true;
        items_[i] = T{};
        ++in_use_;
        if (in_use_ > high_water_) high_water_ = in_use_;
        *out = {i, gen_[i]};
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Gives a block back. A stale, foreign or doubled handle is refused.
    Status release(Handle h) {
        if (!valid(h)) return Status::BadArg;
        used_[h.index] = false;
        gen_[h.index] = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(gen_[h.index] == 0xFFFF ? 1 : gen_[h.index] + 1);
        next_[h.index] = free_head_;
        free_head_ = h.index;
        --in_use_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    bool valid(Handle h) const { return h.index < N && h.gen != 0 && used_[h.index] && gen_[h.index] == h.gen; }

    T* get(Handle h) { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }
    const T* get(Handle h) const { return valid(h) ? &items_[h.index] : nullptr; }

    std::size_t in_use() const { return in_use_; }
    std::size_t available() const { return N - in_use_; }
    std::size_t high_water() const { return high_water_; }
    std::uint32_t failures() const { return failures_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }

private:
    T items_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t next_[N] = {};   // free list, threaded through the indexes
    std::uint16_t gen_[N] = {};
    bool used_[N] = {};
    std::uint16_t free_head_ = 0;  // N when no block is free
    std::size_t in_use_ = 0;
    std::size_t high_water_ = 0;   // the most blocks ever in use at once
    std::uint32_t failures_ = 0;   // acquires refused because none was free
};

// ---- Packet buffers and queues that share one pool --------------------------
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacketBytes = 128;
constexpr std::size_t kBufferCount = 24;

struct PacketBuffer {
    std::uint8_t bytes[kMaxPacketBytes];
    std::uint16_t len;
};

using BufferPool = Pool<PacketBuffer, kBufferCount>;

// A FIFO of packets. The bytes live in blocks of a shared pool; the queue
// itself holds only handles, so moving a packet never copies 128 bytes twice.
template <std::size_t Depth>
class PacketQueue {
public:
    explicit PacketQueue(BufferPool* pool) : pool_(pool) {}

    // Copies a packet in. NoSpace when the pool is used up, Full when this
    // queue is at its depth; either way nothing is queued and no block leaks.
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || bytes == nullptr || len == 0 || len > kMaxPacketBytes) return Status::BadArg;
        if (fifo_.full()) return Status::Full;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = pool_->acquire(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        std::memcpy(b->bytes, bytes, len);
        b->len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        fifo_.push(h);   // cannot fail: checked for room above
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Copies the oldest packet out and frees its block. If it does not fit
    // in cap bytes it stays queued and the result is NoSpace.
    Status take(std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* len) {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || out == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;   // cannot happen while the invariant holds
        if (b->len > cap) return Status::NoSpace;
        std::memcpy(out, b->bytes, b->len);
        *len = b->len;
        fifo_.pop(&h);
        pool_->release(h);
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The length of the oldest packet, without taking it.
    Status front_len(std::size_t* len) const {
        if (pool_ == nullptr || len == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        Handle h;
        const Status got = fifo_.peek(&h);
        if (got != Status::Ok) return got;
        const PacketBuffer* b = pool_->get(h);
        if (b == nullptr) return Status::NotFound;
        *len = b->len;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return fifo_.size(); }
    bool empty() const { return fifo_.empty(); }
    static constexpr std::size_t depth() { return Depth; }

private:
    BufferPool* pool_;
    RingBuffer<Handle, Depth> fifo_;
};

// ---- StaticMap: a hash map of fixed capacity, open addressing ---------------
// Keys are unsigned integers (APIDs, opcodes, parameter ids). A key's home
// slot is key % N; collisions probe forward one slot at a time, wrapping.
// Erased slots become tombstones, so a search never stops early at a gap
// that used to hold something. Every loop runs at most N times.
template <typename K, typename V, std::size_t N>
class StaticMap {
    static_assert(N > 0, "a map needs at least one slot");

public:
    StaticMap() { clear(); }

    void clear() {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) state_[i] = Slot::Empty;
        size_ = 0;
        last_probes_ = 0;
    }

    // Inserts key, or overwrites its value if it is already there.
    // Full when the key is new and no empty slot or tombstone is left.
    Status put(K key, const V& value) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at != N) {
            values_[at] = value;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        // Not present: reuse the first tombstone on the key's path, or the
        // first empty slot. Both are on the path locate() just walked.
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        for (std::size_t probes = 0; probes < N; ++probes) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) {
                state_[i] = Slot::Used;
                keys_[i] = key;
                values_[i] = value;
                ++size_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        return Status::Full;
    }

    Status get(K key, V* out) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        *out = values_[at];
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    V* find(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }
    const V* find(K key) const {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        return at == N ? nullptr : &values_[at];
    }

    bool contains(K key) const { return locate(key) != N; }

    Status erase(K key) {
        const std::size_t at = locate(key);
        if (at == N) return Status::NotFound;
        state_[at] = Slot::Tomb;
        --size_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Writes up to max keys into out, smallest first; returns how many.
    // Insertion sort into the caller's array: no heap, no recursion.
    std::size_t sorted_keys(K* out, std::size_t max) const {
        if (out == nullptr) return 0;
        std::size_t n = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
            if (state_[i] != Slot::Used) continue;
            const K k = keys_[i];
            if (n < max) {
                std::size_t j = n++;
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            } else if (max > 0 && k < out[max - 1]) {
                std::size_t j = max - 1;   // k beats the largest kept key
                while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > k) {
                    out[j] = out[j - 1];
                    --j;
                }
                out[j] = k;
            }
        }
        return n;
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return size_; }
    static constexpr std::size_t capacity() { return N; }
    // Slots examined by the last put, get, find, contains or erase.
    std::size_t last_probes() const { return last_probes_; }

private:
    enum class Slot : std::uint8_t { Empty, Used, Tomb };

    static std::size_t home(K key) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(key % N); }

    // The slot holding key, or N. Stops at an empty slot or after N probes;
    // a tombstone does not stop it.
    std::size_t locate(K key) const {
        std::size_t i = home(key);
        std::size_t probes = 0;
        while (probes < N) {
            ++probes;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Empty) break;
            if (state_[i] == Slot::Used && keys_[i] == key) {
                last_probes_ = probes;
                return i;
            }
            i = (i + 1) % N;
        }
        last_probes_ = probes;
        return N;
    }

    K keys_[N] = {};
    V values_[N] = {};
    Slot state_[N] = {};
    std::size_t size_ = 0;
    mutable std::size_t last_probes_ = 0;
};

// ---- Big-endian byte writing and reading, with a sticky error ---------------
// Network byte order: the most significant byte goes first. After the first
// write or read that does not fit, the object stays failed: every later call
// returns the same error and changes nothing, so a caller can do a whole
// run of calls and check ok() once at the end.
class ByteWriter {
public:
    ByteWriter(std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t cap) : buf_(buf), cap_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : cap) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t v) { return put(&v, 1); }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[2] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 2);
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t v) {
        const std::uint8_t b[4] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 24), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 16),
                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v >> 8), static_cast<std::uint8_t>(v)};
        return put(b, 4);
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t v) { return u32(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(v)); }
    Status bytes(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (src == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        return put(src, n);
    }

    std::size_t size() const { return len_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status put(const std::uint8_t* src, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > cap_ - len_) return fail(Status::NoSpace);   // len_ <= cap_ always, so no wrap
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, src, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t cap_;
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

class ByteReader {
public:
    ByteReader(const std::uint8_t* buf, std::size_t len) : buf_(buf), len_(buf == nullptr ? 0 : len) {
        if (buf == nullptr) error_ = Status::BadArg;
    }

    Status u8(std::uint8_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[1];
        const Status s = take(b, 1, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = b[0];
        return s;
    }
    Status u16(std::uint16_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[2];
        const Status s = take(b, 2, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((b[0] << 8) | b[1]);
        return s;
    }
    Status u32(std::uint32_t* v) {
        std::uint8_t b[4];
        const Status s = take(b, 4, v != nullptr);
        if (s == Status::Ok) {
            *v = (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[0]) << 24) | (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[1]) << 16) |
                 (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[2]) << 8) | static_cast<std::uint32_t>(b[3]);
        }
        return s;
    }
    Status i32(std::int32_t* v) {
        std::uint32_t u = 0;
        const Status s = u32(v == nullptr ? nullptr : &u);
        if (s == Status::Ok) *v = static_cast<std::int32_t>(u);   // two's complement, defined since C++20
        return s;
    }
    Status bytes(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (dst == nullptr && n > 0) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status skip(std::size_t n) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    std::size_t pos() const { return pos_; }
    std::size_t remaining() const { return len_ - pos_; }
    bool ok() const { return error_ == Status::Ok; }
    Status status() const { return error_; }

private:
    Status take(std::uint8_t* dst, std::size_t n, bool have_out) {
        if (error_ != Status::Ok) return error_;
        if (!have_out) return fail(Status::BadArg);
        if (n > len_ - pos_) return fail(Status::TooShort);
        std::memcpy(dst, buf_ + pos_, n);
        pos_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }
    Status fail(Status s) {
        if (error_ == Status::Ok) error_ = s;
        return error_;
    }

    const std::uint8_t* buf_;
    std::size_t len_;
    std::size_t pos_ = 0;
    Status error_ = Status::Ok;
};

// ---- CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE -----------------------------------------------------
// Polynomial 0x1021 (x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1), start value 0xFFFF, bits taken
// most significant first, no final XOR. crc16("123456789") is 0x29B1.
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcInit = 0xFFFF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kCrcPoly = 0x1021;

// One bit at a time: 8 shift-and-maybe-XOR steps per byte. The reference.
std::uint16_t crc16_bitwise(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return kCrcInit;
    std::uint16_t crc = kCrcInit;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ (data[i] << 8));
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

// The 256 answers to "what do 8 steps do to this top byte", worked out by
// the compiler, so the table costs nothing at start-up and sits in ROM.
struct CrcTable {
    std::uint16_t entry[256];
};

constexpr CrcTable make_crc_table() {
    CrcTable t{};
    for (int b = 0; b < 256; ++b) {
        std::uint16_t crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(b << 8);
        for (int bit = 0; bit < 8; ++bit) {
            const bool top = (crc & 0x8000u) != 0;
            crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc << 1);
            if (top) crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(crc ^ kCrcPoly);
        }
        t.entry[b] = crc;
    }
    return t;
}

constexpr CrcTable kCrcTable = make_crc_table();

// Continues a CRC over more bytes: crc16_update(crc16(a), b) == crc16(a then b).
std::uint16_t crc16_update(std::uint16_t crc, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (data == nullptr) return crc;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
        const std::uint8_t top = static_cast<std::uint8_t>((crc >> 8) ^ data[i]);
        crc = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((crc << 8) ^ kCrcTable.entry[top]);
    }
    return crc;
}

// One table lookup per byte.
std::uint16_t crc16(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { return crc16_update(kCrcInit, data, n); }

// ---- The packet format ------------------------------------------------------
//  bytes 0-5   primary header, CCSDS style, big-endian:
//              version:3 | type:1 | secondary header flag:1 | APID:11
//              sequence flags:2 | sequence count:14
//              data length: bytes after the primary header, minus 1
//  bytes 6-9   secondary header: time in milliseconds since boot
//  bytes 10-   payload, 0 to kMaxPayload bytes
//  last 2      CRC-16 of every byte before it
constexpr std::size_t kPrimaryHeaderBytes = 6;
constexpr std::size_t kSecondaryHeaderBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kCrcBytes = 2;
constexpr std::size_t kPacketOverhead = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + kSecondaryHeaderBytes + kCrcBytes;   // 12
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPayload = 96;
constexpr std::size_t kMaxPacket = kPacketOverhead + kMaxPayload;   // 108
constexpr std::uint16_t kMaxApid = 0x7FF;
constexpr std::uint16_t kSeqMask = 0x3FFF;
constexpr std::uint8_t kSeqUnsegmented = 3;

enum class PacketType : std::uint8_t { Telemetry = 0, Command = 1 };

struct PrimaryHeader {
    std::uint8_t version;       // 3 bits; always 0
    PacketType type;            // 1 bit
    bool has_secondary;         // 1 bit
    std::uint16_t apid;         // 11 bits
    std::uint8_t seq_flags;     // 2 bits; 3 means "not split"
    std::uint16_t seq_count;    // 14 bits
    std::uint16_t data_length;  // 16 bits
};

struct Packet {
    PrimaryHeader hdr;
    std::uint32_t time_ms;
    std::uint16_t payload_len;
    std::uint8_t payload[kMaxPayload];
};

// Packs the six header bytes. BadArg if a field does not fit its bits.
Status pack_primary(const PrimaryHeader& h, ByteWriter* w) {
    if (w == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (h.version > 7 || h.apid > kMaxApid || h.seq_flags > 3 || h.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    const std::uint16_t word0 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.version << 13) | (static_cast<unsigned>(h.type) << 12) |
                                                           ((h.has_secondary ? 1u : 0u) << 11) | h.apid);
    const std::uint16_t word1 = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((h.seq_flags << 14) | h.seq_count);
    w->u16(word0);
    w->u16(word1);
    w->u16(h.data_length);
    return w->status();
}

// Unpacks the six header bytes. Checks nothing but that they are there.
Status unpack_primary(ByteReader* r, PrimaryHeader* h) {
    if (r == nullptr || h == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    std::uint16_t word0 = 0, word1 = 0, length = 0;
    r->u16(&word0);
    r->u16(&word1);
    r->u16(&length);
    if (!r->ok()) return r->status();
    h->version = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word0 >> 13);
    h->type = ((word0 >> 12) & 1u) ? PacketType::Command : PacketType::Telemetry;
    h->has_secondary = ((word0 >> 11) & 1u) != 0;
    h->apid = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word0 & kMaxApid);
    h->seq_flags = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(word1 >> 14);
    h->seq_count = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(word1 & kSeqMask);
    h->data_length = length;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Writes p as a whole packet: header (data length and the secondary header
// flag worked out here), time, payload and CRC. *written is set only on Ok.
Status encode_packet(const Packet& p, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (out == nullptr || written == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.hdr.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (p.hdr.apid > kMaxApid || p.hdr.seq_flags > 3 || p.hdr.seq_count > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
    if (p.payload_len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    const std::size_t total = kPacketOverhead + p.payload_len;
    if (cap < total) return Status::NoSpace;
    PrimaryHeader h = p.hdr;
    h.has_secondary = true;
    h.data_length = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPrimaryHeaderBytes - 1);
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    const Status s = pack_primary(h, &w);
    if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
    w.u32(p.time_ms);
    w.bytes(p.payload, p.payload_len);
    w.u16(crc16(out, w.size()));
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Builds packets and numbers them: each APID has its own 14-bit sequence
// count, which starts at 0 and wraps from 16383 back to 0.
class PacketEncoder {
public:
    Status build(PacketType type, std::uint16_t apid, std::uint32_t time_ms, const std::uint8_t* payload, std::size_t len,
                 std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
        if ((payload == nullptr && len > 0) || apid > kMaxApid) return Status::BadArg;
        if (len > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        const std::uint16_t seq = found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
        if (found == nullptr && seq_.size() == seq_.capacity()) return Status::Full;
        Packet p{};
        p.hdr = {0, type, true, apid, kSeqUnsegmented, seq, 0};
        p.time_ms = time_ms;
        p.payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(len);
        if (len > 0) std::memcpy(p.payload, payload, len);
        const Status s = encode_packet(p, out, cap, written);
        if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
        seq_.put(apid, static_cast<std::uint16_t>((seq + 1) & kSeqMask));   // only a sent packet uses a number
        ++built_;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // The count the next packet on apid will carry.
    std::uint16_t next_seq(std::uint16_t apid) const {
        const std::uint16_t* found = seq_.find(apid);
        return found == nullptr ? 0 : *found;
    }

    // Sets the next count for apid (ground tools use it to replay a pass).
    Status set_next_seq(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq) {
        if (apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        return seq_.put(apid, seq);
    }

    std::uint32_t packets_built() const { return built_; }

private:
    StaticMap<std::uint16_t, std::uint16_t, 32> seq_;
    std::uint32_t built_ = 0;
};

// ---- Decoding: trust nothing that came over the radio -----------------------
// Checks in this order, and stops at the first failure:
//   null pointer -> BadArg; under 6 bytes -> TooShort; version -> BadVersion;
//   no secondary header -> BadType; length field too small or payload too
//   big -> BadLength; fewer bytes than the length says -> TooShort;
//   CRC -> BadCrc. On any failure *out and *consumed are left alone.
Status decode_packet(const std::uint8_t* in, std::size_t len, Packet* out, std::size_t* consumed) {
    if (in == nullptr || out == nullptr || consumed == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
    if (len < kPrimaryHeaderBytes) return Status::TooShort;
    ByteReader r(in, len);
    PrimaryHeader h;
    unpack_primary(&r, &h);
    if (h.version != 0) return Status::BadVersion;
    if (!h.has_secondary) return Status::BadType;
    const std::size_t total = kPrimaryHeaderBytes + static_cast<std::size_t>(h.data_length) + 1;
    if (total < kPacketOverhead || total - kPacketOverhead > kMaxPayload) return Status::BadLength;
    if (len < total) return Status::TooShort;
    const std::uint16_t stored = static_cast<std::uint16_t>((in[total - 2] << 8) | in[total - 1]);
    if (crc16(in, total - kCrcBytes) != stored) return Status::BadCrc;
    out->hdr = h;
    r.u32(&out->time_ms);
    out->payload_len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(total - kPacketOverhead);
    r.bytes(out->payload, out->payload_len);
    *consumed = total;
    return Status::Ok;
}

// ---- Framing: packets on a byte stream, each after a sync marker ------------
constexpr std::uint8_t kSyncMarker[4] = {0x1A, 0xCF, 0xFC, 0x1D};
constexpr std::size_t kSyncBytes = 4;
constexpr std::size_t kStreamBufferBytes = 512;

// Writes the sync marker and then the packet's bytes.
Status frame_packet(const std::uint8_t* pkt, std::size_t len, std::uint8_t* out, std::size_t cap, std::size_t* written) {
    if (pkt == nullptr || out == nullptr || written == nullptr || len == 0) return Status::BadArg;
    ByteWriter w(out, cap);
    w.bytes(kSyncMarker, kSyncBytes);
    w.bytes(pkt, len);
    if (!w.ok()) return w.status();
    *written = w.size();
    return Status::Ok;
}

// Pulls whole packets out of a stream that may hold noise, cut packets and
// corrupted packets. Bytes that are not part of a good packet are skipped
// and counted; the decoder never gives up and never waits on garbage.
class StreamDecoder {
public:
    // Appends bytes. Full if they do not all fit: then nothing is appended.
    Status feed(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
        if (data == nullptr && n > 0) return Status::BadArg;
        if (n > kStreamBufferBytes - len_) return Status::Full;
        if (n > 0) std::memcpy(buf_ + len_, data, n);
        len_ += n;
        return Status::Ok;
    }

    // Ok: *out holds the next good packet. Empty: no whole packet yet.
    Status next(Packet* out) {
        if (out == nullptr) return Status::BadArg;
        for (std::size_t guard = 0; guard <= kStreamBufferBytes; ++guard) {   // each pass drops at least 1 byte or returns
            const std::size_t at = find_sync();
            if (at == len_) {
                // No marker. Keep the last 3 bytes: they may be the start of one.
                const std::size_t keep = len_ < kSyncBytes - 1 ? len_ : kSyncBytes - 1;
                drop(len_ - keep);
                return Status::Empty;
            }
            drop(at);
            if (len_ < kSyncBytes + kPrimaryHeaderBytes) return Status::Empty;
            std::size_t used = 0;
            const Status s = decode_packet(buf_ + kSyncBytes, len_ - kSyncBytes, out, &used);
            if (s == Status::Ok) {
                drop_good(kSyncBytes + used);
                ++packets_;
                return Status::Ok;
            }
            if (s == Status::TooShort) return Status::Empty;   // wait for the rest
            if (s == Status::BadCrc) ++crc_errors_; else ++bad_headers_;
            drop(1);   // step past this marker and look for the next
        }
        return Status::Empty;
    }

    std::uint32_t packets() const { return packets_; }
    std::uint32_t crc_errors() const { return crc_errors_; }
    std::uint32_t bad_headers() const { return bad_headers_; }
    std::uint32_t bytes_skipped() const { return skipped_; }
    std::size_t buffered() const { return len_; }

private:
    std::size_t find_sync() const {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i + kSyncBytes <= len_; ++i) {
            if (std::memcmp(buf_ + i, kSyncMarker, kSyncBytes) == 0) return i;
        }
        return len_;
    }
    void drop(std::size_t n) {
        skipped_ += static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n);
        drop_good(n);
    }
    void drop_good(std::size_t n) {
        std::memmove(buf_, buf_ + n, len_ - n);
        len_ -= n;
    }

    std::uint8_t buf_[kStreamBufferBytes] = {};
    std::size_t len_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t packets_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t crc_errors_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t bad_headers_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t skipped_ = 0;
};

// ---- Sequence tracking: which packets never arrived -------------------------
class SequenceTracker {
public:
    // Records a packet. *missed is how many counts were skipped since the
    // last packet on this APID (mod 16384); the first packet misses none.
    // The same count twice in a row is Duplicate, and counts as no loss.
    Status observe(std::uint16_t apid, std::uint16_t seq, std::uint16_t* missed) {
        if (missed == nullptr || apid > kMaxApid || seq > kSeqMask) return Status::BadArg;
        std::uint16_t* last = last_.find(apid);
        if (last == nullptr) {
            const Status s = last_.put(apid, seq);
            if (s != Status::Ok) return s;
            *missed = 0;
            return Status::Ok;
        }
        if (seq == *last) {
            *missed = 0;
            ++duplicates_;
            return Status::Duplicate;
        }
